items.title: IRGC: Hormuz Strait to stay closed if US does not accept Iran's terms
items.summary: The dispute over the Strait of Hormuz comes amid a broader standoff between Tehran and Washington, with tensions playing out on multiple fronts, from economic pressure and diplomatic negotiations to the prospect of further military escalation.
items.body_text:
By continuing to browse our site you agree to our use of cookies, revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. You can change your cookie settings through your browser.
                            
                            I agree
                        
                    
                        World
                    
                    
    13:32, 27-Aug-2026
                    
                
                CGTN
Ships are seen anchored in the Strait of Hormuz, August 10, 2026. /VCG
        Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened if the United States does not accept Iran's conditions, according to the IRGC's official news outlet Sepah News.
IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi told reporters that the strategic waterway remains under Iranian control and no vessel can pass through it without Iran's permission.
"All the enemy warships are at least 400 km away from the Strait of Hormuz, and from the military and territorial perspectives, no vessel is able to pass through this waterway without Iran's permission and management," Mohebbi said, adding that even the route near Oman is fully under Iranian control. He also underlined that the Strait of Hormuz belongs to Iran and Oman.
He said that Iran and Oman have reached agreements on their respective shares of the strait and its revenues following negotiations.
Mohebbi blamed US "obstructionism" for delaying the negotiation process, noting that if Washington returns to compliance with the peace memorandum of understanding (MoU) it signed with Iran in June, "we can open the Strait of Hormuz within the agreed framework."
"Therefore, the United States must accept our conditions. If the United States does not accept our conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened under any circumstance," he added.
In a joint statement on Tuesday night, Iran and Oman announced that they have discussed a phased framework that includes the establishment of a temporary joint shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint demining project.
The statement said that technical negotiations will continue towards a permanent shipping corridor and the future administration of the waterway, including information exchange, traffic management, and relevant navigation and security services.
The dispute over the Strait of Hormuz comes amid a broader standoff between Tehran and Washington, with tensions playing out on multiple fronts, from economic pressure and diplomatic negotiations to the prospect of further military escalation.
Iran calls on UN to condemn US 'economic terrorism'
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has called on the United Nations to condemn what he described as Washington's illegal campaign of "economic terrorism" against Iran, referring to it as "Operation Economic Outcast."
In a letter addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, the president of the Security Council and UN member states, Araghchi said the US campaign was aimed at disrupting Iran's lawful economic ties with other countries through threats of secondary sanctions and exclusion from the US financial system. The letter was published on Wednesday on his Telegram channel.
He argued that the measures represented an attempt by Washington to impose its domestic laws and foreign-policy goals beyond its borders and pressure sovereign nations into changing their legitimate trade relations with Iran.
Araghchi said the UN and its member states now faced a crucial choice: whether to uphold the principles of sovereign equality, non-interference and countries' sovereign rights, or yield to what he called US unilateralism and coercion.
Iran also urged Guterres to examine and report on the humanitarian and human rights impact of the measures, particularly their effects on access to food, medicine, healthcare, energy, transportation and humanitarian aid.
Araghchi added that Tehran reserved the right to seek accountability

items.title: U.S. failure to appoint Australian ambassador "diplomatic insult": former deputy PM
items.summary: Former Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has accused the U.S. of hitting Australia with a "diplomatic insult."
items.body_text:
CANBERRA, Jan. 3 (Xinhua) -- Former Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has accused the U.S. of hitting Australia with a "diplomatic insult."
Fischer, who served as Deputy Prime Minister from 1996 to 1999 under Australia's longest-serving Prime Minister John Howard, on Wednesday said the U.S. administration's failure to appoint an ambassador to Canberra for 18 months indicated Australia was now of "low priority."
John Berry, the former U.S. Ambassador to Australia, resigned in September 2016, leaving the post vacant ever since.
"This is now bordering on a diplomatic insult," Fischer told Fairfax Media on Wednesday. "We've been downgraded, despite all the nice noises. We are a low priority.
Fischer identified U.S. President Donald Trump's opposition to a refugee deal negotiated between his predecessor Barack Obama and Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull as a likely reason for the current administration's failure to appoint an ambassador.
It has long been speculated that Admiral Harry Harris, head of the U.S. Pacific Command, is the likely next ambassador but there has been no confirmation from the White House.
Simon Jackman, head of the United States Studies Centre at the University of Sydney, disagreed with Fischer, saying the delay showed the Trump administration was taking the appointment "extremely seriously."

items.title: South Africa freedom day memorial gathering reveals its pursuit of dignity and inclusive governance in post apartheid era
items.body_text:
IN-DEPTH / IN-DEPTH
                        South Africa freedom day memorial gathering reveals its pursuit of dignity and inclusive governance in post apartheid era
                        Politics finds its rhythm
                        
                     Editor's Note: 
In an era of profound global shifts and increasingly complex regional dynamics, a proper understanding of the world must be rooted in "grounded experience" and localized insights. Global Times English edition, in collaboration with the Academy of International and Regional Communication Studies, Communication University of China, is proud to launch "Local Insights," an English-language column dedicated to original, field-based observations.
We invite Chinese scholars and professionals who are studying, conducting exchanges, or working outside China, as well as international students and friends living and studying in China who are familiar with the social contexts of their home countries or third countries, to begin from first-hand field experience and engage with social, cultural, and contemporary issues beyond China. In the fifth article of this column, drawing on her onâtheâground experience as a Chinese exchange scholar, the author observes a South Africa Freedom Day memorial gathering, revealing how local politics unfolds through collective singing, dancing, and grassroots participation, while also reflecting on the gap between political liberation and economic justice.
As a PhD student, I am currently on an exchange program at Nelson Mandela University in South Africa, with support from the China Scholarship Council. Since arriving here, I have developed a habit of stepping beyond campus whenever possible. Community meetings, municipal events and public gatherings have become a vital way for me to engage with local life. This time, a local friend recommended that I attend a memorial event in Kariega, organized by the Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU) in honor of its former president, Phumzile John Gomomo. Beyond that, I had little sense of what kind of gathering I was about to enter.
It was on the way that I noticed the streets were unusually vibrant. Groups of people were dressed in colorful attire, with bright Xhosa headscarves and garments bearing political symbols. My friend then reminded me that it was April 27, which is Freedom Day in South Africa. On this day in 1994, South Africa held its first non-racial election, formally ending apartheid and inaugurating democratic rule. Over the past three decades, Freedom Day commemorates political liberation, while also inviting recurring reflection on whether the promise of freedom has been fully realized. In that sense, Freedom Day marks an important moment for observing contemporary South African politics and social sentiment.
The aerial view of Johannesburg, South Africa Photo: VCG
From street to hall: Entering Freedom Day
The event was scheduled to begin at 10 am, and we arrived shortly before the hour. Yet there were not many people present. Banners of COSATU, the South African Communist Party (SACP), and the African National Congress (ANC) had already been displayed inside the hall, quietly framing the political context of the gathering. Although my understanding was still limited, I could already sense that their presence mattered. COSATU, SACP and ANC represent key forces in South Africa's political landscape, historically linked through the "Tripartite Alliance" formed during the anti-apartheid struggle and sustained in various forms since 1994. I could see that this was not simply a local gathering, but one embedded within a much longer political tradition.
What struck me first was how different the atmosphere was from what I had expected of a political gathering. There was no sense of urgency or visible tension. My friend introduced me around, and we greeted each other through handshakes, embraces and brief conversations, with a familiarity that suggested long-standing connec

items.title: China to introduce new train timetable from July 1, including high-speed train service between Beijing and Urumqi
items.body_text:
China to introduce new train timetable from July 1, including high-speed train service between Beijing and Urumqi
                        
                        
                    Passengers are pictured at the Beijing Tongzhou Railway Station in the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center in Beijing, capital of China, May 29, 2026. From 2016 to 2026, the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center marks a decade of planning and development. Over the past ten years, it has undergone a remarkable transformation into a vibrant modern area. Photo: Xinhua
China's national railway network will implement a new train-running timetable starting July 1, which will strengthen connectivity between the country's northwestern provinces and the central, southern, and southwestern regions, while also introducing high-speed train service for the first time between Urumqi, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and Beijing, the China State Railway Group announced on Wednesday.
Tickets under the new timetable went on sale on Wednesday.
The upgraded network is expected to further enhance railway transportation capacity and operational efficiency. Under the new timetable, China's national railways will operate 12,174 scheduled passenger trains, marking an increase of 106 trains compared with the current schedule.
For example, the railway authorities have arranged 58 high-speed trains from Xi'an in Northwest China's Shaanxi to destinations including Nanyang of Central China's Henan Province, Hankou of Central China's Hubei Province and Chongqing city in Southwest China.
Wan Yaqiong, director of the ticket sales workshop at Xi'an Station under China Railway Xi'an Group, said that the new timetable will introduce direct services from Xi'an to Hankou, with the fastest round-trip travel time controlled within seven hours, according to a report by the China Central Television (CCTV) News on Wednesday.
Additionally, high-speed trains will operate from Yan'an city in Shaanxi to Shaoshan city in Central China's Hunan, establishing a direct high-speed rail link between the two major "red tourism" destinations - historical sites with a modern revolutionary legacy, the CCTV News report noted.
After the timetable adjustment, high-speed trains will run for the first time between Urumqi station and Beijing West station. At the same time, the T-series trains operating between Urumqi and Chongqing West will be upgraded to Z-series direct express trains, shortening the travel time between the two places by more than two hours.
The railway authorities will increase the number of high-speed services during morning and evening rush hours on certain high-speed rail lines in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, providing greater convenience for commuters.

items.title: Chinese expert criticizes Filipino FM's claim that Japan-Philippines delimitation 'nothing to do' with China, warns move serves ulterior purposes beyond bilateral talks
items.body_text:
Chinese expert criticizes Filipino FMâs claim that Japan-Philippines delimitation ânothing to doâ with China, warns move serves ulterior purposes beyond bilateral talks
                        
                        
                    Philippines' Foreign Minister Maria Theresa Lazaro delivers a speech at the Nikkei Forum at a hotel in Tokyo on June 10, 2026. Photo: VCG
In response to the Philippine foreign minister's claim that its boundary discussions with Japan "have nothing to do" with China, a Chinese expert on Thursday said the soâcalled Japan-Philippines maritime delimitation talks concern an area east of China's Taiwan island and contradict international law and the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The expert noted the move carries ulterior purposes beyond bilateral discussions.
Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Maria Theresa Lazaro said that establishing clear maritime boundaries between the Philippines and Japan is of vital importance to the country's national defense in an interview on Wednesday.
China has criticized such negotiations, while Lazaro claimed the discussion "has nothing to do with them" and "just between the Philippines and Japan." She added, "We should continue with our delimitation talks," even if China keeps objecting or increases pressure, Nikkei Asia reported.
Lazaro also expressed so-called concern over increasing activities by Chinese vessels in waters close to the Taiwan island, per the outlet.
Ding Duo, Director of the Research Center for International and Regional Issues at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, told the Global Times on Thursday that Lazaro's words constitute three violations.
First, it violated the international law, in particular the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, which stipulated, in simple words, that "bilateral treaty does not create obligations or rights for a third State." If the Philippines and Japan reach any agreement regardless of China interests, that constitute a violation, Ding said.
Second, such discussions ran counter to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which stipulated equity in maritime boundary delimitation. Based on this principle, given that the delimitation involves China's interests, and the final decision must not bypass China, Ding added.
The expert further noted that third, in a situation that three parties interests are involved, the acts of Philippines and Japan violated the "obligation of restraint" and "principle of good faith" in international law.
Japan and the Philippines have been hyping so-called maritime delimitation issue recently, concerning an area east of China's Taiwan island. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. agreed to start formal talks on EEZ boundaries and the continental shelf when the president visited Tokyo on a state visit in May, per reports.
In response, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on May 29 that according to China's domestic law and international law including UNCLOS, China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in this area. Japan and the Philippines' so-called maritime delimitation talks constitute a severe violation of China's maritime rights and interests, UNCLOS and other international law and basic norms governing international relations. China strongly deplores and firmly opposes that and has lodged serious protests with both countries.
The so-called delimitation talks are completely illegal, null and void, and will have no effect on China's claims to rights in the area east of the Taiwan island or exercise of China's lawful rights. China urges Japan and the Philippines to immediately stop any violation of China's maritime rights and interests and take concrete actions to uphold regional peace and stability.
Ding also noted that in addition to diplomatic methods to break the Japan-Philippines collusion, China can also conduct normal maritime law enforcement, patrol

items.summary: 大美中国，江山如画。 党的十八大以来，习近平总书记的考察足迹遍及神州大地。祁连山麓、坝上林海，秦岭深处、黄河之滨，总书记在大江奔涌处谋划千秋大计，在山川锦绣间擘画生态蓝图。一系列重要论述，为新时代生态文明建设提供了根本遵循和行动指南。 世界环境日到来之际，我们跟随习近平总书记的脚步，一起呵护山水、寄情山水，领悟守护绿水青山、建设生态文明之道。 江河为脉 心系长江之变，习近平总书记前往沿江重镇，考察长江经济带发展。从三峡库区到洞庭湖畔，从港口码头到企业车间，总书记深入调研，作出一系列重要指示，为新时代江河保护治理提供了重要遵循。 2018年4月，习近平总书记来到湖南岳阳城陵矶水文站考察。在狭窄的站房外长廊上，习近平总书记举目远眺。“共抓大保护，不搞大开发”的战略定力，在这里化作守护一江碧水的坚定行动。 2023年10月10日下午，习近平总书记在江西九江市考察，冒雨在江边察看，了解当地长江国家文化公园建设、长江岸线生态修复等情况。10月12日，总书记在进一步推动长江经济带高质量发展座谈会上回顾长江经济带发展历程，感慨：“做就要做好，坚定做下去。笃行不怠，一以贯之，久久为功。” 黄河安澜是中

items.title: 学习手记 | “环境就是民生”
items.summary: 6月5日是世界环境日，也是我国环境保护法确立的环境日。 22年前的这一天，在时任浙江省委书记习近平部署推动下，以农村人居环境整治为重点的“千万工程”启动。 当时，习近平同志担任浙江省委书记刚半年多，工作千头万绪。他何以将农村人居环境整治作为重点工作？ 在基层调研时，习近平同志发现，在浙江经济快速发展的同时，广大农村却面临“成长的烦恼”，村庄面貌不如人意。 全省3.4万个村庄中，人居环境较好的仅4000个。有人形容：“走过一村又一村，村村都是垃圾村。”还有农民这样描述：“起早贪黑赚钞票，垃圾堆里数钞票，躺在医院花钞票。”可以说，人居环境整治是当时浙江农村群众的一个迫切期盼。 “千万工程”聚焦乡亲们走什么村道、怎么处理畜禽粪便等小问题，却直接关系农民获得感、幸福感，是实打实的民生大事。 老百姓的生活环境如何，习近平同志念兹在兹： 上世纪70年代，在陕北冯家坪公社赵家河大队驻点时，他撸起袖管，一石一瓦盖起村里第一个男女分开的厕所； 到正定工作，不仅大力推进“人拉猪吃”的“连茅圈”改造工作，还拿着大扫帚走上街头搞卫生，推动成立全县第一支专职卫生清洁队； 任福州市委书记，亲自为建造垃圾处理场选址

items.title: 刘国中在安徽调研时强调 全力以赴夺取夏粮丰收 全面打牢秋粮生产基础
items.summary: 新华社合肥6月5日电 中共中央政治局委员、国务院副总理刘国中3日至5日到安徽调研“三夏”农业生产工作。他强调，要深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于国家粮食安全的重要论述，按照党中央、国务院部署，扛稳政治责任，毫不放松抓好夏收夏种夏管，全力以赴夺取夏粮丰收，全面打牢秋粮生产基础，确保完成全年粮食生产目标任务。 刘国中先后来到宿州市、淮南市、六安市，深入小麦机收和夏播现场、农机跨区作业服务点、农事服务中心、粮食仓储中心、地方农科院等，实地察看夏收夏种、农机作业服务保障、粮食烘干收储等工作，详细了解农作物新品种选育、大面积单产提升、农资保供稳价、高标准农田建设等情况。 刘国中强调，“三夏”工作抓得好不好，事关全年粮食生产目标任务能否顺利实现。当前正值“三夏”农业生产关键时期，要抓住有利天气抢晴收获，组织好农机跨区作业，强化服务保障和安全管理，确保夏收高效进行。要抓实抓牢机收减损、烘干晾晒等各项措施，最大程度减少粮食损失。要精心做好夏粮收购工作，引导各类企业积极入市，保障粮食市场平稳运行。要压茬推进夏播，加强农资供应和农事服务，强化技术集成及推广应用，落实落细合理密植、精量播种等大面积单产提升措施，

items.title: 全国人大常委会启动节约能源法执法检查
items.summary: 新华社北京6月5日电 为推动节约能源法全面有效实施，促进更高水平、更高质量做好节能工作，全国人大常委会5日启动节约能源法执法检查。 节约能源法自1998年1月1日实施，并于2007年、2016年、2018年进行了修改。 记者5日从全国人大常委会节约能源法执法检查组第一次全体会议上了解到，为全面深入了解法律实施情况，此次执法检查采取实地检查与委托检查相结合的方式，检查组将赴天津、江苏、湖南、广东、广西、四川等省（区、市）开展实地检查，并委托北京、河北、山西、吉林、上海、重庆等省（市）人大常委会对本行政区域内节约能源法实施情况进行检查。检查组将采取实地检查、听取汇报、组织座谈、典型调研、专题研究、抽查暗访等多种方式，全面准确了解法律实施情况，对带有普遍性的问题深入调查研究。 检查组将重点检查8方面内容：落实节能管理制度情况，推进重点领域节能工作情况，重点用能单位节能管理情况，推动节能技术进步情况，实施节能激励措施情况，与法律配套的行政法规、部门规章以及地方性法规的制定情况，法律实施中存在的其他问题，对节约能源法修改的意见和建议。

items.summary: 在树下院落、乡间凉亭，一场场热气腾腾的“凉亭夜话”，正悄然改变着河南省三门峡市卢氏县基层治理的面貌。从群众自发到如今党委引领下的制度化实践，“凉亭夜话”不仅成为群众表达心声的平台，也构建起基层治理的创新模式，让“小议事”撬动“大治理”。 “凉亭夜话”源于卢氏县木桐乡群众的自发行动。农闲时，村民围坐凉亭、树下，或为化解纠纷说和相劝，或为某一项目献计献策。卢氏县党委因势利导，对此进行规范化、制度化，并在全县推广。 “凉亭夜话”以开放空间为议事场景，每月至少组织一次群众议事会，激发群众参与热情。同时，明确“五议三不议”原则，划定议事边界。通过建立民情收集机制，形成“民情清单”“议事清单”，配套“四公”议事制度和闭环工作机制，加强督促督办。 2024年，“凉亭夜话”决议落实率高达92%，持续激发干部群众谋发展、干事业、促振兴的内生动力。木桐乡年投资59亿元的钼矿项目落地，创办了创业技能培训中心，打造了“灵神粉条”网红品牌，办起了位于豫陕交界地带的烤鱼店，各项产业红红火火，名列全县“十快乡镇”。全县农村党支部领办专业合作社170余家，涌现出一批集体经济收入超百万元的村。（记者 崔志坚 通讯员 刘

items.title: 北京发布14项举措保障新就业群体权益
items.summary: 本报北京6月4日电 （记者王洲）6月3日，北京市司法局、市市场监管局、市总工会联合发布14项具体举措，构建政策协同、法律服务和维权保障三位一体的制度框架保障新就业群体权益。在公共法律服务方面，北京市司法局组织市、区两级公共法律服务中心、乡镇（街道）工作站为新就业形态劳动者提供法律咨询、法律查询服务以及律师、公证、司法鉴定等法律便利服务，村（居）法律顾问也将常住新就业形态劳动者纳入服务范围；设立“城市蜂鸟”法律援助项目，为在交通事故中不负主要责任、无法认定法律援助条件的网约配送员提供公益法律服务。 同时，北京市市场监管部门将发挥网约配送行业党委作用，及时收集、反映、协调解决网约配送员的问题困难和集中诉求，协同开展“清朗网络平台算法典型问题治理”专项行动，推动平台企业落实算法安全主体责任。市总工会将规范召开企业职工代表大会，落实劳动者四项重大权益保障，开通工会法律服务绿色通道，常态化开展工会特色交通安全、职业健康专项教育。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 14 版）

items.title: 北京出台举措优化入境旅游服务

items.title: “阿大葱油饼”焕新记（干部状态新观察·走进一线探作风）
items.summary: “阿大葱油饼”店铺前排起长队。 受访者供图"> “阿大葱油饼”店铺前排起长队。受访者供图 下午两点，午餐时间已过，上海市静安区石门二路上，“吴根存阿大葱油饼”的招牌下还排着长长的队伍。 “阿大”吴根存在上海颇有名气。他做了30多年的葱油饼，一度是上海街头小吃中的“顶流”。直到3年前老店歇业，“阿大葱油饼”才渐渐淡出人们的视线。 年近七旬的“阿大”坐到店门口休息，厨房里忙碌的，是他的儿子吴志勇。 “想把老爸树起来的品牌再做起来，把葱油饼的手艺传承下去。”摘下帽子、口罩，脱掉围裙，吴志勇满头大汗。曾是外企员工的他，有这个念头已经许久。在上海市区多处考察后，今年4月，一家人选中了石门二路这家门面“老店新开”。 “‘阿大葱油饼’回来了！”随着刚出炉的葱油饼照片、视频在网上热传，新店门前迅速热闹了起来。顾客络绎不绝，店里只得贴出提示：每人限购5只。 生意红火令人欣喜，可没成想，紧接着就收到不少投诉。 4月底，周边商户、居民接连反映：店里的油烟乱排，影响正常经营、生活；马路上排队的顾客有时太多，堵住人行道，阻碍交通。 “街道干部来找我时，我是有点蒙的。”吴志勇说，葱油饼要好吃，需要烤和炸，自然产生

items.title: 优化口岸营商环境没有最好，只有更好（快评）
items.summary: 出台高效举措、优化服务体验、强化硬件设施、搭建高效平台……近年来，海关等职能部门和地方政府密切合作，推出一系列精准有力的政策措施，为激发经营主体活力和助力外贸高质量发展注入强劲动能。 口岸营商环境直接关系到国际贸易的便利程度。优化口岸营商环境，意味着在简化流程、提高效率、降低成本上下功夫。无论是通关时间的缩短，还是报关手续的简化，都显著降低了企业的运营成本，加快了货物的流转速度。 优化口岸营商环境没有最好，只有更好。随着全球贸易格局不断变化，口岸营商环境的优化仍将是一个持续的过程。各地各部门应持续提升政策供给质量，更大程度释放政策效应，推动口岸营商环境向着更加高效、透明、公平、便利的方向发展，有力助推贸易强国建设。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 08 版）

items.title: 将适老化理念融入“诗与远方”（专家点评）
items.summary: 自驾出行、列车出游和旅居康养成为越来越多老年人的选择。 银发旅游蓬勃发展，推动了旅游产业升级。无论是城镇还是乡村，都在努力完善旅游基础设施和公共文化服务。为了更好满足老年游客的需求，还应开发更多适合老年人的旅游线路和产品，并加强博物馆、美术馆、酒店等场所的适老化改造。从硬件到服务，全社会应共同发力，将适老化理念融入方方面面，助力老有所游、老有所乐。 值得关注的是，老年人也可能因信息不对称而遭遇消费陷阱，还可能因为行程安排不当而水土不服。文化和旅游部门要联合市场监管等部门，从社交平台的旅游广告和招徕资质审查开始，重点规范交通、餐饮、住宿、购物、自费项目、医疗保障和应急救援等服务标准，加强对强买强卖、诱导消费、价格歧视等行为的综合监管和专项执法，让老年人畅享“诗与远方”。 （作者为中国旅游研究院院长） 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 04 版）

items.title: 习近平总书记关切事｜我们的名字叫“长江”——三个沿江村庄的变迁故事

items.summary: 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在北京中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 新华社记者 黄敬文摄"> 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在北京中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 新华社记者 黄敬文摄 新华社北京6月4日电 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 习近平再次祝贺卢卡申科当选连任总统。习近平指出，中国和白俄罗斯是真朋友、好伙伴。双方一直以诚相待、以信相交。两国传统友好历久弥坚，政治互信牢不可破，各领域合作全面推进。中方始终从战略高度和长远角度看待和发展中白关系，愿同白方一道，推动两国关系和互利合作行稳致远。双方要进一步加强在联合国、上海合作组织等多边框架内协调和配合，共同反对霸权霸道霸凌，捍卫国际公平正义。 卢卡申科表示，这是我第15次访问中国，每一次都真切感受到中方的深情厚谊。白方感谢中方长期以来大力支持和帮助，对中国高度信任，将坚定不移发展对华关系，积极推进对华合作。在国际事务中，中国坚定维护多边主义，反对单边主义和制裁施压，为世界树立了榜样。白方深表钦佩，愿与中方共同捍卫国际公平正义。 王毅参加会见。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 01 版）

items.title: 习近平向韩国当选总统李在明致贺电
items.summary: 新华社北京6月4日电 6月4日，国家主席习近平致电李在明，祝贺他当选韩国总统。 习近平指出，中韩互为重要近邻和合作伙伴。建交33年来，双方超越意识形态和社会制度差异，携手并进、相互成就，实现两国关系平稳健康发展，不仅增进了两国人民福祉，也为促进地区和平稳定和发展繁荣作出积极贡献。 习近平强调，我高度重视中韩关系发展。当前，世界百年变局加速演进，国际和地区形势中的不确定因素增多。作为全球和地区重要国家，中方愿同韩方一道，坚守建交初心，坚定睦邻友好方向，坚持互利共赢目标，共同推动中韩战略合作伙伴关系不断向前发展，更好造福两国人民。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 01 版）

items.title: 公证档案管理办法修订 推进公证电子档案信息化建设
items.summary: 记者6月4日从司法部获悉，司法部、国家档案局近日印发新修订的《公证档案管理办法》，进一步推进公证电子档案信息化建设，优化公证档案保管期限，完善公证档案利用规则等。 公证档案是记录公证活动过程的基本载体，是国家档案的重要组成部分，是公证执业监督和质量管理的主要依据。办法完善公证档案管理部门职责任务，明确国务院司法行政机关负责制定全国统一的公证档案工作制度，并与国家档案主管部门对全国公证档案工作进行监督、指导和检查。 在推进公证档案电子化与文书材料归档数字化转型方面，办法设专章明确公证档案信息化建设的整体性要求和原则性规定，规定公证电子档案与传统载体公证档案具有同等效力，倡导推进公证档案数字化，并对已经数字化的档案备查提出要求。让静态数据转化为服务动能，更好促进减证便民。 此外，办法依据新修订的档案法及其实施条例，规定大幅缩短公证档案保管期限，将永久、60年和20年的保管期限，相应调整为永久、30年和10年，并制作《公证档案保管期限表》，以附件形式附后。办法明确公证档案保管责任，规定公证机构可以将公证档案的保管期限通过书面告知、办公场所公示等方式告知当事人。规范公证档案销毁条件和程序，明确

items.title: 法治力量护航民营经济高质量发展（代表之声）
items.summary: 《中华人民共和国民营经济促进法》颁布施行，令民营企业界广为振奋。这部法律的出台，承载着民营经济人士多年的期盼，回应了经营实践中的痛点、难点问题，必将开启民营经济发展的崭新篇章。 改革开放40多年来，民营经济从小到大、从弱到强，不断发展壮大。我父辈那样老一代民营企业家视法治建设为企业发展根基，呼吁加强法治保障，对民营经济领域法治建设有着深切期盼。上世纪90年代，许多民营企业家为制定乡镇企业法建言献策。从当年的乡镇企业法，到如今的民营经济促进法，映照了我国从推进农村工业化到构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制的深刻变革。 作为一名来自民营企业的全国人大代表，我有幸参与了民营经济促进法的立法过程。去年在草案征求意见阶段提交了意见，今年全国两会期间又提交了相关代表建议，并列席十四届全国人大常委会第十五次会议，见证了新法的审议和表决。让我印象特别深刻的是，立法过程中，立法机关充分听取民营企业家的意见，相关部门负责同志也专程到我们的驻地，就法律条款进行详细解读和沟通，充分体现了党和国家对民营经济的重视、对民营企业诉求的尊重。 党的十八大以来，党中央出台一系列重大举措，促进民营经济持续、健康、高质量发展。

items.title: “阿大葱油饼”焕新记（干部状态新观察·走进一线探作风）

items.title: “填一表、跑一次” 辽宁沈阳推出“公民信息连锁变更一件事”
items.summary: 平日里，你有过变更身份信息多次跑的经历吗？如何让更改身份信息快速又准确，来看看沈阳推出的“公民信息连锁变更一件事”。 2024年10月17日，沈阳市“公民信息连锁变更一件事”正式上线。沈阳居民在申请变更姓名、出生日期、民族、性别、居民身份证号码等基本信息时，可以在线下基层派出所或线上的沈阳政务服务网，通过填写一张表单，提交一次变更申请，进行业务办理。审批通过后，公安内部立即启动跨层级、跨警种联动，外部与社保、医保、公积金等部门跨部门联动，开展“串并联”审批。全部完成后，同步发放新的身份证、驾驶证、机动车登记证、机动车行驶证、保安员证、爆破作业人员许可证、社会保障卡，同步变更医保和公积金账户等信息，证照全部邮寄到家。截至目前，全市已经办理相关业务160余件。 沈阳市民邵某是“公民信息连锁变更一件事”的首位体验者，通过沈阳政务服务网“公民信息连锁变更一件事”板块申请变更姓名后，邵某的身份证、驾驶证、机动车行驶证、机动车登记证书，医保、公积金和姓名同步更改，一次申请全部办理完成。 据介绍，“公民信息连锁变更一件事”改革的实施离不开办事流程优化以及多部门数据共享与协同合作。沈阳市营商环境建设局

items.title: 中央网信办等：开展军队文职人员考试培训专项整治
items.summary: 关于开展军队文职人员考试培训专项整治的通告 近年来，一些教育培训机构以军队文职人员考试培训为名违法违规经营，出现无证经营、虚假宣传、借机敛财等乱象，损害了考生权益，严重影响军队形象声誉和考试公平性。为维护人民军队良好形象、考生切身利益和市场经营秩序，现就有关问题通告如下： 一、严禁仿冒军队文职人员考试主管部门官方微信、微博、网站等行为；不得在互联网上擅自解读、曲解军队文职人员管理、军队文职人员考试有关政策或者擅自发布关于军队文职人员考试的不当宣传、不良炒作、欺骗误导考生和社会公众等信息。 二、各类学校不得违规组织军队文职人员考试培训活动，未经批准不得向军队文职人员考试培训机构提供场地，不得为军队文职人员考试培训机构招揽生源提供便利，学校教师和其他工作人员不得违规到军队文职人员考试培训机构兼职、代课，不得参与编写有关培训材料。各级教育行政部门要按照属地管理原则，配合有关部门开展军队文职人员考试培训专项整治工作。 三、军队文职人员考试培训类广告不得对培训效果作出保证性承诺，不得明示或者暗示有关考试机构或者其工作人员、考试命题人员参加培训；禁止不明码标价、价格欺诈行为。 中央网络安全和信息化

items.title: Study Linking Solar Farms to Bird Loss Draws Scrutiny in China
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018949/Study Linking Solar Farms to Bird Loss Draws Scrutiny in China
items.summary: China’s scientific community has questioned a recent study in the country that concluded solar farms may reduce bird diversity, interrogating the paper’s data and statistical methods.
items.body_text:
Study Linking Solar Farms to Bird Loss Draws Scrutiny in China
Solar farms reduce bird diversity, a Chinese study published last week in the international, peer-reviewed journal Science, announced. But the country’s scientific community has contested the reliability of its birdwatching data and the significance of its statistical findings.
The study, published Aug. 21, was led by researchers at Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, in collaboration with other researchers from China, Vietnam, and the United States.
Examining 2,344 Chinese counties from 2014 to 2023, it found that cutting carbon emissions may come at the cost of protecting biodiversity, as birds’ cropland and grassland habitats are converted for solar projects.
China has been expanding solar power to meet its targets of peaking carbon emissions by 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2060. By 2024, solar facilities covered an estimated 4,520 square kilometers of land and are projected to make up nearly 45% of the country’s electricity generation by 2060.
“The research is not against solar expansion but rather offers policy recommendations on how to do it better,” Li Shanjun, one of the study’s corresponding authors and a professor at the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, told Sixth Tone.
The authors suggested developing solar projects in areas where solar panels cause lower ecological impact, such as in deserts; promoting phased rollouts rather than sudden large-scale expansion; and assessing ecological recovery beyond vegetation density, as they found uniform vegetation inferior for housing bird habitats.
However, experts from the China Ornithological Society said “flaws” in the study’s bird observation data could undermine its conclusions, according to a Tuesday article published on the society’s official WeChat account. The academic group includes ornithologists from universities, research institutes, and conservation organizations nationwide.
The crowdsourced dataset from the China Birdwatching Record Center contained missing bird counts, erroneous records, and reporting differences driven by the growing popularity of birdwatching, the Society wrote.
Among the issues, over 40% of the over 500,000 reports collected during the nine years recorded the presence of species, indicated using the number “1.” However, the Society noted that this is commonly used as a placeholder when the observer did not enter a count, rather than that only one bird was seen, making the data unreliable.
The analysis also said the data had not been properly cleaned. One record from 2015, for example, reported over 2 billion little egrets at a single location. The record was retained in the dataset, contributing to bird totals “beyond a reasonable range.”
Meanwhile, the original study may have removed some migratory waterbirds’ records at wintering sites as statistical outliers, as they recorded tens of thousands of birds at a given location, “potentially underestimating true bird diversity,” the analysis said.
The analysis also noted that birdwatching records surged between 2021 and 2023 amid a growing birdwatching boom in the country, just as authorities were introducing significant solar policies. This, it argued, makes it difficult to determine whether changes in biodiversity data were driven by increased birdwatching or photovoltaic development.
Chinese ecologists generally agree that amid cutting carbon emissions, biodiversity can be protected through careful planning, Ma Zhijun, deputy director of the China Ornithological Society and a co-author of the analysis, told Sixth Tone. Ma is also a professor at Fudan University’s School of Life Sciences.
Such planning means avoiding key wildlife habitats when building solar, wind, and other renewable energy facilities, Ma said.
He added that the “easy availability” of birdwatching datasets has led researchers without a background in bird ecology to use them without “fully understanding their limitations.”

items.title: After ‘Sleep No More,’ What’s Next for Chinese Immersive Theater?
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018941/After ‘Sleep No More,’ What’s Next for Chinese Immersive Theater?
items.summary: China’s immersive productions have grown ever larger and more spectacular. Their next challenge is turning audience participation into genuine understanding.
items.body_text:
After ‘Sleep No More,’ What’s Next for Chinese Immersive Theater?
After 2,670 performances, the immersive theatrical production “Sleep No More,” co-produced by Shanghai Media Group and pioneering British theater company Punchdrunk, will conclude its 10-year run at the McKinnon Hotel in Shanghai on Aug. 30.
When it opened in Shanghai a decade ago, the production wowed local theatergoers with its novelty and impact. Audience members donned white masks and entered a dimly lit building where they could move freely between rooms: following Macbeth, searching for the witches, or wandering the corridors piecing together clues. No one could see the complete story, but “missing out” was part of the experience.
A decade on, immersive theater has blossomed across China, appearing in theaters, scenic areas, museums, shopping malls, and former factories. There are even purpose-built theatrical theme parks. “Unique Henan,” for example, in the suburbs of Zhengzhou, capital of the central Henan province, features 21 performance spaces and nearly 1,000 actors performing almost 700 minutes of material each day. Visitors can spend an entire day exploring the park and still see only a fraction of what it offers. Meanwhile, “Unique Dream of Red Mansions” in Langfang, in the northern Hebei province, takes the classic Chinese novel “Dream of the Red Chamber” as its theme, with four large theaters, eight smaller ones, and 108 interconnected immersive spaces. Its daily performances total more than 800 minutes.
Was all this brought about by “Sleep No More”? Yes and no.
In traditional theater, the theatrical world is confined to the other side of the stage, while the audience sits in darkness and watches a carefully framed reality. This model came under scrutiny in the 20th century. Avant-garde theater pioneers, including Antonin Artaud, Jerzy Grotowski, Peter Brook, and Richard Schechner, reexamined the body, space, presence, and the relationship between audiences and performers. Schechner, in particular, developed the concept of “environmental theater,” emphasizing that a theatrical event encompasses not only performers and text but also the audience, sensory stimuli, architecture, and other elements of the performance space. Modern theater has since continued to seek ways to move audiences beyond fixed seats and into cities, rivers, markets, and historical settings, making space part of the work itself.
Such practices are nothing new in Chinese theater. From 1932 to 1937, playwright Xiong Foxi went to Ding County in Hebei as part of a movement to popularize theater in rural China. His productions integrated stage scenery with the real sky and surrounding forest, while audiences crossed the fourth wall to participate directly in the performance.
Since the early 2000s, director Wang Chaoge’s pioneering “Impression” and “Encore” series have reshaped the spatial aesthetics of China’s cultural tourism performances through large-scale live productions. They took theater beyond the proscenium arch and into outdoor landscapes, familiarizing audiences with expansive, panoramic, and interactive performances. “Encore Pingyao,” which premiered in 2013 in Pingyao, in the northern Shanxi province, went further by dispensing with the traditional stage entirely. Audiences walked through streets, courtyards, and indoor spaces alongside the actors.
“Sleep No More” was therefore by no means the starting point for immersive theater in China. Long before its arrival, Chinese audiences were already familiar with shared spaces, physical participation, and collective rituals. Nevertheless, it marked an important watershed. It gave Chinese theater practitioners an internationally influential model: a mature, replicable, sustainable, and long-running production. By combining free movement, multiple narratives, repeat viewings, and word-of-mouth recommendations, it demonstrated that audiences were willing to pay for highly personalized live experiences.

items.title: Hundreds Still Missing After Deadly China-Nepal Border Mudslide
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018953/Hundreds Still Missing After Deadly China-Nepal Border Mudslide
items.summary: Search teams are still working through deep mud and broken roads as an upstream landslide dam raises fears of further flooding.
items.body_text:
Hundreds Still Missing After Deadly China-Nepal Border Mudslide
On Monday, Zhao Jianing rode his motorcycle through the Gyirong border checkpoint under clear skies, inching past export trucks and lines of BYD vehicles as traffic backed up along the China-Nepal border. He recalled seeing at least a dozen uniformed workers at their posts.
Two days later, a massive surge of water, mud, and debris descended from the Nepali side of the Himalayas and tore through the border area at around 11 a.m. Wednesday. Funneled through a steep valley toward southwestern China’s Xizang Autonomous Region, the torrent swept away police posts and buried the Gyirong checkpoint.
Surveillance footage from outside the checkpoint showed muddy floodwaters surging above the border gates and engulfing the area within seconds as people fled. Aerial footage from state broadcaster CCTV later showed the border zone blanketed in mud, with no buildings visible.
By Thursday, three people had been confirmed dead and 558 remained missing in Gyirong County on the Chinese side, while two people had been rescued. Across the affected area, at least 273 people were dead and 1,384 remained missing.
China’s Ministry of Water Resources told CCTV that a landslide dam had formed upstream, creating a lake containing an estimated 2 million cubic meters of water. The lake was already overflowing, and another 3 million cubic meters were expected to channel into it over the next three days, raising the risk that the dam could fail.
The threat further complicated rescue efforts already hampered by damaged roads and communications infrastructure.
Xizang activated its highest-level emergency response, deploying military transport aircraft, more than 800 firefighters, and armed police officers to the area. Central authorities also allocated 220 million yuan ($30.7 million) for disaster relief, recovery, and reconstruction.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived in the mudslide-hit area of Gyirong Township on Thursday to oversee rescue and relief efforts, state news agency Xinhua reported. He visited on behalf of President Xi Jinping and met rescue workers and people displaced by the disaster.
Wang Qian, an official with the Shigatse military sub-command, told CCTV that the edge of the mudslide was about 2.5 kilometers from the Gyirong checkpoint, where mud was nearly 1.5 meters deep.
Gyirong is Xizang’s largest land port and a major gateway for trade and travel between China and Nepal. As of June 23, the checkpoint had recorded more than 100,000 entries and exits this year, up 12.85% from the same period in 2025.
Crossing into Nepal two days earlier, Zhao, a 26-year-old motorcyclist from Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, remembered the checkpoint as busy but ordinary, with clear skies, lines of export vehicles, and workers directing traffic.
One of those workers, a uniformed man Zhao estimated to be in his 30s, had briefly argued with him over his speed.
After seeing footage of police posts being swept away, Zhao said he kept thinking about the encounter. “I never imagined that just one or two days later, everything would be gone,” Zhao told Sixth Tone. “It happened so fast. I think he probably had no chance to escape. I feel really guilty and upset.”
The road on the Nepalese side beyond the checkpoint was extremely difficult to navigate, he said. In some places, the mud was “as deep as half the length of an arm,” he said, forcing him to use both feet to keep the motorcycle moving. His shoes even came off.
“The cliff was on the right and the muddy road was on the left. I could barely ride. I thought I was going to die there,” he said.
No official investigation has established the cause of Wednesday’s disaster, but several experts said preliminary evidence points to a possible high-altitude ice-rock avalanche originating from a tributary of the Donglin Tsangpo River in Nepal.

MOSCOW, August 28. /TASS/. Russia’s stock market closed in the green on Friday as the ruble-denominated MOEX Index added 1.03% to 2,114.93 points, while the dollar-denominated RTS Index gained 1.45% to 778.32 points. The yuan exchange rate against the ruble rose by 8 kopecks to 12.9 rubles.
BCS World of Investment believes the MOEX Index could continue its rise toward the nearest resistance level around 2,150 points unless there is significant negative news. The yuan could attempt to break through the psychologically important level of 13 rubles early next week.
According to Freedom Global, the MOEX Index may trade within the 2,100-2,200-point range on Monday. Forecasts for the dollar, euro, and yuan exchange rates for Monday are 85-87 rubles, 98-100 rubles, and 12.5-13 rubles, respectively.
According to Tsifra Broker, with the peak of tax payments now past, the balance of risks points to a further gradual weakening of the ruble toward the upper ends of the ranges of 12.6-13 rubles per Chinese yuan, 85-87 rubles per dollar, and 99-101 rubles per euro.

items.body_text:
NEW YORK, August 28. /TASS/. Fourteen Russian men and women will compete in singles at the 2026 US Open in this year’s final Grand Slam tournament opening on Sunday.
In men’s singles Russia will be represented by Daniil Medvedev (7th-seed), Andrey Rublev (23rd), Karen Khachanov and Roman Safiullin (both unseeded).
On the women's side, they have: Mirra Andreeva (5th-seed), Diana Shnaider (15th), Yekaterina Alexandrova (18th), Anna Kalinskaya (21st), Lyudmila Samsonova, Anna Blinkova, Alina Korneyeva, Anastasia Zakharova (all unseeded), Polina Yatsenko and Kristina Lyutova, two of the tournament's many qualifiers.
Russia’s Yelena Pridankina still has a chance to enter the women’s singles if she gets a lucky-loser pass.
The 2026 US Open is played on outdoor hard courts at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York between August 30 and September 13. The tournament will award a record $108 million in prize money. Aryna Sabalenka from Belarus and Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz are the tournament’s reigning champions in women’s and men’s singles respectively.
Russian tennis players are participating in international tournaments under a neutral status. The US Open is no exception.
Russian players’ neutral status at tennis tournaments
On February 28, 2022, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) issued recommendations to international sports federations to bar athletes from Russia and Belarus from taking part in international tournaments, citing Moscow's special military operation in Ukraine as the reason.
Following the IOC's recommendations in late February 2022, the majority of global sports federations moved to exclude athletes from Russia and Belarus from all international sports tournaments.
The International Tennis Federation (ITF) ruled on March 1, 2022, to suspend the membership of the Russian and Belarusian national tennis federations while also canceling all previously scheduled tennis tournaments in the two countries.
On March 14, 2022, the ITF also confirmed its prohibition on the Russian and Belarusian national tennis teams from participating in the 2022 Davis Cup and the 2022 Billie Jean King Cup.

items.title: Ukraine’s budget deficit in 2027 could exceed projections — Bloomberg
items.summary: According to the report, talks between Kiev and the International Monetary Fund have faced headwinds due to "politically sensitive demands" from the country’s second-largest lender
items.body_text:
NEW YORK, August 28. /TASS/. Ukraine's budget deficit in 2027 could be larger than forecast, requiring additional aid from the European Union as a result, Bloomberg wrote, citing sources.
Talks between Kiev and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have faced headwinds due to "politically sensitive demands" from the country’s second-largest lender, sources said.
In July, the IMF projected that Ukraine’s deficit would total 17.8% of GDP in 2027 - 3.3 percentage points lower than in 2025. However, this forecast presumes that the Ukraine conflict will end in 2026, the agency noted. "As the war drags on, the figure is expected to be revised upward," Bloomberg said, citing one of its sources.
It's still unclear just how big Ukraine's budget deficit will be, while finding the money to keep the country is an equally murky prospect, he said. Moreover, the impact on the IMF program remains a mystery. Last week Kiev started a new round of negotiations with the IMF to release a new aid tranche. Should those fall through, Kiev could lose $5 bln worth of international aid this year alone.
The Financial Times reported on Thursday, citing sources, that a number of European countries feared that the financial aid provided by the EU would be insufficient for Kiev, leading many to speculate that they would once again try to seize Russia’s frozen assets. Among EU members supporting the initiative are Sweden, the Netherlands, Spain, and Poland.

items.title: Warsaw wants nuclear deterrence, but without nukes
items.summary: Warsaw wants to participate in NATO’s and the EU’s nuclear deterrence schemes but appears unwilling to host such weaponry itself Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Warsaw wants nuclear deterrence, but without nukes
Poland has sent confusing signals regarding the potential deployment of nuclear weaponry on its territory, in what appears to be an attempt to enjoy the fruits of deterrence without hosting foreign munitions.
In recent months, a dozen European NATO members, including Poland, have expressed a desire to either host nuclear weapons or take part in nuclear-sharing initiatives to varying degrees. Apart from existing nuclear sharing within the bloc, which involves hosting US munitions, France has proposed an EU-focused scheme to deploy its own weapons to willing nations.
The confusion began on Thursday, when Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski appeared to rule out ever hosting the weaponry on the country’s soil.
“I would like to say very clearly and openly: Poland does not want to have nuclear warheads on its territory,” Zalewski told reporters at NATO headquarters in Brussels. “We want to participate in NATO nuclear deterrence, [which] does not mean to have a nuclear warhead on our territory.”
The remarks caused quite a stir, with some interpreting it as a refusal to participate in the proposed European or even existing NATO nuclear-sharing schemes. The confusion prompted Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz to step in and assure the public that Warsaw still wants to participate in nuclear sharing.
“To dispel any doubts: Poland remains steadfastly interested in participating in the NATO Nuclear Sharing program. We are also conducting talks regarding the proposal for participation in the European nuclear protective umbrella. Our government’s stance on these issues is unequivocal,” he wrote on X.
While the minister did not explicitly say whether Warsaw was open to hosting foreign nukes, Zalewski doubled down on his original remarks later in the day. Poland remains committed to participating in “NATO’s nuclear deterrence, [but] without storing nuclear weapons,” the official wrote on X while berating those confused by his statements. “Security requires competence and seriousness. Claiming that Nuclear Sharing [equates to] storing nuclear weapons in Poland is ignorance or deliberate manipulation,” he asserted.

items.title: Iran may be the key to the Mecca Pact’s future
items.summary: Tehran’s possible inclusion could turn a tentative defense bloc into the basis of a broader regional security order Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Iran may be the key to the Mecca Pact’s future
The reported invitation for Iran to join the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement puts a new perspective on what the new alliance might ultimately become.
Mehdi Rahimi, head of the Iranian parliament’s news agency, said that the proposal was under consideration by the country’s leadership and argued that the creation of a regional security umbrella would represent a victory for the Islamic Republic. Shortly afterwards, however, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stated that Tehran had received no formal invitation, although proposals for dialogue with the pact’s members on collective regional security had indeed been raised. For the moment, this appears to be a political overture intended to test the reactions of the parties rather than the beginning of a formal accession process. Even so, it suggests that the agreement is not intended as an alliance against Tehran, but as the possible foundation of a security system built with Iranian participation.
The Mecca Agreement was signed on August 7 by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Its central provision declares that an armed attack against one member will be regarded as an attack against all. The formula theoretically combines a formidable set of capabilities: Saudi Arabia’s immense financial resources and influence over global energy markets, Türkiye’s large military and sophisticated defence industry, and Pakistan’s substantial military experience and nuclear arsenal. Yet the public statements offer no detailed decision-making procedure and do not specify what action each signatory would be obliged to take during a crisis. At this stage, the pact is only a political declaration of collective deterrence and not a proper military alliance.
Erosion of the American monopoly
Donald Trump welcomed the pact and expressed satisfaction that the states of the region were finally assuming greater responsibility for their own defense. His response was consistent with his longstanding view that Washington’s allies should bear a larger share of military expenditure, allowing the US to reduce its costs and step back from the role of unconditional guarantor of other nations’ security. Seen from this perspective, the agreement might appear to be a success for American policy, since three US partners are establishing an additional mechanism of deterrence without Washington’s direct involvement.
Yet behind this public enthusiasm lies a trend that is far less favorable to the US. The Mecca Pact cannot be described as the first symptom of declining American influence in the Middle East, but it is the clearest institutional sign to date that regional powers no longer regard the American security umbrella as sufficient and have begun constructing autonomous centers of power. Washington retains its military bases, weapons systems, intelligence capabilities and relationships with regional elites, but it is gradually losing its monopoly over the rules by which Middle Eastern security is organized.
The US-Israeli war against Iran accelerated this transformation because it revealed the double-edged nature of American security guarantees. The US military presence may deter adversaries, but it can also draw the Gulf states into conflicts whose timing and objectives are determined without their meaningful participation. Iranian strikes, disruption to maritime trade and threats to energy infrastructure demonstrated that a close partnership with Washington does not insulate regional states from danger and may instead force them to bear the consequences of American policy.
Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan are not abandoning American weapons or political ties, yet they want a mechanism capable of functioning even when Washington’s priorities diverge from their own.

items.title: Sovereignty on the ballot in Iceland’s EU referendum
items.summary: Icelanders are about to vote on restarting EU accession talks, but the ‘no’ side says the country’s sovereignty is at stake Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Sovereignty on the ballot in Iceland’s EU referendum
After decades outside the bloc’s periphery, Iceland is about to hold a referendum on reopening membership talks with the EU. Is the Viking nation preparing to trade sovereignty for stability? Or is it climbing aboard a sinking ship?
Icelanders go to the polls on Saturday, August 29 to answer a straightforward, yes or no question: “Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?”
The referendum is not legally binding, but liberal Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir has pledged to honor its result.
What stage are talks between Iceland and Brussels at?
Iceland applied for EU membership in 2009, in the chaotic aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis. The country’s three biggest banks, Kaupthing, Landsbanki, and Glitnir, collapsed in the same week, and rather than force taxpayers to cover their balance sheets, Reykjavik washed its hands of the problem and let them fail.
The Icelandic krona plummeted, inflation soared, and center-right Prime Minister Geir Haarde resigned. Amid the meltdown, the newly empowered Social Democrats argued that by joining the EU and adopting the euro, Iceland could shield itself from future shocks – even as Iceland recovered far more quickly than EU members such as Greece, Ireland, and Portugal, which were subjected to crippling austerity measures by Brussels, the World Bank, and the IMF in the wake of the crisis.
The Social Democrats won the argument, convincing their left-wing, Euroskeptic coalition partners to vote for application. The left agreed, with the caveat that the final membership deal would be put to the people in a referendum.
Following a change of government, accession talks were shelved in 2013. Iceland, it was reasoned, had emerged from the financial crisis in good shape, and joining the EU would erode the island nation’s sovereignty, potentially diluting its control of rich fishing grounds, with no tangible benefits in return.
How do the polls stand before the vote?
With less than a day to go, the latest polls suggest that the vote will come down to the wire. A poll by market research firm Maskina published on August 25 shows the referendum passing by 51.3% to 48.7%. Two days later, a Gallup poll showed a near mirror inversion of these results, with the ‘no’ side leading by 51.6% to 48.4%. The result in both surveys was inside the margin of error, making the outcome impossible to predict. However, the ‘no’ side has been steadily closing the gap since July, and if the trend holds, could succeed in putting membership talks on ice for the foreseeable future.
The Yes vote: Safety in numbers
The two major parties in Frostadottir’s coalition – her Social Democrats and Foreign Minister Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir’s Reform Party – support EU membership. Their arguments are the same as they were in 2009, with one key addition: Membership would add a layer of defense against any potential attempts by US President Donald Trump to gain control over Iceland, as he is currently threatening Greenland. Although this is an unlikely scenario, the current US ambassador in Reykjavik caused widespread anger in January when he joked “that Iceland will be the 52nd state and he’ll be governor."
To Foreign Minister Gunnarsdottir, membership provides safety in numbers. “That is so important for us to see a group of like-minded nations stand together on principles and values,” she told AP. “That is also what I’m looking at when I see the European Union in this volatile world.”
Iceland’s six other major parties – from conservatives to centrists to leftists – all oppose membership. In an effort to persuade their voters, Frostadottir has sold the referendum as a zero-risk proposition. A ‘yes’ vote would merely restart talks, she has argued, pointing out that any deal offered by Brussels would still have to pass another referendum. It would also give Icelanders “the option of seeing what an agreement looks like,” she said last month.

items.title: Russian Military Conducts Mobile ICBM Test
items.summary: The missile was launched from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome in the northwestern Arkhangelsk region, the Defense Ministry said.
items.body_text:
Russia’s Defense Ministry announced Friday that it conducted a successful combat training launch of a mobile, solid-fuel intercontinental ballistic missile from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome in the northwestern Arkhangelsk region.
The Strategic Missile Forces deployed a mobile launcher battery to a remote area before firing the missile across the country to the Kura test site on the Kamchatka Peninsula, located more than 6,700 kilometers (4,160 miles) to the east.
Video released by the Defense Ministry showed the missile launch from a forested location.
The military said the goal of the launch was to confirm the “tactical, technical and flight characteristics of the missile system.” 
“All assigned tasks were completed in full,” the ministry said, adding that the ICBM maintained a “flawless trajectory.”
It did not identify the missile used in the launch. The Defense Ministry reportedly launched the RS-24 Yars system from Plesetsk to Kura as part of wide-ranging missile forces exercises in mid-May.
The latest launch comes less than a week after unverified reports claimed that Ukrainian drones targeted Plesetsk, Russia’s only military spaceport.

items.title: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Ukrainian Presidential Aide Oleksiy Arestovych 11 Years in Absentia
items.summary: A judge found Arestovych guilty of spreading false information about the Russian military and publicly calling for terrorism.
items.body_text:
A judge in Moscow on Friday sentenced Oleksiy Arestovych, a former adviser to the Ukrainian president’s office, to 11 years in prison in absentia after finding him guilty of spreading false information about the Russian military and publicly calling for terrorism.
Russian investigators accused Arestovych of publishing false statements about a deadly Russian missile strike on a railway station in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk in April 2022.
Prosecutors also accused Arestovych of calling on Ukrainians to sabotage railway lines used to resupply Russian troops in a March 2022 video.
A judge from the Second Western District Military Court delivered the guilty verdict against Arestovych following a closed-door trial.
In addition to the 11-year prison sentence, the judge also banned Arestovych from managing websites for four years.
Prosecutors had requested a sentence of 15 years in prison for Arestovych, according to the exiled news outlet Mediazona.
“What a sophisticated cover-up operation,” Arestovych wrote on Telegram in response to the court ruling.
Arestovych served as an adviser to the head of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s office until January 2023, when he resigned after claiming a Ukrainian air defense missile caused a deadly strike on an apartment in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro.
He has since recast himself as a critic of the Ukrainian government and amassed an online following on his YouTube channel. Arestovych now lives outside of Ukraine. Zelensky sanctioned him last year.
Russia added Arestovych to its list of “terrorists and extremists” in May 2023 and placed him on its wanted list in October 2023. Moscow’s Basmanny District Court placed Arestovych in pre-trial detention in absentia in February 2024.

items.title: Sverdlovsk Region Court Bars Yabloko From Regional Assembly Race
items.summary: Sverdlovsk is the fifth region where Yabloko has had its list of candidates barred from running in the regional assembly races in September.
items.body_text:
A judge in the Sverdlovsk region has disqualified the liberal Yabloko party’s list of candidates from the upcoming regional assembly elections, the court said Friday.
The regional ban follows Russia’s Supreme Court ruling last week to reject Yabloko’s final appeal against a nationwide ban barring its candidate list from the State Duma elections next month.
The Sverdlovsk Regional Court ruled in favor of a lawsuit filed by the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR), which accused Yabloko of a range of violations that include those cited in the Supreme Court ruling.
LDPR claimed Yabloko committed copyright infringement, overspent its funds and shared content on banned platforms like Instagram and Facebook. Konstantin Kiselyov, who leads Yabloko’s Sverdlovsk region list of candidates, argued that the same accusations can be leveled against the other parties running in the elections, including LDPR.
“Each party and their leaders are on these banned social networks. I come across official state agencies there, and they can’t live without them,” Kommersant quoted Kiselyov as saying in court.
Yaroslav Shcherbakov, another Yabloko member in the Sverdlovsk region, also accused LDPR of openly calling for the elimination of its political competitor.
Yabloko’s Yekaterinburg branch said it would appeal the ruling.
The Sverdlovsk region is the fifth in Russia where Yabloko has had its list of candidates barred from running in the regional assembly races in September, either through court rulings or rejections by local election commissions.
Yabloko faces the risk of being stripped of its official registration due to legal requirements to field candidates in at least 20% of regional assembly elections or 10% of gubernatorial races every seven years, according to exiled journalist Farida Rustamova.

items.title: Aluminum producer Rusal promises to ‘minimize the socioeconomic consequences’ of mothballing the plants whose closure once forced Putin to intervene
items.summary: Aluminum producer Rusal plans to temporarily mothball part of its raw materials production in Russia, the business daily Kommersant said, citing a letter seen by journalists that the company sent to Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin.
items.body_text:
Aluminum producer Rusal promises to ‘minimize the socioeconomic consequences’ of mothballing the plants whose closure once forced Putin to intervene
Aluminum producer Rusal plans to temporarily mothball part of its raw materials production in Russia, the business daily Kommersant said, citing a letter seen by journalists that the company sent to Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin.
The plan includes the Pikalyovo Alumina Refinery (PGLZ), the Severouralsk Bauxite Mine (SUBR), and the alumina-producing Bogoslovsk and Ural plants, according to Kommersant.
The enterprises generate $800 million in annual losses for Rusal, and the company estimates it will need $1.8 billion in investment to restore its raw materials division.
Rusal asked the government to consider state support for regions and municipalities, promising to “minimize the socioeconomic consequences” of the mothballing.
One source in the metals market told Kommersant the main risk of the mothballing is potential layoffs in the company towns where the plants operate, particularly Krasnoturyinsk, Severouralsk, and Kamensk-Uralsky.
Pikalyovo, a company town in the Leningrad region, became one of the major flashpoints of social unrest in 2009. After the town’s three main employers — an alumina plant, a cement plant, and a chemical plant — shut down, unemployed residents took to the streets and blocked the federal highway between Novaya Ladoga and Vologda. Then-Prime Minister Vladimir Putin traveled to the town. The State Duma, the lower house of Russia’s parliament, called what happened in Pikalyovo “an example of irresponsible behavior by business.” The plants’ operations were eventually restored.

items.body_text:
An exiled dissident’s wife returned to Russia for a visit. She’s now serving 10 days in jail — over a locked phone.
Elena Morgunova, the wife of Russian performance artist Pavel Krisevich, was detained and sentenced to 10 days of administrative arrest for disobeying police orders, the projects “Zona Svobody” and “Slovo Zashchite” said, citing those close to her.
Police detained Morgunova in Skopin, a town in Russia’s Ryazan region, on August 28. According to “Slovo Zashchite,” she had returned to Russia temporarily from France, where she and her husband have lived since leaving the country in December 2025.
Morgunova was riding a bus with her mother when police stopped it, ostensibly to check documents. According to “Slovo Zashchite,” the officers took an interest only in the two of them. After questioning Morgunova about her time in France, they sent her to court, charging her with disobeying police for refusing to unlock her phone.
Pavel Krisevich was sentenced in 2022 to five years in a penal colony over a June 2021 performance on Red Square, during which he delivered a manifesto denouncing the police state and fired two shots into the air. He was released in January 2025, and by the end of that year he had left Russia with his wife following two consecutive administrative arrests.
Former Pussy Riot activist Rita Flores said on August 24, 2026, that officers of Russia’s Federal Security Service had recruited her in early 2023. She said she agreed to cooperate with the FSB and gather information on contemporary artists, including Krisevich, with whom she was friends.

items.title: Nepal floods: How recent reports warned of this disaster months ago
items.summary: Recent floods in Nepal and Tibet followed ICIMOD's warnings about melting glaciers. These reports highlighted doubled ice loss rates and increased flood risks across the region. A catastrophic flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse killed hundreds and left many missing. Smaller glaciers are shrinking faster, intensifying hazards like glacial lake outburst floods. Regional cooperation is vital for understanding and preparing for these cross-border mountain disasters.
items.body_text:
Months before the devastating floods struck Nepal and Tibet, two landmark reports by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) had warned that rapidly melting glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya(HKH) were escalating the risks of catastrophic floods and other cryosphere-related disasters.
Released in March 2026, the reports found that glacier ice loss across the region had doubled since 2000, with the smallest and most vulnerable glaciers shrinking rapidly and intensifying hazards such as glacial lake outburst floods.
It also revealed that glaciers have lost up to 27 metres of ice thickness since 1975
The warnings have come into sharp focus after a catastrophic flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse struck the Nepal-China border region this week, killing hundreds and leaving nearly 1,000 people missing.
Researchers are investigating whether an ice-rock avalanche from a high-altitude location triggered the disaster.
ICIMOD cryosphere specialist Mohd Farooq Azam told news agency PTI that the incident involved the detachment of bedrock from beneath a glacier, with ice and rock cascading down into the valley.
âThis is basically an ice and rock avalanche. So, as per current understanding, there is a detachment of the bedrock, which means that the bedrock from below the glacier is detached from its position and came down to the valley that created this disaster,â Azam said.
HKH glaciers lost 12% of their area in three decades
The two ICIMOD reports, Changing Dynamics of Glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya Region from 1990 to 2020 and HKH Glacier Outlook 2026: Insights from 50 Years of Himalayan Glacier Monitoring, provide a detailed assessment of glacier change across the region.
According to the reports, HKH glaciers lost around 12% of their total area and 9% of their estimated ice reserves between 1990 and 2020.
The Hindu Kush Himalaya contains the largest volume of ice outside the polar regions, with more than 63,700 glaciers covering nearly 55,782 square kilometres.
Also read: 
Himalayan glaciers shrinking at alarming pace, ice loss doubled in 21st century, says ICIMOD
These glaciers feed at least ten major Asian river systems and support food, water, energy and livelihoods for billions of people downstream.
ICIMOD said around 78% of the glacier area, located between 4,500 and 6,000 metres above sea level, is highly exposed to elevation-dependent warming.
âThis isnât a distant problem; itâs a crisis unfolding in real-time, with new disasters every summer and monsoon,â Pema Gyamtsho, director General of ICIMOD, said.
âThe fact that ice loss rates have doubled this century should shock us all into action,â he added.
Smaller glaciers face faster losses and rising hazards
The ICIMOD analysis found that the region's smallest glaciers are shrinking more rapidly than others.
âBetween 1990 and 2020, HKH glaciers lost about 12% of their total area, but the losses are most acute for the regionâs smallest glaciersâthose below 0.5 kmÂ²âwhich are shrinking more rapidly than others,â Sudan Bikash Maharjan, remote sensing analyst at ICIMOD and lead author of the glacier dynamics report, said.
He warned that the trend poses immediate risks of localised water shortages for high mountain communities and intensifies hazards such as glacial lake outburst floods.
Three-fourths of the region's glaciers fall within this vulnerable size category, according to ICIMOD.
Flood-hit valley faces risk of secondary flash flood
The immediate situation in Nepal has also highlighted another danger associated with debris and temporary lakes formed after major mountain disasters.
Azam told PTI that debris from the ice-rock avalanche has accumulated at a river confluence, creating a temporary dam. Water is continuing to collect behind it, raising concerns about a possible secondary flash flood.
âThis dam is collecting water, and it is expected that over the next three days, there will be more water collected in this temporary pond

items.title: WC: Belgium break Indian hearts in shootout as Harmanpreet’s side finishes eighth
items.summary: India's spirited hockey fightback concluded with heartbreak against Belgium. The teams played to a thrilling 3-3 draw in regulation time. Belgium ultimately prevailed in a tense penalty shootout after the match. India had initially taken the lead through Abhishek's early field goal. Harmanpreet Singh scored twice to force the shootout, but Belgium won.
items.body_text:
Indiaâs spirited fightback ended in heartbreak as Belgium prevailed in a tense penalty shootout after the two sides played out a thrilling 3-3 draw in regulation time. India had made the brighter start and took the lead through Abhishek, whose sixth-minute field goal gave the hosts a 1-0 advantage. Belgium responded with sustained pressure, earning multiple penalty corners, but Indiaâs defence held firm.
The match changed dramatically in the second quarter. Roman Duvekot restored parity for Belgium with a close-range finish before Hugo Labouchere put them ahead with a powerful drag-flick from a penalty corner. Belgium went into half-time 2-1 up.
India came out strongly after the break and levelled through captain 
Harmanpreet Singh
, who converted a penalty corner with a superb drag-flick in the 31st minute. Belgium challenged the goal with a review, but the decision went India's way.
The third quarter remained fiercely contested, with Belgium applying pressure and India creating opportunities of their own. Despite Belgium enjoying more possession, India held their shape to take the scores level at 2-2 into the final quarter.
Belgium strike again, India refuse to give up
Belgium regained the lead in the 47th minute when Nicolas de Kerpel fired home a field goal. 
The goal was referred for a possible obstruction, but the original decision was upheld and Belgium moved 3-2 ahead. India were dealt another blow when veteran Manpreet Singh took a stick to the face and left the field for medical attention.
With time running out, India pulled their goalkeeper in favour of an additional outfield player and threw numbers forward in search of an equaliser. Their gamble paid off in dramatic fashion.
Harmanpreet struck again in the 60th minute, finding the target to make it 3-3 and force a penalty shootout.
Shootout drama ends India's hopes
The shootout began disastrously for India. Harmanpreet's first attempt was saved by Belgium goalkeeper Vincent Vanasch after the Indian captain appeared to stop while expecting a whistle. Belgium converted their opening attempt, while Vanasch then denied Sukhjeet Singh as well.
India eventually found their rhythm. Shilanand Lakra opened India's account before Belgium restored their advantage. Dilpreet Singh then converted to bring the shootout level at 2-2.
Belgium regained the lead through a penalty stroke after Mohith was penalised for a foul on Van Dessel, with Hendrickx converting. India stayed alive when Abhishek scored to make it 3-3.
The decisive moment came when Duvekot found the target for Belgium. India took a referral in an attempt to overturn the decision, but the call stood.
Belgium therefore won the shootout and ended India's brave fight after an extraordinary contest and they finish 8th in this World Cup.

items.title: A shared disaster, beyond borders and geopolitics
items.summary: For Nepal, India and China, the devastating cross-border floods are a stark reminder of nature’s fury, and that cooperation must transcend the boundaries of geopolitics
items.body_text:
On Wednesday, August 26, 2026, at approximately 8.44 a.m. Nepal time, what initially appeared to be a 4.4-magnitude earthquake struck near the Nepal-China border. It triggered the collapse of an enormous glacial slab, which plunged a kilometre below to the valley floor, resulting in devastating flash floods. The United States Geological Survey later confirmed that the seismic activity was, in fact, the glacial collapse itself and the landslide (later registered as equivalent to an earthquake measuring 5.2) rather than by tectonic shifts. Preliminary estimates suggest that 579 people have perished in Nepal, with nearly 2,000 people missing, many of them believed to be foreigners.
Entire villages and towns that this writer has previously travelled through have been swept away. Vital infrastructure, such as bridges and hydropower stations, has been completely decimated. A staggering 475 megawatts of generating capacity has been wiped off Nepal’s electricity grid. This may go down as the most devastating natural disaster Nepal has ever witnessed.
Nature’s fury knows no borders
For Nepal and its two neighbours, India and China, which ordinarily see themselves caught up in geopolitical contestations in the country, the catastrophic force of Mother Nature is a reminder that the political dimensions of geography are relevant only insofar as nature does not intervene, unexpectedly and destructively. The natural world does not recognise political boundaries in the same way that the custodians of nation-states do. China and India both suffered substantial losses from Wednesday’s floods. Human and property losses continue to mount in all three countries, including Nepal.
China’s Gyirong Port, the largest land trade port in the Tibet Autonomous Region and the primary gateway between Nepal and China, was designated an international-standard land port. An upgrade in August 2017 led to its transformation, upgrading it from a bilateral crossing to a fully recognised international gateway.
Built at a cost of $175.8 million, the port and the services it provided are now effectively buried beneath heavy sediment and debris.
Access roads on the Chinese side leading to the Nepal border, as well as power supplies and local communication links, have been completely severed or severely damaged. There are reports of fatalities on the Chinese side — a number that is almost certain to rise. There are also reports of people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong County, including foreign nationals.
Editorial | Danger from above: On the Nepal flood
The loss of human life for India is tragic, with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) confirming that Indian nationals are missing or untraced. Most of them were tourists-cum-pilgrims headed to the abode of Lord Shiva at Kailash Mansarovar. This is a route this writer has travelled on more than a few occasions. The pilgrims would have driven from Kathmandu through the lush, rocky and distinctly narrow river valley to reach Gyirong Port, before proceeding further upwards to the majestic Tibetan Plateau.
Flood fallout for India
For India, the downstream flood threats to its States have been severe, although the immediate threat from some of these events may have passed. Floodwaters reached the Gandak, Kosi and Ganga rivers in Bihar, prompting authorities in Patna to go on maximum alert and deploy large teams, particularly to the Valmikinagar Barrage and along vulnerable embankments, to monitor alarmingly high water levels. Riverside communities were evacuated to safer locations. Authorities in Uttar Pradesh also went on alert, with the State’s Relief Commissioner tracking developments in real time, as overflowing rivers from Nepal naturally flow into Indian territory.
Border districts such as Maharajganj and Kushinagar stepped up emergency surveillance and deployed emergency personnel. India’s National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) deployed teams across the Bihar-Uttar Pradesh border area. New Delhi also activated an exten

items.title: Nepal flood toll rises to 579; nearly 2,000 still missing
items.summary: More than 4,500 people, including 85 Indians, were rescued; 98 Indian tourists are still unaccounted for; the Nepal govt. allows foreign experts to join the search operation following intense diplomatic pressure
items.body_text:
The death toll in the Nepal flash floods touched 579 on Friday (August 28, 2026), even as the search for nearly 2,000 missing people continued for the third day after the disaster struck.
Also read: Nepal flash flood updates on August 28, 2026
The Nepal Police said more than 4,500 people had been rescued. Of the 183 Indian tourists reported missing, 85 had been rescued while 98 remained unaccounted for, the Nepal Tourism Board said.
Indians account for the highest number of missing foreign nationals.
People from more than 30 countries are among those reported missing, the Board said. They include 65 from the United States, 61 from Ukraine, 51 from Malaysia, 35 from Australia, and 33 from the United Kingdom.
Amid questions over how flooding on such a massive scale could have occurred in the Bhotekoshi river in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when no rain was recorded, scientists are working to piece together the chain of events.
Nepali authorities have said the disaster may have originated in the Lhende Khola on the Nepali side. The Lhende Khola is a transboundary, high-altitude river that originates in Gyirong County in Tibet and flows south into Nepal, where it joins the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems.
Scientists believe an ice-and-rock collapse may have sent debris into the Lhende valley, temporarily blocking the river before a massive surge of water and debris swept downstream into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers.
Note of caution
Nepal’s Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, drawing on satellite imagery shared by the Chinese side, has reached a similar preliminary conclusion.
According to an official at the department, the imagery pointed to a combination of an ice avalanche, permafrost movement, and a rockslide. “The avalanche originated on the Nepali side of the territory, but very close to the boundary, and caused flooding that crossed the Nepal-China border, causing extensive damage on both sides,” said Binod Parajuli, a senior divisional hydrologist at the department’s Flood Forecasting Division.
He said a full technical assessment was still pending, as the department’s immediate focus remained on rescue operations. He said there was still a risk of further flooding, although it was unlikely to be on the same scale, and urged people living in the area to exercise caution.
Diplomatic pressure
Meanwhile, the Nepal government has reversed its earlier decision not to seek assistance from international search and rescue teams. Sources said the government decided to seek help from foreign experts in limited areas following intense diplomatic pressure from countries whose citizens remained unaccounted for after the disaster.
On Wednesday (August 26, 2026), the government said Nepali rescuers were capable of carrying out search and rescue operations and that it would not permit rescue teams from other countries to enter Nepal. But on Friday (August 28, 2026), the government decided to seek assistance from a limited number of foreign specialists for tunnel rescue operations, DNA testing, and forensic examinations.
In a social media post, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said reports that the country had rejected foreign assistance were misleading. He said the government was continuously coordinating with India, China and international partners on the assistance and supplies needed for rescue and relief operations.
