items.title: Motta acelera MP do fim da taxa das blusinhas e marca votação na Câmara para segunda-feira
items.summary: Presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta
items.body_text:
Motta acelera MP do fim da taxa das blusinhas e marca votação na Câmara para segunda-feira
Lula conseguiu emplacar aliados na presidência e relatoria da comissão que analisa a medida
O presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), marcou para a próxima segunda-feira a votação da medida provisória (MP) sobre o fim da “taxa das blusinhas”. A medida está prevista para ser votada pelo plenário da Câmara na noite de segunda, logo após ser analisada por uma comissão mista com deputados e senadores.
A manutenção do fim da cobrança de 20% sobre compras internacionais de até US$ 50 é uma das bandeiras eleitorais que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pretende usar na campanha à reeleição.
Pelo calendário estabelecido, a comissão mista vai analisar a MP durante reunião que está marcada para 16h de segunda. Logo depois, a partir das 18h, o plenário da Câmara deve votar a iniciativa.
O texto teve sua tramitação acelerada após ficar travado no Congresso por falta de acordo.
A MP estava travada e corria o risco de perder a validade sem ser votada devido à pressão da oposição, de empresários do setor produtivo e de um afastamento entre o presidente Lula e o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP).
Lula conseguiu emplacar aliados no comando da comissão mista após se reaproximar do presidente do Senado. O deputado Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG) é o presidente do colegiado e a senadora Leila Barros (PDT-DF) é a relatora.
A escolha dos principais postos da comissão aconteceu após uma reunião entre Lula, Alcolumbre e Motta. Após a conversa, foi fechado um entendimento para ela ser votada antes da data limite, prevista para o dia 8 de setembro.
Nas últimas semanas, Lula se reconciliou com o presidente do Senado. Os dois estavam afastados desde a rejeição pelo Senado da indicação do advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias, para o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).
A MP acaba com a cobrança de 20% para produtos importados de até US$ 50. O termo "taxa das blusinhas", que a MP quer dar fim, é utilizado para se referir ao programa Remessa Conforme, criado para viabilizar a cobrança do Imposto de Importação de 20% sobre compras internacionais de até US$ 50.
Antes, na prática, a taxa estava zerada. Para compras acima de US$ 50, segue valendo o imposto de 60%.
A retomada do debate ocorre em um contexto de pressão sobre o custo de vida e de tentativa do Palácio do Planalto de melhorar a percepção de renda da população.
O debate ganha tração em um contexto no qual o governo também trabalha em medidas para reduzir o custo de crédito e o comprometimento de renda da população com dívidas.
O principal receio para redução da taxa das blusinhas era a reação do varejo doméstico, que passou a defender a tributação como forma de equilibrar a concorrência com plataformas estrangeiras.

items.summary: O cantor Zé Felipe disse que estava “indo atrás” da “paixãozinha” que tinha “acabado de chegar”, na madrugada desta sexta-feira (28), no hangar do Parque do Peão, em Barretos (SP). A fala foi registrada em vídeo por um amigo do cantor, publicado nas redes sociais, e viralizou porque a ex-namorada Ana Castela desembarcou no local pouco antes. Zé Felipe não citou o nome dela.
items.body_text:
Zé Felipe disse que estava "indo atrás" da "paixão" que tinha "acabado de chegar", na madrugada desta sexta-feira (28), no Parque do Peão, em Barretos (SP). A fala foi registrada em vídeo por um amigo do cantor e publicada nas redes sociais. Ele não citou o nome de ninguém.
As imagens foram feitas no hangar onde pousam as aeronaves que levam artistas à Festa do Peão. Zé Felipe aparece com amigos, comemora e avisa que estava deixando a festa. Ao ser perguntado sobre o que fazia ali, responde: "Indo atrás da minha paixão". Em seguida, completa: "Eu tenho um pouquinho de paixão, e ela acabou de chegar".
O vídeo passou a circular porque a cantora Ana Castela, ex-namorada de Zé Felipe, tinha desembarcado no mesmo hangar minutos antes. Ele havia se apresentado horas antes no Palco Camping, e ela voltou ao parque na madrugada. Não há registro de encontro entre os dois.
O que mostra o vídeo
No registro, Zé Felipe não menciona nome, cidade ou qualquer outro elemento que identifique a pessoa de quem fala. Depois de dizer que tem "um pouquinho de paixão", minimiza: afirma que "passa rápido também".
As imagens mostram apenas a conversa entre ele e os amigos no hangar.
Namoraram por dois meses em 2025
Zé Felipe e Ana Castela assumiram o namoro em outubro de 2025, com fotos publicadas nas redes sociais. O relacionamento durou cerca de dois meses e terminou em dezembro, sem troca de acusações.
Em entrevista em abril deste ano, Ana Castela afirmou que a relação virou amizade. "Já criamos essa relação de amizade, não tem mais nada, e vai continuar dessa forma", disse.
Os dois na Festa do Peão
Zé Felipe, de 28 anos, é filho do cantor Leonardo, que se apresenta no Estádio de Barretos neste sábado (29). Nesta edição da festa, comandou a terceira edição do projeto "Uma Por Ano", no Palco Camping, na noite de quinta-feira (27).
Ana Castela, de 22 anos, nasceu em Amambai (MS) e foi criada em Sete Quedas, também no Mato Grosso do Sul. Conhecida como "Boiadeira", estourou em 2022 com "Pipoco" e se tornou o principal nome do agronejo. Cantou no Estádio na sexta-feira de abertura, dia 21.
LEIA TAMBÉM

items.title: Leandro Domingos recebe homenagem da Assembleia Legislativa de SC
items.summary: Leandro Domingos recebe placa de reconhecimento durante sessão especial da Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina, em Florianópolis. Alesc / Divulgação O presidente do Sistema Fecomércio-Sesc-Senac Acre e vice-presidente Financeiro da Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC), Leandro Domingos Teixeira Pinto, foi homenageado pela Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina (Alesc), na noite desta segunda-feira (10), em Florianópolis, durante uma sessão especial em comemo
items.body_text:
Leandro Domingos recebe placa de reconhecimento durante sessão especial da Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina, em Florianópolis. — Foto: Alesc / Divulgação
O presidente do Sistema Fecomércio-Sesc-Senac Acre e vice-presidente Financeiro da Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC), Leandro Domingos Teixeira Pinto, foi homenageado pela Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina (Alesc), na noite desta segunda-feira (10), em Florianópolis, durante uma sessão especial em comemoração aos 78 anos da Fecomércio-SC e aos 80 anos do Sesc e do Senac em Santa Catarina. A honraria reconhece sua atuação na CNC e sua contribuição para o fortalecimento do Sistema Comércio.
A solenidade foi realizada no Plenário Deputado Osni Régis, no Palácio Barriga Verde, sede do Legislativo catarinense, e reuniu dirigentes nacionais e estaduais, empresários, conselheiros, representantes de instituições parceiras e outras personalidades ligadas ao Sistema Comércio. Ao todo, 25 homenagens foram concedidas durante a sessão.
Leandro Domingos recebeu uma placa de reconhecimento concedida pelo Poder Legislativo Catarinense, na qual a Assembleia destaca os relevantes serviços prestados por ele à representação empresarial e ao Sistema Comércio.
Segundo o texto da homenagem, o Legislativo catarinense reconhece sua atuação como vice-presidente Financeiro da Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo, destacando sua contribuição para o desenvolvimento econômico, social e cultural de Santa Catarina e para o fortalecimento do Sistema Comércio no estado.
A honraria foi proposta pelo deputado estadual Berlanda e assinada pelo presidente da Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina, deputado Julio Garcia, e pelo parlamentar proponente.
Para Leandro Domingos, receber a homenagem representa não apenas um reconhecimento à sua trajetória institucional, mas também uma distinção que alcança o trabalho coletivo desenvolvido pelo Sistema Comércio em defesa do setor produtivo e do desenvolvimento econômico e social.
“Receber esta homenagem da Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina é motivo de profunda honra e, sobretudo, de grande responsabilidade. Mais do que um reconhecimento pessoal, recebo esta distinção como uma homenagem ao trabalho coletivo que o Sistema Comércio desenvolve em defesa do setor produtivo e na construção de um ambiente cada vez mais favorável ao desenvolvimento econômico e social. Representar a CNC e contribuir para o fortalecimento das Federações do Comércio, do Sesc e do Senac é uma missão que exige compromisso, diálogo e permanente dedicação. Compartilho este reconhecimento com todos aqueles que, diariamente, trabalham pela valorização do empresariado, pela geração de oportunidades e pelo desenvolvimento do nosso país. Agradeço à Assembleia Legislativa de Santa Catarina, ao deputado Berlanda e ao presidente Julio Garcia pela honraria e pela deferência, que reforçam a importância de seguirmos construindo, por meio do diálogo institucional, caminhos capazes de aproximar o setor produtivo das grandes decisões que impactam a sociedade.”
Reconhecimento à atuação no Sistema Comércio
A homenagem a Leandro Domingos ocorreu em uma solenidade que celebrou a trajetória de instituições que possuem papel estratégico na representação empresarial, na educação profissional e na promoção da qualidade de vida dos trabalhadores do comércio.
Fundada em 10 de agosto de 1948, a Fecomércio-SC completa 78 anos de atuação na representação dos setores de comércio de bens, serviços e turismo. Já o Sesc e o Senac celebram oito décadas de atividades em Santa Catarina, com ações voltadas à educação, cultura, saúde, lazer, qualificação profissional e desenvolvimento social.
A solenidade reforçou a importância da atuação conjunta do Sistema Comércio na promoção do desenvolvimento econômico e social, destacando a contribuição de dirigentes e instituições que participam dessa trajetória.

items.title: Os mapas e gráficos que mostram a magnitude e o impacto da avalanche no Nepal e Tibete
items.summary: Desastre natural ocorreu na região do Himalaia e afetou grandes áreas da fronteira entre Nepal e Tibete, deixando quase 600 mortos e 2 mil desaparecidos.
items.body_text:
Os mapas e gráficos que mostram a magnitude e o impacto da avalanche no Nepal e Tibete
  - Author, Equipe de Jornalismo Visual
  - Role, BBC News Mundo
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 2 min
Quase 600 pessoas morreram e 2 mil estão desaparecidas após uma avalanche devastadora atingir a fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete na quarta-feira (26/8).
As imagens chocantes de pessoas correndo para salvar suas vidas durante a tragédia foram vistas em todo o mundo.
As autoridades permanecem em alerta para possíveis novos deslizamentos de terra, e as equipes de resgate continuam buscando sobreviventes na área devastada.
Quase 4,5 mil pessoas estão dedicadas a essa tarefa durante o que são consideradas horas "críticas" para a recuperação dos corpos.
O desastre natural ocorreu na região do Himalaia e afetou grandes áreas da fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, incluindo a passagem de fronteira de Gyirong.
Inicialmente, foi relatado que o deslizamento de água, rochas e terra foi causado por um terremoto de magnitude 4,4, registrado pelos sensores do Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS, na sigla em inglês).
No entanto, a agência explicou posteriormente que a causa mais provável foi o colapso de uma geleira antes do terremoto.
De acordo com o USGS, foi o rompimento de grande parte de uma geleira em uma região montanhosa que causou o terremoto subsequente.
A geleira teria invadido o vale, arrastando gelo, rochas e sedimentos em seu rastro.
Os especialistas estimam que isto bloqueou o canal do rio Lhende Khola.
E quando esse bloqueio cedeu, formou-se uma enorme tromba d'água que atingiu as áreas povoadas.
A hipótese levantada pelos especialistas, e que precisa ser confirmada por estudos científicos mais avançados, também é consistente com imagens de satélite que mostram o colapso da geleira.
Esta região fronteiriça é especialmente vulnerável a desastres dessa natureza devido à sua geografia.
Trata-se de uma área acidentada, que abrange algumas das montanhas mais altas do mundo, geleiras, campos de neve e terrenos instáveis.
A enchente destruiu casas e estradas inteiras, deixando centenas de pessoas desabrigadas.
Por ser um destino turístico popular, vários estrangeiros estão entre as vítimas fatais.
A enchente repentina arrastou muitos corpos para distritos distantes rio abaixo, e a identificação e o resgate dos mortos podem representar um grande desafio.
Segundo a Cruz Vermelha, estima-se que cerca de 93 mil pessoas possam ter sido afetadas pelo desastre de quarta-feira.

items.title: Desastres como o do Nepal podem ser evitados? Perguntas e respostas sobre a tragédia que matou mais de 500 e deixou quase 2 mil desaparecidos
items.summary: Desastre poderia ter sido evitado? Qual foi a dimensão do ocorrido? Confira respostas sobre a tragédia iniciada na quarta-feira (26/8).
items.body_text:
Desastres como o do Nepal podem ser evitados? Perguntas e respostas sobre a tragédia que matou mais de 500 e deixou quase 2 mil desaparecidos
Deslizamentos de terra e enchentes repentinas de grandes proporções na fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete causaram danos generalizados, deixando ao menos 579 mortos e quase 2 mil desaparecidos.
Imagens do desastre ocorrido na quarta-feira (26/8) mostram uma onda de lama e pedras arrastando prédios, estradas e veículos enquanto pessoas fugiam dos destroços que avançavam rapidamente na região de Nuwakot.
Um vídeo mostra um fluxo massivo de água e lama descendo por um desfiladeiro ao longo do rio Trishuli e atingindo o posto fronteiriço de Rasuvagadhi, um complexo de vários andares.
Grandes inundações também foram relatadas nos rios Bhote Koshi e Narayani.
O Centro Internacional para o Desenvolvimento Integrado de Montanhas no Nepal alertou que inundações secundárias podem ocorrer nos próximos dias devido aos detritos que estão sendo levados pelos rios.
Esses temores fizeram com que os resgates fossem pausados temporariamente, mas os esforços já foram retomados na manhã desta sexta-feira (28/08).
Enquanto isso, autoridades e cientistas continuam estudando o que ocorreu e se preparando para eventuais desdobramentos daqui pra frente.
Resumimos aqui o que se sabe até o momento.
1. O que causou a avalanche?
O ministro das Relações Exteriores do Nepal afirmou inicialmente que um terremoto havia ocorrido na fronteira entre seu país e o Tibete pouco antes do deslizamento de terra, o que levou à especulação de que a atividade sísmica poderia ter desencadeado a tragédia.
O Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS, na sigla em inglês) também chegou a relatar que o evento de quarta-feira poderia ter sido um terremoto de magnitude 4,4.
No entanto, a agência americana confirmou posteriormente que o incidente "foi, na verdade, um colapso glacial e fluxo de detritos" que causaram "impactos catastróficos".
Sabe-se que as mudanças climáticas estão acelerando o derretimento glacial na região do Hindu Kush-Himalaia. Enquanto os esforços de resgate continuam, os cientistas estão tentando reconstruir com precisão a sequência de eventos.
Simon Cook, glaciologista e professor de Energia, Meio Ambiente e Segurança na Universidade de Dundee, afirmou que "as mudanças climáticas podem ter um impacto".
"O permafrost mantém parcialmente unidas algumas encostas de montanhas; esse permafrost está aquecendo, descongelando e se degradando, então mais deslizamentos de terra ocorrerão", explicou Cook à BBC.
Uma possibilidade é que a água da chuva ou do degelo tenha desestabilizado o terreno ou o próprio gelo, desencadeando uma reação em cadeia.
Os cientistas analisarão imagens de satélite para determinar exatamente onde ocorreu o deslizamento de terra, se algum lago glacial secou repentinamente e onde o rio pode ter sido bloqueado.
Eles também estudarão dados sobre as chuvas recentes.
2. É possível prevenir desastres como esse?
Especialistas apontam que desastres como deslizamentos de terra, avalanches e colapsos glaciais não podem ser completamente evitados, mas seus impactos podem ser reduzidos.
Cada vez mais, sistemas de alerta precoce estão sendo instalados em vales vulneráveis e ao redor de lagos glaciais. Esses sistemas podem monitorar mudanças nas condições ambientais e fornecer tempo valioso para evacuações.
Pesquisadores também afirmam que uma melhor cooperação transfronteiriça é essencial, já que muitos desses desastres se originam em áreas remotas do Tibete antes de afetar o Nepal.
"Se tivesse começado no Nepal, poderíamos ter visto daqui. Mas em incidentes como este, o sistema de compartilhamento de informações entre os países precisa ser fortalecido", explicou Basanta Raj Adhikari, especialista em desastres da Universidade Tribhuvan, no Nepal.
A longo prazo, cientistas dizem que reduzir a exposição ao risco pode ser a defesa mais eficaz.

items.title: Brasil cria 58,5 mil postos de trabalho em julho, aponta Caged
items.summary: Abertura de vagas caiu 56,3% na comparação com mesmo mês de 2025
items.body_text:
Economia
Brasil cria 58,5 mil postos de trabalho em julho, aponta Caged
Abertura de vagas caiu 56,3% na comparação com mesmo mês de 2025
Os dados divulgados pelo Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged), do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego, apontam que 58.568 postos de trabalho com carteira assinada foram abertos em julho. O indicador mede a diferença entre contratações e demissões.
O saldo é 57,3% menor em relação a junho, quando o país criou 137.044 empregos.
A criação de empregos caiu 56,3% em comparação a julho do ano passado, pressionada pelos juros altos e pela desaceleração da economia. No mesmo mês de 2025, tinham sido criados 133.932 postos de trabalho, nos dados com ajuste, que consideram declarações entregues em atraso pelos empregadores.
Em relação aos meses de julho desde 2020, esse é o resultado mais baixo da série. A mudança da metodologia no Caged impede a comparação com anos anteriores a 2020.
Acumulado
De janeiro a julho, o Caged registrou queda de 20,9% no acumulado de vagas formais:
- 972.203 (sete meses de 2026);
- 1.229.107 (sete meses de 2025).
Os dados trazem ajustes, quando o Ministério do Trabalho registra declarações entregues fora do prazo pelos empregadores e retifica os dados de meses anteriores.
Setores
Na divisão por ramos de atividade, quatro dos cinco setores pesquisados criaram empregos formais em julho.
- Serviços: +24.098 postos;
- Construção civil: +12.691;
- Agropecuária: +12.523;
- Indústria (de transformação, de extração e de outros tipos): +11.315
Um setor demitiu mais do que contratou em julho:
- Comércio: -8.114 postos
Tradicionalmente, o mês de julho é fraco para o comércio, principalmente para o varejo, que dispensou 3.674 pessoas a mais do que admitiu.
Destaques
Nos serviços, a criação de empregos foi puxada pelo segmento de transporte, armazenagem e correio, com a abertura de 18.150 postos formais. A categoria de saúde humana e serviços sociais abriu 12.235 vagas. O setor de educação, no entanto, fechou 7.352 postos.
Na construção civil, o destaque positivo ficou com o segmento de obras de infraestrutura, que abriu 7.087 empregos formais. Em segundo, vêm os serviços especializados para construção, com 4.253 postos.
Na indústria, o maior gerador de empregos foi a fabricação de produtos alimentícios, com 6.994 vagas, seguida por fabricação de veículos automotores, reboques e carrocerias (+3.440) e fabricação de máquinas, aparelhos e materiais elétricos (+1.950).
Regiões e estados
Quatro das cinco regiões registraram abertura de vagas formais em julho.
Veja abaixo o desempenho de cada região:
- Sudeste: +21.668 postos
- Nordeste: +18.973
- Centro-Oeste: +9.943
- Norte: +8.375
- Sul: -628
Na divisão por unidades da federação, 22 registraram saldo positivo e cinco demitiram mais do que contrataram. Os destaques na criação de empregos foram em São Paulo (+17.814), Mato Groso (+5.766) e Minas Gerais (+5.199).
As unidades da federação que eliminaram empregos formais em julho foram Espírito Santo (-2.605), Rio Grande do Sul (-903), Tocantins (-366), Santa Catarina (-248) e Distrito Federal (-134).
Segundo o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego, no Espírito Santo, as demissões decorrem do fim da safra de café. No Tocantins, estão relacionadas ao comércio e à agropecuária. No Rio Grande do Sul, concentraram-se na indústria do fumo e no comércio.
Carteira assinada
Com a criação de empregos formais, o número de trabalhadores com carteira assinada encerrou julho em 48.082.866, alta de 0,12% em relação a junho e de 1,02% em relação ao mesmo mês do ano passado.
Apoie o jornalismo que chama as coisas pelo nome
Muita gente esqueceu o que escreveu, disse ou defendeu. Nós não. O compromisso de CartaCapital com os princípios do bom jornalismo permanece o mesmo.
O combate à desigualdade nos importa. A denúncia das injustiças importa. Importa uma democracia digna do nome. Importa o apego à verdade factual e a honestidade.
Estamos aqui, há mais de 30 anos, porque nos importamos. Como nossos fiéi

items.title: Por um projeto nacional para o Brasil
items.summary: É hora de lutar pela reafirmação da democracia e pela defesa da soberania, escrevem Benedita da Silva, Elias Jabbour, José Dirceu e Manoel Severino
items.body_text:
Artigos
Por um projeto nacional para o Brasil
É hora de lutar pela reafirmação da democracia e pela defesa da soberania, escrevem Benedita da Silva, Elias Jabbour, José Dirceu e Manoel Severino
As eleições de 2026 não serão apenas mais um momento da história de nosso país. Tudo leva a crer que se tratará de um momento de definição histórica do Brasil, onde um projeto claramente de caráter antipopular e neocolonial afrontará um campo construído desde o início da redemocratização e liderado pelo presidente Lula. Democratas, nacionalistas, desenvolvimentistas, ambientalistas, movimentos sociais e populares estarão na linha de frente nesta batalha de caráter civilizatório.
Mirando além do horizonte, o momento é especial por outros motivos. Estaremos diante da luta pela reafirmação de nossa democracia duramente conquistada e implacavelmente atacada. O que faz a atual quadra histórica diferente também é o clima internacional marcado tanto pelo recrudescimento da violência estadunidense e pela cobiça aberta sobre nossos recursos naturais estratégicos quanto pela emergência de projetos nacionais autônomos que orbitam em torno de mecanismos como o BRICS+.
É nesse ambiente internacional que a reafirmação do papel do Estado na economia e o fortalecimento de blocos nacionais de capitais impõem ao Brasil, e às esquerdas em particular, elevar o nível da intervenção pública.
Isso significa que a já citada reafirmação democrática e a recuperação, consolidação e ampliação de direitos sociais estão intimamente relacionadas com o novo papel que devemos empreender: sermos a vanguarda de um projeto nacional de desenvolvimento que garanta a reafirmação do Brasil enquanto bloco de capital autônomo e pronto para propor a plena integração sul-americana.
Mais: criando as condições para retomar o elo perdido da industrialização em massa de nossa economia, reconstruir as infraestruturas que unificam nosso mercado nacional e, o mais importante, entregar futuro e esperança a partir da geração de empregos de qualidade, garantindo mobilidade social e destruindo os pilares subjetivos que permitem a existência da extrema-direita enquanto alternativa de poder no Brasil.
Esse desenvolvimento deverá ser, simultaneamente, soberano, socialmente inclusivo e ambientalmente sustentável, articulando crescimento econômico, redução das desigualdades e enfrentamento da crise climática.
Soberania e reindustrialização nacional
A reafirmação de nosso campo político, além da reeleição de Lula, passa por nossa capacidade de embalar a sociedade brasileira em torno da bandeira da soberania e de seu exercício através de um arrojado projeto nacional reindustrializante, inclusivo e verdadeiro portador de futuro. A reconstrução de nossas infraestruturas passa pela ampliação do Programa de Aceleração do Crescimento (PAC), acrescido de metas de conteúdo local, transferência de tecnologia, geração de empregos no país e fortalecimento das cadeias produtivas nacionais em cada empreendimento.
Em vez de abrir uma nova e complexa frente de disputa constitucional sobre a diferenciação entre capital nacional e estrangeiro, devemos concentrar esforços na criação de instrumentos concretos de compras públicas, financiamento, encomendas tecnológicas e proteção dos setores estratégicos, assegurando contrapartidas ao capital estrangeiro e ampliando a capacidade produtiva brasileira. Um país capaz de criar esperança e futuro para seus filhos não pode ter sua indústria de transformação em sua mínima histórica de 10,8%.
Precisamos enfrentar, de uma vez por todas, a necessidade de coordenar as políticas fiscais e monetárias com programas como a Nova Indústria Brasil. A taxa de investimentos em relação ao PIB no ano de 2024 foi de apenas 16,8%. Trata-se de um número que indica um país sob embargos, sanções ou mesmo fora do sistema financeiro internacional.
Alcançar o piso de 25% nesta variável é fundamental para darmos conta de demandas represadas e gerar empregos industriais e em serviços tecnológicos

items.body_text:
The Presidency has tackled former Vice President Atiku Abubakar over his pledge to “open the borders” if elected president, insisting that Nigeria’s land borders are already open.
The Presidency made this known in a statement on Friday by the Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communication, Sunday Dare, titled, “Atiku and the Borders: Nigerians Deserve Facts, Not Campaign Slogans.”
According to the Presidency, the Federal Government reopened most of the country’s land borders on March 14, 2024, and has not reversed the decision.
“The facts are straightforward: Nigeria’s land borders are already open,” the statement said.
“It is therefore difficult to understand which borders the former Vice President intends to ‘open’ when the borders are already open. On February 14, 2026, President Tinubu opened the Kamba borders in Kebbi State, with attendant economic and diplomatic gains.”
The Presidency said if Atiku was referring to relaxing existing border controls, Nigerians deserved an explanation of the specific controls he intended to remove and the safeguards his administration would put in place.
“If he means he would relax existing border controls, then Nigerians deserve to know precisely which controls he intends to remove, why he considers their removal necessary, and what safeguards his administration would deploy against terrorism, arms trafficking, smuggling, human trafficking, and other forms of transnational organised crime,” it said.
The statement stressed that opening borders did not mean removing security controls.
“This distinction is fundamental.
“But of course, Atiku is unhinged now, and he would say or announce anything to attract and deceive the politically gullible.
“An open border is not an uncontrolled border. Modern border management is designed to facilitate legitimate movement, trade and economic interaction while preventing criminals and terrorist organisations from exploiting the same channels. Effective border governance therefore requires a combination of immigration control, customs administration, intelligence-sharing, surveillance, technology and coordinated security operations.”
The Presidency said the issue was particularly important given Nigeria’s security environment and its links with developments across the Sahel and the Lake Chad Basin.
“This is particularly important for Nigeria because our northern security environment cannot be divorced from developments across the Sahel and the Lake Chad Basin.
“As Atiku rightly acknowledged, Nigeria shares borders with Niger, Chad, and Cameroon. While the region continues to confront terrorism, violent extremism and transnational organised crime have proven to be domestic disturbances that have found border porosity as a channel for their export to other countries.”
The Presidency cited the Global Terrorism Index 2026 in arguing for effective border management.
“The security reality is compelling. The Global Terrorism Index 2026 indicates that approximately 41 per cent of terrorist attacks occur within 50 kilometres of an international border, while about 64 per cent occur within 100 kilometres. Borderlands are particularly vulnerable where difficult terrain, limited state presence and weak coordination create opportunities for terrorist organisations to operate.”
It added, “The implications for Nigeria are obvious. As domestic insurgencies evolve into increasingly networked and transnational terrorist threats, effective border management becomes an indispensable component of national security. Terrorists and criminal networks exploit sovereign boundaries precisely because security forces cannot simply pursue them across international borders without appropriate cooperation and legal frameworks.”

items.body_text:
The Nigeria Football Federation has appointed Dr Ayo Abdulrahaman as the new Chief Operating Officer of the Nigeria Premier Football League as the 2026/27 season kicked off on Friday.
The appointment was announced by the NFF on Friday, the same day the new NPFL season opened with a headline fixture between Shooting Stars and newly promoted Inter Lagos at the Adamasingba Stadium, Ibadan.
The federation said Abdulrahaman’s appointment took immediate effect.
His appointment followed a directive issued by the NFF on Thursday, August 27, for all board members and chief executive officers of the various leagues, as well as chief operating officers who are not members of NFF staff, to vacate their positions.
The directive is part of the federation’s ongoing restructuring of its management and league administration.
The NFF also appointed Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme as its interim General Secretary on Thursday.
Ikpeme confirmed Abdulrahaman’s appointment, saying it was made in line with the federation’s directive.
Abdulrahaman will now oversee the operational administration of the NPFL as clubs begin their campaigns in the new season.
The opening-day fixture in Ibadan saw Shooting Stars face newly promoted Inter Lagos as the NPFL returned to action across the country.
The new season will see clubs compete for the league title, continental qualification places and survival as the campaign progresses.
The appointment comes a day after the NFF appointed Ikpeme as its interim General Secretary, following the directive for members of the federation’s management and secretariat affected by the restructuring to vacate their positions, PUNCH Online reports.

items.body_text:
Laying flowers and embracing, thousands of people gathered in Oslo on Friday to pay their respects to Norway’s King Harald, who died on Friday aged 89 after a reign of three and a half decades.
Harald’s 53-year-old son immediately succeeded him on the throne, announcing he would reign under the name King Haakon VIII.
Haakon takes over a monarchy long hailed for its modernity and modesty, but beset by a string of scandals in recent years.
A motor procession with King Harald’s casket left Oslo University Hospital on Friday evening, taking the late monarch on the 20-minute ride to the royal palace, televised images showed.
Members of the public braved the rainy weather to line the streets to catch a glimpse of the procession, which included the royal family.
King Haakon VIII had arrived at the palace just before lunch with his 22-year-old daughter Ingrid Alexandra — the new crown princess — to formally inform the government of his father’s death.
In a statement, Haakon thanked “the government and Norwegian people for their support and sympathy for the Royal Family at this time”.
“An era has ended. A new one begins. The king is dead. Long live the king,” Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said in a speech shortly after meeting the new monarch.
“We will remember King Harald for his love for his people, for his humour and warmth, and for his unwavering faith in us,” he said.
Store was later seen laying down flowers in front of the palace.
Norway’s parliament said the new monarch would take an oath of allegiance in its main chamber on September 1.
The government announced a period of national mourning until Harald’s funeral, the date of which is yet to be set.
A king of his time
Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, King Harald, had been in hospital in Oslo since August 17, suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells that leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
Store said Harald, who ascended to the throne in 1991, was “a king of his time and for his time”, noting that he accompanied Norway through decades of enormous change during which the country “grew richer, we became more numerous, and we became more diverse”.
Thousands of Norwegians massed outside the palace in Oslo as it began to rain. They laid down mountains of flowers, cards and red, white and blue national flags, and many hugged and held each other.
“He was the king of the people,” mourner Kristoffer Hamre told AFP.
The palace lowered its flag to half-mast after Harald’s death was announced, but raised it again after Haakon arrived for the meeting with the government.
Another flag on the royal balcony and those at other official buildings will remain at half-mast until after Harald’s burial.
Like many mourners, Vigdis Haug, 65, said she valued Harald’s ability to unify people.
“I think he has been such a down-to-earth king who has cared about all of us, and the words he always uses when he gives a speech are so wise and so valuable,” she told AFP.
Harald was widely seen as the embodiment of an open and tolerant Norway.
Many of those AFP spoke with pointed in particular to his speech after neo-Nazi Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 people in twin attacks on July 22, 2011, in Norway’s worst massacre since World War II.
“He was someone who always seemed to find the words that brought us together and gave us a sense of security,” Caroline Vagle, a reporter for magazine Se og Hor, told AFP.
Tributes poured in from leaders around the world, including those of France, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Jordan and Ukraine, as well as the royal houses of Europe.
Turbulent year
Harald faced mounting health problems in his final years, forcing him to scale back his official schedule.
But he ruled out abdicating, arguing that he took a lifelong oath before the Norwegian parliament.
The past year has been a turbulent one for the Norwegian royal family.

items.body_text:
WASHINGTON: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday warned that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of waters “rightfully allocated to it” under the Indus Waters Treaty would have “profound consequences for regional peace and security”.
The IWT has come under strain since India announced in 2025 that it was placing its treaty obligations in abeyance. The announcement followed an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation.
In his virtual address to a Washington seminar on “The Indus Waters Treaty: South Asian Security at the Crossroads”, he declared that Pakistan would strongly safeguard its “legitimate rights and interests” under the treaty and international law.
FM Dar said the 1960 agreement remained “valid, binding and fully operative” despite India’s unilateral decision in April 2025 to place it “in abeyance”.
“The treaty contains no provision permitting either party to unilaterally suspend or place it in abeyance,” he said, adding that neither country could, “through a unilateral political declaration, extinguish obligations solemnly undertaken under international law.”
FM Dar said the issue went beyond the bilateral relationship, arguing that it concerned “the sanctity of treaties” and “confidence in international law”.
“If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined,” he said.
He also stressed that geography made cooperation unavoidable, noting that “states cannot alter the direction in which rivers flow”.
“That is precisely why rules matter,” FM Dar said, urging the international community to preserve treaty-based water governance in South Asia.
The foreign minister further said the treaty had survived wars, military crises, diplomatic breakdowns and prolonged political tensions for more than six decades because both countries had understood that water on which “hundreds of millions of lives depend” was too fundamental to be subjected to fluctuations in political relations.
“Today, however, that principle faces its gravest challenge,” he said.
FM Dar said Pakistan’s position was clear and consistent and that treaty-based proceedings had continued despite India’s assertion of “abeyance”, reinforcing the principle that “unilateral action cannot displace an agreed legal framework”.
Pakistan has pursued arbitration over disputes concerning Indian hydroelectric projects on the Western Rivers, particularly Kishenganga and Ratle.
The Court of Arbitration at The Hague has continued proceedings, with earlier rulings addressing its jurisdiction and questions concerning the interpretation and application of the treaty.
The treaty allocates the three eastern rivers to India and the three western rivers, including the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, primarily to Pakistan, subject to specified Indian uses.
FM Dar said resorting to the Permanent Indus Commission, a neutral expert or a Court of Arbitration “is not an act of confrontation” but “the implementation of the very legal framework to which both countries agreed and are bound”.
“Pakistan has consistently sought to resolve differences through dialogue, diplomacy and the mechanisms provided under the Treaty,” he said.
He said the dispute was especially serious because Pakistan’s agriculture, food security, energy production, livelihoods and economic development depended heavily on the Indus River system.
“The Indus Basin is the lifeline of more than 250 million Pakistanis,” Dar said. “Water security for Pakistan is therefore inseparable from economic security, food security and, ultimately, national security.”

items.body_text:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs0.58 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.17 per litre.
Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs342.02 per litre while HSD will cost Rs371.44 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.
According to a Petroleum Division notification, the new prices will be applicable from Aug 29 to Aug 31.
The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.
The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.
Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.
The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.
The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.
Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.
Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.
Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.body_text:
Nepal’s disaster authority on Friday put the number of people missing after devastating floods at 1,924, two days after the disaster killed at least 579 people in the country.
The number of missing includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the rivers where a wall of water powered down on Wednesday morning, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
Rescue teams used heavy machinery to dig through mud and debris in Nepalese towns devastated by a flash flood two days ago, as hopes of finding survivors faded and officials worked to reduce the risk of further catastrophic flooding.
The flood ripped through villages and valleys, destroying power stations, roads and bridges along a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and is popular with trekkers and pilgrims.
Authorities in Nepal used helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands cut off in towns and valleys while emergency services, some using sniffer dogs, recovered dozens of bodies swept down into the plains.
Around 320 Indian nationals are still missing in the aftermath of the devastating flash flood, a spokesperson for India’s foreign ministry said, adding that at least 400 were stranded but safe on the Chinese side, while another 96 had crossed into Nepal by land.
Dibga Tamang was among the last people rescued from the hard-hit town of Rasuwa on Thursday, airlifted along with three others to an army camp in Nuwakot.
“All of our people have gone. They are dead,” Tamang said. “I have no one left waiting for me. Everything and everyone is gone. The end.”
The sheer amount of water and debris stirred up now risks triggering a further disaster.
Nepal’s disaster management authority warned that a lake formed by debris blocking the Bhotekoshi River was rising and at risk of bursting, while on the other side of the border China said that some three million cubic metres of water, the equivalent of about 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools, was expected to flow into an already dammed lake over the next three days.
There is a high risk the lake could breach, with peak flow expected around September 1, Chinese state media said, citing the water resources ministry.
Chinese authorities have mobilised an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys and 3D modelling of the barrier lake, but accessing it was challenging.
“After the glacier collapse created the lake, many isolated cliffs and steep cliffs appeared along it,” one of the engineers, Chen Hanxiao, told CCTV.
Chen said the general approach to reducing the lake’s threat is to excavate a drainage channel at a lower point of the dam, but the width and depth of that channel needed calculations based on how fast the water will flow and how quickly the lake will fill.
Their next tasks were to monitor the lake and collect data from the lake floor, as well as weather monitoring in the coming days.
Nepali Army working to rescue 100 trapped in hydropower tunnel
Nepali Army teams searched for more than 100 people trapped inside a hydropower tunnel, as India offered to send a specialised rescue team.
India has extensive experience with difficult Himalayan tunnel rescues, including specialised teams of “rat-hole” miners. However, the uncertainty was agonising for families waiting for news.
“I have not heard from him since I spoke to him at 7am that day. We have not had any news about them either, if they are being rescued or not,” Sita Adhikari, whose husband was trapped in the hydropower tunnel, told reporters.
“We will have hope as long as we have our breath… We need them to be rescued as soon as possible,” she said.
Two army helicopters were sent to the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in the mountainous Rasuwa district.

items.title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope to launch this weekend: What is its purpose?
items.summary: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope to launch this weekend: What is its purpose?The National Aeronautics and Space Administration is all set to launch one of its most powerful telescopes till date on Sunday, August 30, 2026. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will lift off...
items.body_text:
Published August 29, 2026
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is all set to launch one of its most powerful telescopes till date on Sunday, August 30, 2026.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will lift off aboard the SpaceX Falcon Heavy from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center at 7:26 a.m. EDT from Florida.
The telescope will take 90 days to travel 1 million miles from Earth before the Engineers could begin inspecting its instruments. So, the space enthusiasts expecting to see photos from Roman will have to wait until next year.
The new telescope will work differently from James Webb and Hubble Space Telescopes, which are already in space because it has Wide Field Instrument which helps it see an area of sky roughly 100 times larger than Hubble's, allowing it to survey huge sections of the universe much faster.
Scientists expect Roman to map billions of galaxies and help investigate some of the biggest questions in modern astronomy, including dark energy, dark matter and how the universe has changed over time.
It will also search for exoplanets, including worlds that are difficult to detect with other telescopes.
The telescope uses a 2.4-meter primary mirror originally designed for US spy satellites before it was given to NASA. The mirror is roughly the same size as Hubble's, but Roman is designed to cover a much wider patch of sky at once.
NASA expects the telescope's main mission to last at least five years.

items.title: SECP launches unified digital framework for faster investor onboarding
items.summary: A man uses a mobile phone as he takes a photo of the electronic board displaying share prices during a trading session at the Pakistan Stock Exchange, in Karachi on November 28, 2023. — ReutersThe Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan has introduced a unified digital...
items.body_text:
Published August 29, 2026
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has introduced a unified digital investor onboarding framework to make entry into Pakistan’s capital market faster and easier by reducing repetitive verification, simplifying documentation and setting clear timelines for opening investor accounts.
The framework particularly aims to facilitate first-time and digital investors, with Sehl/Sahulat accounts to be processed within one working day and Normal Accounts within two working days.
Applicants will receive tracking IDs, while any deficiencies will be communicated within the prescribed timeframe and reasons for rejection provided in writing, said a press release issued here on Friday.
The initiative is part of SECP’s broader drive to expand retail participation, particularly among young Pakistanis, and increase the country’s capital-market investor base to 2.5 million.
“Our focus is to remove entry barriers and use technology to make the investor journey simpler, faster and more accessible. The objective is to unlock the significant untapped potential of Pakistan’s capital market by broadening participation, particularly among the youth, and building a deeper and more inclusive market,” said SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu.
Issued through Circular No. 19 of 2026, the framework standardises onboarding requirements across securities brokers, asset management companies, insurers and other regulated intermediaries, creating a more consistent investor experience across the regulated financial sector.
A key feature is the elimination of repetitive customer verification. Where prescribed verification has already been completed by an eligible regulated financial institution or notified third party, intermediaries can rely on that verification instead of requiring the investor to repeat the process.
The framework also enables API-based straight-through processing and digital onboarding, including instant UIN issuance and opening of CDC sub-accounts, reducing paperwork and manual intervention.

items.title: Partial Lunar eclipse transforms the Moon into a “blood red” celestial display
items.summary: Partial Lunar eclipse transforms the Moon into a “blood red” celestial display
items.body_text:
Partial Lunar eclipse transforms the Moon into a "blood red" celestial display
- By Zaeem Basir -
- Aug 28, 2026
Stargazers across multiple continents were treated to a vivid astronomical event on August 28, 2026, as a partial lunar eclipse turned the moon a deep reddish-copper hue. The astronomical spectacle—often referred to as a “Blood Moon”—was visible across North and South America, Europe, Africa, and parts of Asia under clear night skies.
The phenomenon occurs when the Earth passes directly between the Sun and the Moon, casting its shadow across the lunar surface.
Why Does a Lunar Eclipse Turn the Moon Red?
Despite being classified as a partial lunar eclipse, the event delivered striking visual results due to atmospheric light filtering:
Rayleigh Scattering: Sunlight passing through Earth’s atmosphere loses shorter blue wavelengths while longer red and orange wavelengths bend toward the Moon.
Atmospheric Conditions: Dust and clouds within Earth’s atmosphere amplify the deep copper-red tone projected onto the lunar disk during peak shadow alignment.
Astronomers noted that night skies offered ideal viewing conditions in high-altitude and low-light regions, allowing astrophotographers to capture detailed imagery of the transition.
Global Viewing Highlights and Public Reaction
Observatories and amateur skywatchers turned out in large numbers to document the alignment. Unlike solar eclipses, lunar eclipses are safe to view directly without special protective eye equipment:
In the Americas, the best views came during the late evening when the Moon was fully covered in deep red.
Across Europe and Africa, the eclipse showed up in the early hours before dawn. Conditions were especially clear over Southern Europe and Northern Africa, giving sharp visibility.
For sky watchers, binoculars and backyard telescopes made it easy to catch the details, with the umbral shadow edge slowly creeping across the Moon’s craters.
Looking Ahead: Next Astronomical Events
Astronomers point out that while full total lunar eclipses are relatively rare, partial eclipses offer equally distinct visuals due to the high contrast between the shadowed and sunlit portions of the lunar surface. Skywatchers can anticipate further planetary conjunctions and meteor showers scheduled across the 2026 celestial calendar.

PIMS likely to face high-level inspection tomorrow: sources
- By Web Desk -
- Aug 28, 2026
ISLAMABAD, August 28, 2026: A high-level inspection team is likely to visit the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) tomorrow following the recent fire incident at the hospital, ARY News reported.
According to sources, the leaves of heads of clinical and non-clinical departments at PIMS have been cancelled.
The PIMS administration has been directed to ensure the attendance of all department heads during the inspection. Department heads have also been instructed to ensure the timely attendance of their subordinate staff.
The orders were issued by the Executive Director of PIMS.
The administration has also been directed to keep all relevant records and information available for the inspection.
Sources said the high-level inspection team will inspect clinical and non-clinical departments at PIMS and receive briefings from officials of different departments.
Earlier, contradictions emerged between the statements of the health minister and doctors regarding the fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital in Islamabad.
The minister said a spark fell from the air conditioner, while a gynaecologist said the spark came from a bundle of wires, not the AC.
Speaking on the programme The Reporters, Chairman of the Standing Committee on Health Mahesh Kumar said that when nurses were questioned, they appeared confused and it seemed they had been taught what answers to give.
He said reports of all three committees should be submitted within 48 hours so that the entire nation can see them. The Standing Committee will examine how much truth the reports contain, he added.
The Standing Committee on Health also visited PIMS hospital. Committee members demanded the resignations of Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal and the head of PIMS.
It may be recalled that 14 newborn babies were killed in a fire at the PIMS nursery the previous day, while an aunt managed to rescue one newborn.

items.title: Naqvi leads drive to make Islamabad encroachment-free
items.summary: The campaign aims to reclaim government land and properties from illegal occupation. The post Naqvi leads drive to make Islamabad encroachment-free appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Islamabad is making progress toward becoming an encroachment-free model capital as authorities continue a zero-tolerance operation against illegal encroachments under the leadership of Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi.
The campaign aims to reclaim government land and properties from illegal occupation, restore civic order and make Islamabad cleaner, greener, safer, more attractive, environmentally friendly and tourism-oriented.
Teams from the Capital Development Authority and Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad are conducting coordinated anti-encroachment operations under the leadership of CDA Chairman and Islamabad Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf and the supervision of MCI Chief Executive Officer and Deputy Director General Enforcement Dr Anam Fatima.
Authorities said the whole-of-government approach has strengthened coordination among relevant institutions, ensuring effective enforcement, monitoring and follow-up.
The zero-tolerance campaign targets illegal constructions, commercial extensions, roadside stalls and kiosks, encroachments on green belts and footpaths, occupation of government land, and unauthorized commercial use of residential properties.
Operations have been carried out in several areas, including Saidpur Village, Noorpur Shahan, Islamabad Expressway and Tarnol. Authorities said the operations have removed illegal structures and encroachments, reclaimed valuable government land and restored public passageways.
Anti-encroachment operations are also continuing in markets, residential sectors, service roads and green belts.
According to officials, thousands of kanals of government land, properties and commercial assets worth billions of rupees have been reclaimed during the campaign.
The removal of encroachments has also improved traffic flow, pedestrian access, green belts, parks and the overall urban environment.
The campaign has received public appreciation, with supporters describing the sustained and indiscriminate action as progress toward effective governance and equal enforcement of the law.
Officials and supporters have also used the term “Mohsin Speed” to describe the government’s focus on rapid and results-oriented governance.
Authorities said continued implementation of the campaign could further strengthen Islamabad’s position as a clean, green, safe, sustainable and attractive model capital.
More read, Naqvi’s bold remarks put governance under spotlight
The anti-encroachment drive is also being presented as a potential national model for good governance, protection of public land, equal enforcement of laws and balanced urban and rural development.

items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Trump administration has revoked former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami Mohammed Al Shakarchi’s US visa after she was put on an FBI terrorist blacklist. The US […] The post US revokes ex-Iraq finance minister’s visa after FBI adds her to terrorism watchlist appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
US revokes ex-Iraq finance minister’s visa after FBI adds her to terrorism watchlist
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Trump administration has revoked former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami Mohammed Al Shakarchi’s US visa after she was put on an FBI terrorist blacklist.
The US State Department announced the decision on Friday, stating Sami, Iraq’s finance minister from 2022 to July 2026, had her visa canceled after the FBI added her to its terrorist blacklist.
US authorities did not explain why they included her on the list.
Officials said that Sami had already departed the United States before his visa was canceled.
The action precludes her from returning on that visa.
The discovery comes weeks after Sami was implicated in a broader corruption probe in Iraq.
An Iraqi court summoned the former minister earlier this month, and she was allegedly put on a judicial wanted list as authorities probed charges against high political and government officials.
She was thought to be outside Iraq and had not been captured.
The summons is not a conviction, and Iraqi police have not shown Sami’s crime in court.
Her inclusion on the US terrorist blacklist is unrelated to the Iraqi corruption inquiry, and US officials have not publicly said if the two cases are related.
The action marks a significant shift in Washington’s approach to Sami.
Before becoming finance minister in 2022, she was named to the State Department’s International Women of Courage Award while working as Iraq’s deputy finance minister and budget director-general.
The department at the time recognized her as playing a key role in efforts to combat corruption in Iraq’s public finances.
At the 2022 award ceremony, then-Secretary of State Antony Blinken lauded Sami’s anti-corruption efforts, emphasizing her work exposing financial scams and defending public resources.
In October 2022, previous Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s cabinet appointed Sami as Finance Minister, and she served in that role until July of this year.
Her story has given the anti-corruption fight in Baghdad a worldwide dimension.
Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administration has started a series of investigations, arrests, and asset seizures aimed at former and current officials to recoup public monies and strengthen state control.
The State Department has not publicly explained the information behind the FBI watchlist decision or announced any criminal charges against Sami in the United States.
The FBI’s public Most Wanted Terrorists list should not be confused with the larger terrorist blacklist maintained by the US government; Sami is not included on the public Most Wanted Terrorists site.

items.title: Nepal floods trauma ‘enormous’: Red Cross
items.summary: The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster has left an "enormous" level of trauma, the Red Cross said Friday, with early estimates suggesting 93,000... The post Nepal floods trauma ‘enormous’: Red Cross appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Nepal floods trauma ‘enormous’: Red Cross
Geneva – The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster has left an “enormous” level of trauma, the Red Cross said Friday, with early estimates suggesting 93,000 people may have been affected.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), the world’s largest humanitarian network, fears the death toll from Wednesday’s disaster, already above 500, will continue to rise.
“Due to roads and bridges having been washed out and both cell coverage and electricity cuts, we have not yet been able to access some of the hardest-hit areas,” said David Fisher, the IFRC head of delegation for Nepal.
“The trauma of this event is enormous,” he told a Geneva press conference, speaking from Kathmandu.
“Thousands of homes have been destroyed or suffered significant damage. We believe that at least 93,000 people have been affected and in great need.”
Nepal’s Red Cross has begun providing emergency relief, including food, water, hygiene kits, mattresses and blankets.
The floods and landslides that struck Nepal and China’s autonomous Tibet region saw a tsunami-like wall of water bury homes, smash bridges and sweep away vehicles.
UN aid chief Tom Fletcher said on X that the United Nations was “moving at speed to save lives”.
Lila Pieters Yahia, the UN resident coordinator for Nepal, said drinking water was being airlifted into affected areas.
“The damage is just incredible,” she told the press conference, speaking from the field, adding that more than 40 bridges had been destroyed or badly damaged and “over 40 kilometres (25 miles) of road completely destroyed”.
She said search and rescue operations were the government priority.
– ‘Cascading hazards’ –
“We haven’t seen a mountain hazard event like this for a very, very long time,” Kamal Kishore, head of the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, told the press conference.
“It’s really immense and we are still coming to grips with the extent the damage.”
He said the disaster was still unfolding in an ecosystem where one disaster could trigger “a range of cascading hazards”.
The UN children’s agency UNICEF, said at least 14 children were confirmed dead.
“Sadly, we’re only seeing the beginning of this tragedy,” spokesman Ricardo Pires told reporters.
“For those who survived, the emergency is far from over. Children now face increased risks of disease, malnutrition, violence and exploitation, as well as the psychological impact of what they have experienced.”
He said 18 schools had been destroyed and another 20 damaged, with an estimated 10,000 children urgently needing support to continue their education.
The World Health Organization said eight health workers were missing and six health facilities had been damaged.
“The priority is to ensure continuity of health services,” WHO spokesman Tarik Jasarevic said.
He said the UN health agency had delivered surgical masks and gloves and body bags to Nepal.

UEFA’s legal move ‘massive escalation’ in bitter Infantino feud
Paris – UEFA’s intention to launch a legal suit accusing FIFA president Gianni Infantino of “criminal mismanagement” is a “massive escalation” of their feud, a former marketing director of the International Olympic Committee told AFP.
UEFA, European football’s governing body, has urged Infantino to resign over his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the World Cup.
On Thursday, UEFA withdrew “on a provisional basis” its threat to boycott FIFA tournaments, but not before dropping a bombshell by announcing it was “considering legal action arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by FIFA.”
“UEFA and other interested parties are preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement,” read the legal document drawn up by UEFA’s US-based lawyers and to be filed in a court in Florida.
For Michael Payne, former head of marketing at the IOC, this could prove to be devastating for Infantino.
“UEFA’s legal threat, going after Infantino and FIFA for ‘criminal mismanagement’ is a massive escalation — a move no member federation has ever undertaken against a governing body for over a century,” he told AFP.
“Discovery, if the papers are ever released, will not paint a pretty picture, and open up a whole new focus around Infantino’s leadership and governance — or lack of.”
Terrence Burns, who served as brand and marketing strategist for two successful World Cup host bids, said it could affect Infantino’s hopes of being re-elected to a fourth and final term in Rabat next March.
“I think the legal threat is the better weapon of the two,” he told AFP.
“A boycott hurts the players and the fans, and it could make Infantino look like the victim.
“Going the legal route does the opposite because it’s aimed at him personally, not at the game, and it keeps the story alive on a timetable FIFA cannot control.
“And that’s the real point!
“It could run through the November nomination deadline (November 18 for candidates to declare) and into the March vote.”
– ‘Civil war’ –
Infantino has stayed put despite the onslaught of criticism from UEFA and two fellow confederations including CONCACAF, whose Canadian president Victor Montagliani is viewed as the likeliest challenger.
Neither Payne nor Burns are surprised, with the former saying: “Infantino has no choice but to tough it out — he has nowhere else to go.”
Burns, who has played a pivotal role in five successful Olympic bid city campaigns, says Infantino has an invaluable weapon.
“I think time is on his side, not UEFA’s,” said the American.
“Every week this drags on is another week he’s the president, meeting heads of state, doing deals, handing out the things a president can hand out.”
Burns believes the 56-year-old Swiss incumbent seems to have the numbers to be re-elected.
“It’s 211 votes, not three confederations, and he’s spent 10 years building that base one federation at a time,” said Burns.
“Saudi Arabia, Argentina, Mexico, most of Africa, and much of the Gulf are already with him.
“I think he’ll fight to the last day because fighting is the only strategy.”
Payne, who is credited with overhauling the IOC’s brand and finances in two decades as marketing supremo, says Infantino should learn from history.
“There is a very real risk of civil war — does that mean break away — or non-stop pressure on Infantino, paralysing his leadership, until he has no choice to eventually resign, as (Sepp) Blatter was forced to after his re-election,” said the 68-year-old Irishman.
Burns is more circumspect about the divisions.
“I’d stop short of civil war,” he said.
“Nobody wants to break the World Cup — too much money is riding on it, for everyone.
“To me, it feels more like a family feud over who runs the business, but it’s real, and it won’t fix itself.”

items.body_text:
The technical staff of the Egyptian national team, led by head coach Hossam Hassan, has scheduled a friendly match against Tanzania on October 5 in Cairo. The fixture forms part of the Pharaohs’ broader preparation strategy for upcoming continental commitments, centered around the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).
The mid-autumn friendly follows Egypt’s opening fixtures in the qualifying campaign against Angola and South Sudan. Technical staff intend to leverage the international window to assess player fitness, evaluate tactical sharpness, and integrate fringe talent into the squad dynamic ahead of subsequent qualifying rounds, Pulse Mubasher reported.
Egypt’s preparatory camp is scheduled to assemble on September 17 to gear up for the opening double-header. The Pharaohs will host Angola at Cairo International Stadium on September 25 before traveling to Juba to take on South Sudan at Juba National Stadium on September 29. Managing staff view the away fixture in South Sudan as a crucial early test in their push to secure maximum points at the start of the qualifying process.
Following the September fixtures, Egypt will face Malawi in back-to-back qualifying legs in November 2026, before wrapping up their qualifying campaign in March 2027 with return matches against South Sudan and Angola.
The technical committee views the upcoming fixture against Tanzania as a vital calibration opportunity to finalize the core squad lineup and evaluate match readiness ahead of the tournament proper.

items.body_text:
The suspects involved in the armed kidnapping of a woman in Sheikh Zayed could face the death penalty if convicted, prominent Cassation and Supreme Constitutional Court attorney Amr Abdel Salam stated.
Abdel Salam explained that the legal framework governing the case falls under Article 290 of Egyptian Penal Code No. 58 of 1937, as amended by Law No. 5 of 2018. Under standard provisions, abduction through coercion or fraud carries a minimum rigorous imprisonment sentence of 10 years.
Escalating statutory penalties
The severity of the punishment increases based on specific aggravating circumstances:
Ransom demands: Abductions involving a ransom carry 15 to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment.
Targeting women or minors: If the victim is a woman or a child, the penalty automatically escalates to life imprisonment.
Compounded offenses: Capital punishment (the death penalty) applies if the abduction is linked with sexual assault or rape.
Abdel Salam stressed that final legal classifications and sentencing will depend entirely on the Public Prosecution’s ongoing investigation and evidence gathering.
He also commended law enforcement agencies for apprehending the suspects within 48 hours after video footage documenting the incident surfaced online, highlighting the Interior Ministry’s rapid response in maintaining public safety and deterrence.

items.body_text:
Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council          
        Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here.
Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.
US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.
Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.
Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.
Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.
In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.
Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment.
On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro.
Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.
Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.
RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.
Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.
And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations.
Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.

Once bitter enemies Amhara, Tigray reach understandings in fight against Ethiopian govt          
        In mid-August, the leader of the Amhara insurgency fighting to overthrow Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed made a surprising announcement.
The collection of armed Amhara movements fighting in the country’s northwest under the unified Fano umbrella would join an alliance of seven other anti-government groups across the country, Fano leader Zemene Kassie told the Swiss publication, Le Temps.
What makes the move surprising is that the alliance includes members of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), whom the Amhara forces that make up the Fano fought against during the 2020-2022 war.
In addition to the TPLF, the alliance includes forces from Gumuz, Oromo, the Berta people and Somalia, Zemene said.
At the national level, the fight between Ethiopian oppositional groups and the government comes against the backdrop of a struggle over the future of the country’s multinational federal system and state’s right to self-determination.
However, this tension has a larger regional dynamic given Ethiopia’s involvement in the war in Sudan and its expressed desire to secure access to the Red Sea either by diplomatic coup or by force.
While fighting between the Fano and the Ethiopian government has transformed much of the Amhara Region into an active war zone since late 2023, the beginning of August saw clashes between TPLF forces and the Ethiopian military that threatened to transform long standing simmering tensions between the groups into an active war.
An African Union diplomat based in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr at the time that any expansion of the fighting in Tigray would have an impact on the calculations of every regional actor because the borders linking Sudan, Ethiopia and Eritrea are no longer merely dividing lines between states. They now form part of an interconnected regional security system in which domestic wars and geopolitical interests overlap, the diplomat added, making any new outbreak of fighting in Tigray a potential factor in reshaping the security landscape of the entire East African region.
The government has responded to the early August clashes with increased military activity.
In a statement issued on Friday, the Tigray regional government warned the international community that the region is nearing “another catastrophic war.”
An economic and security blockade has escalated following clashes that broke out on August 1, the statement added, with air strikes and artillery shelling hitting civilian areas, causing casualties and destruction and disrupting cultural activities.
In an interview with Oromia Broadcasting Network on August 7, Abiy criticized the TPLF leadership, accusing it of clinging to outdated political methods and forging alliances that he said threaten stability.
TPLF deputy chair Amanuel Assefa pointed to a strike on August 20, when a drone hit a residential area in Mekelle, Tigray’s capital. Residents speaking to Mada Masr confirmed the strike and said several homes were damaged.
Medical sources at Mekelle’s Ayder Specialized Hospital said 13 people were brought in with injuries following the strike, including five women and children, with three in serious condition. The injured ranged in age from two to 60, the sources said.
Tigrayan authorities also said a second strike hit near Mekelle University, though there is no confirmed information on casualties or damage as of the time of publishing.
The strike on Mekelle came only days after another attack that Tigrayan authorities attributed to the Ethiopian military, where a drone struck a farmers’ training center in the Dandera village, about 15 km from Mekelle, on August 18.
While the government hit Tigray, Fano forces continued to secure strategic wins against the Ethiopian military.
