items.title: Caldo record e sabbia del Sahara sull’Italia: il fenomeno sempre più diffuso
items.summary: La quinta ondata di calore dell’estate 2026 porta sulla Penisola una vasta nube di pulviscolo desertico
items.body_text:
Caldo record e sabbia del Sahara sull’Italia: il fenomeno sempre più diffuso
La quinta ondata di calore dell’estate 2026 porta sulla Penisola una vasta nube di pulviscolo desertico
2' di lettura
2' di lettura
Una vasta nube di polvere sahariana ha raggiunto l’Italia accompagnando l’ennesima ondata di caldo estremo dell’estate 2026. Dalle isole maggiori al Nord, il pulviscolo proveniente dal Nord Africa ha reso il cielo lattiginoso, con sfumature giallastre e una riduzione della visibilità, in coincidenza con temperature che in alcune aree del Mezzogiorno hanno superato i 40 gradi.
Chiedilo al Sole
Secondo le previsioni meteorologiche, il trasporto di sabbia e polveri desertiche è stato particolarmente intenso tra il 27 e il 28 agosto, quando le correnti meridionali associate all’anticiclone africano hanno sospinto verso il Mediterraneo enormi quantità di aerosol minerali. Le concentrazioni più elevate hanno interessato inizialmente Sardegna e regioni meridionali, per poi estendersi al Centro-Nord, coinvolgendo l’intera penisola.
Il fenomeno non è nuovo, ma la sua portata e la sua frequenza stanno attirando crescente attenzione da parte della comunità scientifica. Le intrusioni di polvere sahariana rappresentano infatti una componente naturale del sistema climatico mediterraneo: ogni anno milioni di tonnellate di sabbia vengono sollevate dai deserti nordafricani e trasportate dai venti verso l’Europa. Tuttavia, l’aumento delle ondate di calore e la maggiore persistenza delle configurazioni atmosferiche che favoriscono la risalita di masse d’aria subtropicali sembrano contribuire a rendere questi episodi più frequenti e più intensi.
Gli effetti sono immediatamente visibili. Il cielo perde la sua tipica limpidezza estiva e assume una colorazione opaca, talvolta tendente al giallo o al marrone. Le polveri in sospensione diffondono la luce solare e possono determinare tramonti particolarmente intensi e scenografici. In presenza di precipitazioni, inoltre, il pulviscolo si deposita al suolo dando origine al fenomeno della cosiddetta “pioggia rossa”, che lascia evidenti tracce su automobili, finestre e superfici esposte.
L’impatto non riguarda soltanto il paesaggio. Le polveri desertiche contribuiscono ad aumentare le concentrazioni di particolato atmosferico, in particolare PM10, con possibili conseguenze per la qualità dell’aria. Diversi studi hanno evidenziato come gli episodi di trasporto sahariano possano determinare superamenti delle soglie di particolato monitorate dalle agenzie ambientali, soprattutto nelle regioni meridionali e insulari.

items.title: España
items.summary: Destaca la colaboración "esencial" de Rabat para frenar la crisis y defiende que es "indispensable" el diálogo que se tiene
items.body_text:
El ministro de Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, salva de responsabilidad alguna a Marruecos en la entrada masiva de unos 72.000 inmigrantes en Ceuta y centra toda la culpa de la crisis en la "viralización inédita de mentiras y bulos" en las redes sociales, que sería la única causa del episodio que sucedió el pasado 30 de julio en la ciudad autónoma.
El Gobierno insiste, pues, en el relato exculpatorio de Marruecos ante el Congreso a pesar de que hasta una parte de Sumar y sus socios parlamentarios le están recriminando que se está manteniendo una posición de "debilidad" por no "llamar a las cosas por su nombre".
Lejos de ir por ese camino, la comparecencia extraordinaria de Albares en la Comisión de Exteriores del Congreso ha ensalzado la cooperación de Marruecos y su papel "esencial" para "frenar la crisis" y para "prevenir una situación similar en el futuro".
Así, ha recalcado que fruto del diálogo entre países se pudo "facilitar" el retorno de un 90% de los inmigrantes que entraron el día 30 de julio en menos de 48 horas y ahora "gestionar" el regreso de aquéllos que aún permanecen en la ciudad. También que permitió que no se produjera otra entrada masiva el 15 de agosto en Ceuta a pesar de los llamamientos que había en redes sociales para volver a repetirlo.
Por todo ello, Albares ha subrayado que el "diálogo diplomático" con Marruecos "es indispensable, dado que es nuestro vecino al otro lado de la frontera de Ceuta y Melilla, ante situaciones como ésta, en las que la respuesta pasa necesariamente por la diplomacia". Esta afirmación llega cuando hay grupos políticos que reclaman una revisión de las relaciones diplomáticas con Marruecos, algo que el ministro no contempla lo más mínimo.
¿Entonces hubo un "ataque híbrido" de Marruecos? Albares ni siquiera ha pronunciado esas palabras ni mucho menos ha deslizado que Rabat pudiera estar detrás. Al contrario, ni el más mínimo reproche, sólo alabanzas por su ayuda.
De este modo, el ministro de Exteriores ha descargado toda la culpa en la viralización de "mentiras y bulos" a través de las redes sociales sobre las consecuencias de una sentencia del Tribunal Supremo acerca de las entradas por mar. "La desinformación en las redes sociales que han sido el detonante inmediato de esta crisis al deformar una sentencia del Tribunal Supremo y ha sido también el vehículo que condujo a miles de personas a lanzarse sobre Ceuta con noticias falsas", ha explicado.
"Como en otros momentos críticos en otras partes del mundo, las plataformas han sido el canal inflamable por el que se han propagado mentiras a una escala global y a una velocidad sin precedentes", ha proseguido.
En un repaso cronológico, Albares ha dado datos de esa viralización. De cómo el vídeo de dos mujeres jóvenes cruzando a nado alcanzó una difusión muy destacada el 28 de julio. Algo que propició que prensa e influencers marroquíes se hicieran eco y multiplicaran la difusión hasta desatar un impacto de 30 millones de personas, especialmente en Marruecos. Eso hizo que entre el 28 y el 30 de julio, se extendiera de manera "explosiva" el bulo de que las fronteras estaban abiertas y que no se expulsaría a quienes entrasen por mar. En todo este relato de los hechos, Albares no ha mencionado en ningún que Marruecos hubiera haber intervenido de alguna manera para extender esas "noticias falsas". Ni siquiera que se sospecha.
Recriminado por los grupos por la actitud que mantienen el Gobierno respecto al papel que pudo desempeñar Marruecos, Albares se ha revuelto. "Yo no soy el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Marruecos. Soy de España, el que tiene que hablar con Marruecos en beneficio de Ceuta y de Melilla".
"Yo soy exclusivamente el amigo de España y de los españoles, y hablo con quien tenga que hablar en beneficio de los intereses de España. items.title: España
items.summary: El Ministerio del Interior ha solicitado formalmente a la Comisión Europea el despliegue de agentes de Frontex, Europol y la agencia de asilo (EUAA) para acelerar el triaje y la tramitación de expedientes de los migrantes en Ceuta
items.body_text:
El Gobierno ha pedido a la Comisión Europea el apoyo de la Agencia Europea de Fronteras y Costas (Frontex) y de Europol para las labores de triaje de los migrantes que quedan en Ceuta tras la entrada masiva del 30 y 31 de julio.
El ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, ha enviado una carta a la directora general de Migración y Asuntos Internos de la Comisión, Beate Gminder, en respuesta a la oferta que esta hizo al embajador de España ante la Unión Europea para que distintas agencias comunitarias ayudasen en la crisis.
Marlaska ha solicitado el refuerzo por parte de Frontex, Europol y la Agencia de la Unión Europea para el Asilo (EUAA) del dispositivo puesto en marcha para gestionar el triaje y tramitar los expedientes de las personas que todavía permanecen en Ceuta de manera irregular.
Además, en el caso de Frontex, Interior ha solicitado extender la duración de la operación Minerva, que cubre los puertos de Algeciras, Tarifa y Ceuta durante la operación Paso del Estrecho, más allá del 2 de septiembre, tanto como sea posible.
Más agentes de Frontex y colaboración para las entrevistas
El Gobierno ha pedido 10 agentes adicionales de Frontex para el triaje, con el objetivo de agilizar la recogida de información de los migrantes que aún no han sido sometidos a ese procedimiento.
Considera asimismo de gran utilidad la asistencia de la EUAA en la realización de entrevistas y la puesta a disposición de intérpretes, si bien el trabajo de estos profesionales podría realizarse de forma telemática debido a la falta de espacio en la ciudad.
Tras concluir el triaje y, en su caso, el procedimiento de asilo en frontera, Interior concretará la asistencia de Frontex necesaria para ejecutar determinados retornos a través de los mecanismos de mediación y acuerdos bilaterales que la agencia mantiene con distintos países de origen.
Marlaska ha recordado a la Comisión Europea que España solicitó el 24 de agosto una ayuda de emergencia superior a los 32 millones de euros con cargo a los fondos FAMI (Fondo de Asilo, Migración e Integración) y al IGFV (Instrumento de Gestión de Fronteras y Visados), y confía en su «pronta resolución».
El ministro también ha pedido que el buque oceánico Duque de Ahumada de la Guardia Civil, que opera seis meses al año a las órdenes de Frontex, permanezca en aguas españolas durante 2027.
Por último, la carta demanda mantener el sistema EUROSUR Fusion Services, operado por Frontex, que proporciona imágenes satelitales de la frontera con Marruecos para vigilar zonas marítimas, puertos, costas y áreas prefronterizas estratégicas.
Respecto a Europol, el ministro aboga por profundizar la cooperación con las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad del Estado, especialmente en la investigación de redes de tráfico de personas y el análisis estratégico.
Podemos exige "protección y acogida" a los migrantes
Las eurodiputadas de Podemos, Irene Montero e Isa Serra, han solicitado mediante una carta la actuación "urgente" de la Comisión Europea ante la crisis en Ceuta, denunciando los "ataques racistas" contra migrantes y la "negligente" gestión del Gobierno de España, al que acusan de una "dejación de sus obligaciones" de protección y acogida. Ante esto, han reclamado a la institución comunitaria que realice un seguimiento específico para asegurar que la respuesta española sea plenamente compatible con el Derecho de la Unión y los derechos humanos.
Asimismo, han alertado sobre el "clima de hostilidad y odio" promovido por grupos de extrema derecha, ejemplificado en el bloqueo al convoy de la Cruz Roja y los altercados en la playa de Benítez, además de informar sobre el registro de 16 agresiones sexuales. Por ello, han pedido proteger a las organizaciones y activistas sobre el terreno, reforzar de inmediato la prevención frente a la violencia sexual y la trata, e investigar la responsabilidad de Marruecos y su posible complicidad con Estados Unidos e Israel.

items.title: Crisis migratoria
items.summary: La pena privativa de libertad ha sido sustituida por la expulsión del territorio nacional, con la prohibición de regresar a España durante cinco años
items.body_text:
- Crisis migratoria Doce migrantes detenidos tras asaltar con piedras un vehículo del Ejército y herir a cuatro militares en Ceuta
El Juzgado de lo Penal de Ceuta ha acordado la expulsión de España de once ciudadanos marroquíes detenidos por su implicación en el ataque sufrido este jueves por una patrulla militar del Grupo de Regulares en la zona de Benzú, después de que aceptaran una condena de dos años de prisión por un delito de atentado contra agentes de la autoridad.
Según la sentencia dictada este viernes tras alcanzarse un acuerdo entre la Fiscalía y las defensas, la pena privativa de libertad ha sido sustituida por la expulsión del territorio nacional, con la prohibición de regresar a España durante cinco años.
Los once condenados reconocieron su participación en los hechos y mostraron su conformidad con la pena propuesta por el Ministerio Público, lo que permitió la celebración de una vista de conformidad y evitó la celebración del juicio.
De acuerdo con los hechos recogidos en la resolución judicial, los acusados formaban parte de un grupo de migrantes irregulares que se encontraba en las inmediaciones de Benzú y que presuntamente había preparado una acción contra los vehículos que transitaran por la zona. Finalmente, el objetivo del ataque fue una patrulla militar de Regulares.
Durante la agresión fueron lanzadas piedras contra el vehículo en el que viajaban los militares, un incidente que se saldó con cuatro efectivos heridos de diversa consideración. Tras los hechos, las fuerzas de seguridad desplegaron un operativo que culminó con la detención de doce personas.
La situación procesal del duodécimo arrestado difiere de la del resto de implicados. El acusado rechazó el acuerdo planteado por la Fiscalía y negó haber participado en la agresión.
Durante su comparecencia judicial aseguró que se encontraba durmiendo en el momento en que se produjo la intervención policial y desvinculó completamente su presencia en la zona de los hechos investigados.
Ante la falta de conformidad con la acusación, el juez acordó mantener su ingreso en prisión provisional mientras continúa la tramitación del procedimiento penal y se fija la fecha para la celebración del juicio correspondiente.

El Sevilla FC negocia con el Leipzig por Conrad Harder
El delantero no tendría sitio tras el fichaje de Marc Guiu por el conjunto alemán
El Sevilla FC ya se ha decidido por un delantero para completar su nóminas de arietes. Se trata de Conrad Harder, el futbolista noruego del Leipzig que acaba de quedarse sin sitio en su equipo tras el fichaje de Marc Guiu ... por el conjunto alemán. Se da la circunstancia de que el delantero catalán también estuvo entre las opciones del Sevilla para su delantera. Sin embargo la operación era económicamente viable, aunque el jugador estaba por la labor de bajarse el sueldo, seguía siendo insuficiente para que el Sevilla pudiera hacerle un hueco en la plantilla.
Ahora, aunque también ha tanteado al serbio Ratkov, a José Ignacio Navarro le gusta más la opción de Harder. Las negociaciones están abiertas dese hace unos días, tal y como ha adelantado El Chiringuito. Según ha podido conocer este medio, el Sevilla se encuentra muy bien posicionado para hacerse con la cesión de este delantero, por el que el Leipzig abonó unos 24 millones de euros. Se confía en que la operación se cierre pronto y, al fin, se cierre el apartado del tercer delantero.
Esta incorporación era una de las exigencias prioritarias de Luis García Plaza. Si bien a José Ignacio Navarro le ha costado dar con un perfil interesante, que encaje con las posibilidades económicas sevillistas. El club tiene unos dos millones de euros de límite, que estaba destinado para el ariete ansiado. Se seguirá liberando con la salida de Vargas y alguna otra más que pueda concretarse de aquí al martes, pero la dirección deportiva ha querido zanjar ya este tema y se confía en que el acuerdo con el Leipzig llegue pronto.
Varias intentonas frustradas
El Sevilla estuvo muy cerca de tener a George Ilenikhena cerrado como cedido, pero los problemas financieros del Al-Ittihad bloquearon la operación. Era el perfil que más convencía a Luis García Plaza, puesto que complementaba a Robbie Ure, por el que el club ha pagado más de seis millones de euros. El Sevilla ha mantenido ciertas esperanzas en torno al posible desbloqueo de la situación del franco-nigeriano, pero el final del mercado acecha y había que mover ficha, más aún tras el rapapolvo de García Plaza hoy en rueda de prensa.
El Sevilla ha tanteado los nombres de Guiu y de Ratkov. El primero, demasiado caro, y el segundo no terminaba de convencer ni al entrenador ni al director deportivo. Hace unos días, el Sevilla preguntó por la situación de Conrad Harder, al que el Leipzig le está buscando una salida en este mercado, bien fuera como cesión o traspaso. Ante la imposibilidad de vender al delantero por un precio cercano a lo que costó, el préstamo es la vía más fácil y José Ignacio Navarro quiere cerrarlo lo antes posible.

Cómo seguir el Sevilla FC - Atlético de Madrid

Todo lo que hay que saber del Sevilla FC - Atlético de Madrid
Inesperado, por positivo, ha resultado el comienzo de temporada del Sevilla, que ha enlazado un par de victorias en esta apertura del Campeonato aun con la plantilla en construcción, cogida con alfileres y con varias posiciones pendientes de movimientos en esta recta final del mercado. «Estos seis puntos ya no nos los quita nadie», comentaba García Plaza al término del choque en Bilbao, donde el Sevilla gozó de superioridad numérica muy pronto, tras la expulsión de Yuri, se adelantó de inmediato y puso tierra de por medio en el segundo tiempo con un par de goles más que encarrilaron el triunfo. items.title: The Strait of Hormuz after six months of war: Blockades, drones and the shadow fleet
items.summary: Attacks on commercial vessels continue in the strategic waterway as Iran and Oman finalize negotiations over a new shipping route
items.body_text:
The Strait of Hormuz after six months of war: Blockades, drones and the shadow fleet
Attacks on commercial vessels continue in the strategic waterway as Iran and Oman finalize negotiations over a new shipping route
Six months have passed since U.S. President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began launching missiles at Iran, a conflict that has disrupted some of the world’s main trade routes, particularly the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, 20% of the hydrocarbons and fertilizers consumed globally reached international markets through the strategic waterway. Half a year later, despite negotiations and agreements, traffic is far from returning to normal.
But the crucial passage is not fully closed, contrary to what both the United States and Iran claim with their respective blockades: using tactics associated with the so-called shadow fleet, shipping companies on both sides are risking vessels and crews to keep trade flowing.
“We are essentially at a stalemate. There is no clear military, political or diplomatic solution in sight, and I don’t think anyone can say with certainty how traffic in the Strait of Hormuz will return to normal,” says Dimitris Maniatis, chief advisor at consultancy Marisks, in comments to EL PAÍS. “Traffic can rise or fall from one week to the next, but volumes remain well below usual levels. We have moved from an acute crisis to a prolonged period of risk. As a result, the shipping sector has begun adapting to the crisis rather than waiting for it to end.”
Before the war, an average of 130 ships passed through these waters each day in either direction. Today, that figure has fallen to fewer than 20 vessels a day. After the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June, there were a few weeks when traffic climbed above 60 vessels a day, raising hopes of a swift recovery in trade. But after Trump declared the ceasefire effectively over in early July following an Iranian attack on several ships, the situation returned to crisis levels.
Iran has tightened its blockade at the narrowest point of the Strait of Hormuz and periodically launches projectiles or naval drones at some of the vessels that venture through those waters without seeking permission from the Revolutionary Guard. The United States, for its part, has reimposed its blockade in the Gulf of Oman and is attempting to stop all ships bound for, or departing from, Iranian ports.
The shadow fleet
To bypass both blockades, shipping companies are effectively forcing their vessels to go dark. They do so by switching off the transponders that transmit their location to the Automatic Identification System (AIS), or by falsifying those signals, practices prohibited under international maritime regulations except in cases of extreme danger, such as sailing through pirate-infested waters.
It is a tactic that Western countries have long accused nations such as Russia and Iran of using to conceal shipments and evade sanctions, but one that is now also being employed by European and Gulf shipping operators to bypass Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by navigating through Omani territorial waters along a route protected by the U.S. Navy.
For example, maritime intelligence company Windward detected that last Tuesday six oil tankers entered the Persian Gulf and another departed for the Indian Ocean using the route through Omani waters. All seven vessels did so with their AIS systems switched off.
These tankers are part of a new strategy Arab countries are using to export their production. Large crude carriers pass through the Strait of Hormuz and then transfer their cargo to vessels anchored off the ports of Fujairah and Sohar, in the Gulf of Oman. On August 25 alone, the tracking platform TankerTrackers.com recorded 15 ship-to-ship transfers involving roughly 25 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products originating from countries along the southern and western shores of the Persian Gulf.

items.title: In the US, ICE arrests at school bus stops spark fear as students return to class
items.summary: Worries about immigration raids are contributing to a decline in Hispanic student enrollment

In the US, ICE arrests at school bus stops spark fear as students return to class
Worries about immigration raids are contributing to a decline in Hispanic student enrollment
This Tuesday, the biggest event in the city of Danbury, Connecticut, was the start of the new school year, much as it was in other states across the country. But this year, the excitement that back-to-school season usually brings for children and families was overshadowed in migrant communities by the fear of ending the day in a detention center. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) chose the symbolic date to ramp up its operations, turning school bus stops into traps.
This morning in Danbury, ICE was arresting parents at school bus stops.
But it’s more sinister. ICE waited until the kids were on the bus so when they are dropped off at the end of the day, they are alone, scared to death they can’t find their parents.
I’m heading to Danbury.
“This morning in Danbury, ICE was arresting parents at school bus stops. But it’s more sinister. ICE waited until the kids were on the bus so when they are dropped off at the end of the day, they are alone, scared to death they can’t find their parents,” said Democratic Senator from Connecticut Chris Murphy in a post on his social media.
Dozens of people were detained this week by immigration agents in Danbury and, although the operations were not limited to parents of schoolchildren, the first day of the school year was marked by fears of arrest.
Danbury Mayor Roberto Alves, who is the son of undocumented immigrants, posted a video and statement offering guidance on residents’ rights and lamenting that “on a morning that should be filled with backpacks, school buses, nervous smiles and excitement, no child should carry that kind of fear.”
Alves underscored the gravity of the situation: “There are kids who are going to come home from school and there is going to be a parent missing. These folks need our help,” he said.
Videos of some of the arrests in Danbury, showing the heavy-handed tactics of immigration agents, have circulated on social media, spreading fear throughout the migrant community.
ICE, the agency at the forefront of U.S. President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign, has consistently denied carrying out operations at schools. But images from the past school year showing agents arresting parents as they dropped off their children and detaining students near school grounds have left a lasting impact on many families, some of whom would rather have their children leave school than risk being detained.
Alves said ICE appeared to be using racial profiling during the Danbury raids, stopping people who looked as though they were of Central or South American origin.
In Maryland, where Hispanic students account for more than 23% of K-12 enrollment, the number of Hispanic students has fallen for the first time. The decline breaks a years-long trend of steady growth, with enrollment having risen from 182,000 students in the 2020-21 school year to 211,000 last year. This year, enrollment has dropped to 209,500.
In Montgomery County, where Hispanic students make up the largest demographic group, accounting for more than 35% of enrollment, Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) issued a statement acknowledging that “recent federal immigration enforcement actions, locally and across the country, have caused anxiety for many members of our community.” Enrollment in MCPS exceeded 159,000 students last school year, but this year’s projections suggest a total of only “more than 150,000.”
Beyond fears of encountering immigration officers on the way to school, many parents worry that the information provided when enrolling their children could end up in the hands of immigration authorities. MCPS has sought to address those concerns, stating that “Montgomery County Public Schools does not ask about immigration status at enrollment or at any other time. items.title: The women standing by Lindsay Clancy: ‘We need to understand what drove her to kill her children. It cannot happen again’
items.summary: The pink-dressed supporters, who have protested at the Massachusetts trial, say doctors failed to provide adequate treatment despite the mother’s severe mental health struggles
items.body_text:
The women standing by Lindsay Clancy: ‘We need to understand what drove her to kill her children. It cannot happen again’
The pink-dressed supporters, who have protested at the Massachusetts trial, say doctors failed to provide adequate treatment despite the mother’s severe mental health struggles
Jeanne, Marta, Rebeca and Ariana. Four women from four different generations, with different outlooks on life and from different parts of the United States. But they all have one thing in common: the story of Lindsay Clancy, the nurse who strangled her three children on January 24, 2023, before attempting to take her own life, has shattered them. They want to show their support for a woman who, they say, was not only a killer but also a victim of a medical system that did not know how to treat her. That is why they are urging the jury to find her not criminally responsible for the tragedy and to commit her to a psychiatric facility, where she can recover, rather than send her to prison for the rest of her life.
Jeanne Diachun worked as a nurse in Plymouth for 35 years. When she first heard about the Lindsay Clancy case, she was horrified that a woman with three children, a fellow nurse from her own state, could commit such an atrocity. “At first I thought, as anyone would, that she had done something horrible. I can’t even imagine someone doing that. But the more I learned about the case, the more I saw that she had sought help everywhere. And no one knew how to respond,” says the 81-year-old, who was in the courtroom on Tuesday for what is expected to be the final week of the trial. The defense and the prosecution delivered their closing arguments on Thursday. All that remains now is for the jury to decide whether to convict or acquit the defendant.
There is something in Clancy’s story that made Diachun think of her own family. “I remembered the day when, when my sisters and I were little, my mother started to scream out the window. I was only four years old. I don’t know exactly what happened to her, but they took her away and she was admitted to a hospital for three months. This case has made me relive my own story,” she says shortly before the hearing begins. “This is all tragic. There are no winners here,” she adds, referring to those trying to score points from the drama.
Ariana Anthony was born 65 years after Diachun. But the generational gulf between them does not prevent them from seeing the case in much the same way. The 16-year-old student stands alone outside Plymouth Superior Court dressed in pink and holding a sign calling for justice for Cora, Dawson and Callan, the three children strangled by their mother with exercise bands in the basement of their home in Duxbury, a 15-minute drive away.
The final days of the trial did not see a repeat of the images that had spread around the world: dozens, sometimes hundreds, of women dressed in pink in support of Clancy, often drawing fierce criticism. Anthony is well aware of the backlash: “I’ve been insulted too, called a clown, but I don’t care. I’m here because I believe we all must learn a lesson from this. And that something like this cannot happen again.”
Health experts have expressed hope that the tragedy will at least help shine a light on shortcomings in the treatment of mental health conditions. Terms such as psychosis and postpartum depression have moved from being almost taboo subjects to appearing in headlines, newspaper articles and television programs.
Glorifying a killer?
The wave of support from women has sparked criticism from many who believe it is glorifying a killer. items.title: MPs demand broadcaster be taken off of the air after panelists praised Adolf Hitler

items.body_text:
MPs demand broadcaster be taken off of the air after panelists praised Adolf Hitler
A large majority of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of Dutch parliament, is urging culture minister Rianne Letscher to take decisive action, including potentially revoking the broadcasting license of far-right broadcaster Ongehoord Nederland (ON!) after the company praised Hitler in one of its panel shows, RTL Nieuws reports.
Pressure has mounted in the last week after the incident occurred on the online panel show Let’s Twist Again. MPs and critics have accused the segment of normalizing and justifying Nazi ideology by portraying Adolf Hitler as an “anti-globalist crusader.”A public petition demanding the removal of Ongehoord Nederland quickly garnered over 20,000 signatures.
MPs from a wide range of parties, including PRO, D66 and CDA, have condemned the broadcast. They declared that the political patience with the broadcaster has completely run out. Parliament wants ON! permanently removed from the Dutch broadcasting system. The Tweede Kamer has officially scheduled a parliamentary debate on the future of ON! for September 24.
Letschert has said that she is actively exploring all legal options to intervene. She openly discussed the possibility of stripping ON! of its broadcasting license but warned that doing so requires strict, legally airtight criteria.
Letschert emphasized that she cannot simply ban the broadcaster by decree, as a judge would immediately overturn an arbitrary decision. ON! must be proven to have systematically violated the Media Act and journalistic standards.
ON! was also in hot water a few months earlier. In June, ten fellow public broadcasters sent a joint letter to Letschert refusing to cooperate with ON! due to repeated violations of the journalistic code of conduct.
While the overarching NPO organization acknowledged that ON! regularly breaks the Code of Journalistic Conduct, the NPO stated it lacks the legal mandate to issue sanctions or formally request the minister to expel them. This kicked the responsibility back to Letschert and parliament.

Over 170 students, teachers at Breda University fall ill due to suspected food poisoning
Around 175 students and teachers at Breda University of Applied Sciences (BUas) have become sick during an orientation week at a campsite in Poppel, Belgium. The university said that there is a high chance that it was caused by a “large outbreak of food poisoning.”
Over 800 students took part in the orientation. After participants fell ill, an emergency plan was drawn up by the university together with the Belgian Public Health Service.
Those of whom fell ill received treatment and support. Some were also picked up by parents, guardians, and other relatives.
The students who were sick, but who did not have available family to care for them, were transported back to Breda where the university will assist them. “Due to the scale and seriousness of the situation, it has been decided not to proceed with the remainder of the introductory program on Friday morning,” the educational institution said in a statement.
The applied sciences university said it was “shocked by the situation.” It has asked medical experts to consult with them on the situation.

items.title: Solution found to continue basic healthcare for children in asylum shelters
items.summary: A solution has been found to continue providing basic pediatric healthcare to around 20,000 children in asylum shelters in the Netherlands, Minister Bart van den Brink of Asylum and Migra
items.body_text:
Solution found to continue basic healthcare for children in asylum shelters
A solution has been found to continue providing basic pediatric healthcare to around 20,000 children in asylum shelters in the Netherlands, Minister Bart van den Brink of Asylum and Migration and the COA announced. The municipal health services GGD GHOR will continue providing vaccinations, growth monitoring, developmental assessments, and other preventive care for the next three years while the COA slowly transitions to its new provider, NRC reported.
Youth doctors and nurses from GGD GHOR currently provide pediatric care in asylum shelters. But the Central Agency for the Reception of Asylum Seekers (COA) was required to tender healthcare for child asylum seekers in accordance with the regulations. In April, Gezondheidszorg Asielzoekers (GZA), part of the healthcare chain Arts en Zorg, won that tender.
GGD GHOR was scheduled to stop this care on October 1. But GZA wouldn’t take over until June 1, 2027. That meant that for eight months, children in asylum shelters would not have access to basic pediatric care. The issue prompted parliamentary questions in May.
On Wednesday, the COA and Minister announced that GGD GHOR will take responsibility for providing this care during the transitional period, which has been substantially extended to three years. NRC reported that GGD GHOR requested the longer transition period because it gives the service “the opportunity to recruit and retain staff and at the same time focus on a controlled transfer.”
“The chosen transitional solution with GGD GHOR Nederland is aimed at ensuring that asylum-seeking children retain access to youth healthcare even during the transitional period,” the COA said. “Work is being done on continuity and careful transfer to the future implementation situation.”
Van der Brink told parliament that he “deeply regrets that insufficient attention was paid to the necessary transitional period during the tendering process.” According to him, discussions with the parties involved showed that transitioning the care for these children from one provider to another “is complex and impactful.” To ensure this happens carefully and with children always having access to health care, a three-year bridging contract was chosen, he said.
According to the Minister, it “goes without saying that the COA, given the outcome of the tender and award to GZA as of June 1, 2027, would have preferred to prevent this.”
He also said that he “cannot yet anticipate the potential legal and financial ramifications.”

Oldebroek council executive apologises for Kalashnikov photo
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
A member of the executive on Oldebroek council in Gelderland has apologised for posting a photograph of himself posing with a Kalashnikov in front of a pro-Russian flag. Standing next to him in the photo is a former Almere council candidate for the far-right FvD party, according to the Volkskrant.
Tom de Nooijer, of the local Christelijk Verbond Oldebroek party, shared the image on Instagram after visiting Transnistria, a self-declared, unrecognised pro-Russian region that broke away from Moldova after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
De Nooijer said he had been on holiday in Moldova and travelled to the region out of a “historical interest in the Soviet past”, and went to a shooting range there. He said the trip was private and not meant as a political statement. He is a former presenter of the right-wing broadcaster Ongehoord Nederland.
He initially declined to comment or apologise, prompting anger from opposition councillors. “They fled the violence he is glorifying by posing for a pro-Russian flag,” said Frank van ’t Ende, referring to the 200 Ukrainian refugees the council houses. A ChristenUnie councillor called the photo “shocking”.
Mayor Tanja Haseloop-Amsing told Omroep Gelderland that the council’s executive had been “unpleasantly surprised” by the image.
In a written statement on Wednesday, De Nooijer distanced himself from the hammer-and-sickle flag in the photo, called the visit unwise and apologised to anyone who might have been insulted.

items.title: Dutch spy agencies to get more powers against foreign enemies
items.summary: The Netherlands’ two intelligence agencies are to gain new powers to track and disrupt “obvious adversaries” such as Russian hackers,...
items.body_text:
Dutch spy agencies to get more powers against foreign enemies
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The Netherlands’ two intelligence agencies are to gain new powers to track and disrupt “obvious adversaries” such as Russian hackers, Chinese spies and Iranian operatives without asking permission in advance, under a draft law published by the cabinet.
The domestic intelligence service AIVD and military intelligence service MIVD would no longer need prior sign-off to follow an individual hacker online. “By then they have already gone,” said defence minister Dilan Yesilgöz.
Once a foreign service is formally designated an adversary, the agencies could pursue anyone thought to be working for it, with a watchdog checking afterwards whether their actions were lawful and able to halt operations it considers inappropriate.
The plans have raised concerns about the privacy of Dutch citizens. Yesilgöz said oversight would remain in place. “Putin and his cronies do not deserve our privacy, but the people of the Netherlands do,” she said.
The bill would also let the agencies work more closely with Dutch banks, universities and online platforms, warn them of risks and, in some cases, demand information from them. Interior minister Pieter Heerma, who is responsible for the AIVD, declined to name specific organisations.
It follows the previous cabinet’s abandoned plan to screen 8,000 foreign researchers and students for espionage risks, which was judged unworkable. Oversight of the two agencies would be merged into a single body.
The draft is open for public consultation before it goes to parliament.

items.body_text:
“We have to stop this man”: mass sperm donor fathered 121 kids
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
A Dutch man has fathered at least 121 children as a sperm donor and is still active, according to an investigation by current affairs programme Nieuwsuur – the latest in a line of mass donors who exploit a gap in the legal rules by working outside licensed clinics.
The man, who is 43 and from the Groningen region, donated to several sperm banks but operates mainly online, approaching women directly. Investigators spoke to dozens of affected mothers, and said the true figure is probably far higher.
They also found that the man sat on a government commission that evaluated the Dutch donor law in 2019. It is unclear how or why he was appointed.
Dutch clinics may not use a single donor for more than 12 families. But donors and would-be parents who arrange conception privately are bound by no legal maximum, a gap that lets a determined donor father dozens or hundreds of children unchecked. Nieuwsuur revealed last year that clinics had produced at least 85 mass donors.
The health and youth care inspectorate IGJ, part of the health ministry, said it did not know the man and called the case “very undesirable”. But a spokesperson said the inspectorate oversees care provided in clinics, not conception arranged in the private sphere.
Evasive behaviour 
 The donor children’s foundation Stichting Donorkind and several of the mothers want him to stop. “We have to stop this man,” they told the programme.
The mothers say he lies about how many children he has fathered, growing evasive or hinting he will break off contact when pressed – leverage that matters to women who want their child to be able to know their biological father one day.
Some of the women told Nieuwsuur he sent them sexually suggestive messages, offering to help conceive via the “natural method.” One mother from the Randstad who tried to report him said the police were no help. “The police just stared at me blankly,” she said.
Traces abroad
 There are also signs that the same man has fathered children abroad. One mother traced several children in Germany through an online DNA database, and the man has donated at a Danish sperm bank.
The man declined to be interviewed, saying he wanted any contact to run anonymously through the mothers or official bodies. He asked for privacy for himself and the families, and would not confirm how many children he has conceived.
The most notorious Dutch case remains that of Jonathan Meijer, who fathered some 550 children worldwide and was ordered by a court to stop in 2023.

items.title: Polish government sets out draft 2027 budget with deficit remaining at 7.1% of GDP
items.summary: Defence, healthcare and the energy transition are among the spending priorities.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Poland’s government has approved a draft budget for 2027 that keeps defence, healthcare and the energy transition among its spending priorities, while projecting another year of heavy borrowing.
The deficit is forecast at 7.1% of GDP, unchanged from 2026 but well above the level of 3.7% the government had committed to reach by 2027 after Poland was placed under the European Union’s excessive deficit procedure in 2024.
Rada Ministrów przyjęła projekt ustawy budżetowej na 2027 rok.
Projekt odpowiedzialnie łączy finansowanie bieżących potrzeb państwa i przedsięwzięć wzmacniających jego bezpieczeństwo oraz potencjał rozwojowy.#BudżetPolaków
🔗 https://t.co/SjWyBUwi8U pic.twitter.com/X9ue6cw5ns
— Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 28, 2026
The budget – which must still be consulted with business and trade union representatives before being approved by parliament and then signed by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki – sets total expenditure at 977.6 billion zloty (€225.4 billion), 58 billion zloty more than this year.
Revenues are projected to rise by 68.4 billion zloty to 695 billion zloty, leaving a nominal budget deficit of 282.6 billion zloty, the highest on record and 10 billion zloty more than this year.
Defence spending will remain high, at 198.1 billion zloty, equivalent to 4.5% of GDP, one of the highest levels in NATO. The healthcare budget will reach 274.1 billion zloty, up 26.3 billion zloty from 2026. Spending on energy security and transformation will rise 8.3% year-on-year to reach 19.7 billion zloty.
The government expects GDP growth to remain strong, at 3% in 2027, while average inflation is forecast at 2.8%, within the central bank’s target of 2.5%, plus or minus one percentage point.
Average wages are expected to rise by 5.9% next year in nominal terms, slightly slower than the 6.4% forecast for this year. The government expects that unemployment, measured according to the national methodology, will stand at 6% at the end of 2027, broadly unchanged from its current level.
Poland’s gross borrowing needs are projected at 565 billion zloty in 2027, below the 688 billion zloty budgeted for this year. Debt-servicing costs, however, are expected to rise to 107 billion zloty, up 17 billion zloty from this year.
Finance minister Andrzej Domański said that the rise in debt-servicing costs is driven by an increase in the overall volume of debt and the need to refinance bonds issued in 2020 and 2021 at very low interest rates.
Poland's debt has been growing at the second-fastest rate in the EU this year, and is set to continue rising.
What is behind this trend – and should we be worried – asks Alicja Ptak in the latest of her series of articles and podcasts on Poland’s economy https://t.co/1pvnb2ZxoY
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 30, 2025
The projected deficit leaves Poland under continued pressure to bring its public finances into line with EU fiscal rules.
In 2024, the country was placed under the EU’s excessive deficit procedure after its deficit exceeded the bloc’s limit of 3%. Warsaw pledged at the time to bring the deficit below 3% by 2028.
However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record.
“The 2027 budget represents a continuation of expansionary fiscal policy, and Poland is making no progress in correcting its excessive deficit and is taking no action to bring it below 3% of GDP,” wrote analysts at ING Bank Śląski today. “The result is a further increase in public debt.”

items.title: Polish “vampire” burial sheds light on 17th-century efforts to keep the dead in their graves
items.summary: The remains of a teenage girl were found with a padlock fastened to her toe and a sickle placed across her neck.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Researchers investigating an unusual 17th-century burial in northern Poland, in which the remains of a teenage girl were found with a padlock fastened to her toe and a sickle placed across her neck, believe the measures may have been intended to stop her returning from the dead.
The burial, discovered in 2022 at an unmarked cemetery in the village of Pień, is an example of what archaeologists describe as “anti-vampiric” or “anti-demonic” burial, in which precautions were taken to protect the living from a deceased person believed to pose a danger.
In a newly published academic paper, a team of researchers led by Dariusz Poliński, an archaeologist at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, say that the girl, whom they have named “Zosia”, may have been blamed by her contemporaries for misfortunes such as disease and famine.
The unusual combination of objects that Zosia was buried with – a triangular padlock attached to her left big toe and an iron sickle laid across her throat, with the blade facing towards her neck – immediately attracted archaeologists’ attention when they were discovered.
Poliński and his colleagues have used radiocarbon dating, DNA sequencing, isotope analysis and X-ray and microscopic imaging to investigate the burial. Their findings have now been published in the Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports.
The researchers have established that Zosia, who was aged between 17 and 19, died around the mid-17th century, most likely between 1620 and 1674. Her grave appears to have been secured in two stages, with analysis of soil layers showing that it was reopened after the initial burial and the sickle added later.
“It was unusual that there were two precautions, two methods of showing that this skeleton should be kept in the grave – so the fear of the body coming back to life was greater,” Poliński told CNN.
The researchers say the padlock had several possible meanings in funerary symbolism. It could mark the end of earthly life and the transition to the world of the dead, prevent contact between the living and the dead, break a run of bad luck, or protect the community from the deceased returning.
“In some interpretations, it was also believed to help halt the spread of epidemics,” Poliński told the Polish Press Agency (PAP).
The sickle had a more direct purpose: if the deceased tried to rise from the grave, it was positioned to sever the head or slit the throat, preventing her from returning to the world of the living.
However, the latest findings suggest there may have been a third protective element.
Researchers found “a distinct green discolouration” in the oral cavity, suggesting that an object containing a high proportion of copper had been placed in the girl’s mouth. Given the extent of the discolouration, they have largely ruled out the possibility that it was simply a coin.
“The protective measures taken at the time of the original burial and subsequently after the grave was opened clearly demonstrate the immense fear of Zosia,” said Poliński, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska.
The grave of a "vampire child" – who was turned face down and secured with a padlock to ensure he could not rise from the grave – has been discovered in Poland
Researchers believe the site was a cemetery for those excluded or feared by the local community https://t.co/Ez2QgvMnuX
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2023

A dispute has emerged between Poland’s government and the office of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki over whether Poland would be willing to host allied nuclear weapons.
Deputy defence minister Paweł Zalewski announced on Thursday that Poland wants to participate in the US-led NATO nuclear sharing programme, but without actually hosting warheads. That prompted criticism from Nawrocki’s senior foreign policy aide, Marcin Przydacz, who says Poland should host such weapons.

Zalewski met on Thursday with Elbridge Colby, US under secretary of defence for policy, at NATO’s headquarters in Brussels. Afterwards, he was asked by reporters if an expanded future US military presence in Poland might include nuclear weapons.
“No. I would like to say this very clearly and openly: Poland does not want nuclear warheads on its territory,” replied Zalewski, quoted by broadcaster TVN.
The minister added that Poland still wants to be part of NATO’s nuclear deterrence programme. However, he said that this could be achieved without hosting the weapons themselves.
Those remarks triggered criticism from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party. Former PiS defence minister Mariusz Błaszczak said that refusing to host warheads “in practice means renouncing participation in nuclear sharing”.
“Poland should strive for full participation in nuclear sharing,” added Błaszczak. “This is not a matter of Poland possessing its own nuclear weapons, but of strengthening NATO’s nuclear deterrence on the eastern flank.”
Criticism also came from other sources, including retired Brigadier General Stanisław Koziej, who served as head of the National Security Bureau (BBN) of former President Bronisław Komorowski, who is an ally of the current government.
Koziej called Zalewski’s announcement “an incomprehensible strategic mistake in the field of deterrence”. He said that, to deter Russia, Vladimir Putin must know that there is the possibility Poland could host nuclear weapons.

Late on Thursday, Zalewski commented on the controversy. He rejected Błaszczak’s claim that refusing to host warheads would effectively exclude Poland from nuclear sharing.
“We want to participate in NATO’s nuclear deterrence programme without wanting the stationing of nuclear weapons in Poland,” he wrote. “Thanks to our efforts, NATO has opened up precisely such a possibility.”
In response to Koziej, Zalewski argued that “intentions do not deter, real capabilities do…above all, those whose use we ourselves decide upon”.

items.title: Defense agencies admit problems but plan no resignations
items.summary: A recent audit has highlighted major problems in the Ministry of Defense's area of responsibility for the second year in a row. Defense agencies acknowledge the problems but do not see them as sufficient grounds for resignations.
items.body_text:
Defense agencies admit problems but plan no resignations
A recent audit has highlighted major problems in the Ministry of Defense's area of responsibility for the second year in a row. Defense agencies acknowledge the problems but do not see them as sufficient grounds for resignations.
In fact, the National Audit Office's audit of the state's consolidated annual report, published Friday, was in many ways a continuation of previous years' findings.
In July 2024, the National Audit Office sent a letter to Kusti Salm, then permanent secretary of the Ministry of Defense, stressing that the working procedures of the Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) and the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) needed to be put in order. It also noted that the volume of assets that had not been inventoried remained high.
The audit uncovered errors in documenting purchases of goods, advance payments and the accounting of inventories.
In last year's audit, the National Audit Office also highlighted several problems in the defense sector.
At the time, the National Audit Office said shortcomings in the working procedures of the Estonian Center for Defense Investments and the Estonian Defense Forces affected the accounting of assets, expenses and receivables, both in financial accounts and in budget execution. Problems with working procedures dating back to previous years remained unresolved, while the sharp increase in the amount of money available to the defense sector was also increasing risks, some of which had already materialized.
According to the audit, for example, an advance payment balance of €9.6 million had accumulated in one supplier's account since 2018, effectively functioning as a long-term interest-free loan at the expense of Estonian taxpayers.
Over the years, RKIK had continued to order goods from the supplier but had for several years failed to use the option of offsetting new orders against the advance payment.
This year's report, meanwhile, highlighted that the Ministry of Defense had taken on commitments not included in the state budget. The National Audit Office found that the state may have to cover €70 million in off-budget expenditure.
Ministry of Defense Permanent Secretary Kaimo Kuusk said the potential expense stems from a supplier failing to fulfill its obligations, with the ministry now involved in litigation with the company. It remains unclear, however, whether the risk will materialize.
Former Defense Minister and chair of the Riigikogu State Budget Control Select Committee Urmas Reinsalu (Isamaa) said the Ministry of Defense had explicitly promised not to incur such expenses again and that the ministry had therefore simply lied.
Kuusk responded: "We'll put it right. The explanatory memorandum should have described this hypothetical risk."
For the second year in a row, however, the question has arisen: Who is responsible, if anyone?
Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur (Reform) did not answer calls from ERR, but Kuusk confirmed that the permanent secretary is responsible for the ministry's finances. Kuusk did not, however, see grounds for resigning.
"We have actually been taking a comprehensive look at the entire area of government since July. As for the action plan that was put in place last year, I am not satisfied with the pace at which we moved forward with it. It has [now] become much more concrete and thorough, with specific people and deadlines. It's not enough just to set a final deadline — that's something I've learned over the course of my career as a civil servant," he said.
All sides admit problems
In addition to the Ministry of Defense, the audit highlighted issues at two bodies within the ministry's area of responsibility: the Estonian Center for Defense Investments and the Estonian Defense Forces.

items.title: Health Insurance Fund hopes to reach a balanced budget by 2030
items.summary: The Health Insurance Fund forecasts next year's expenditures at nearly €2.7 billion, and the deficit is expected to shrink to €44 million. The fund aims to reach budget balance gradually by 2030.
items.body_text:
Health Insurance Fund hopes to reach a balanced budget by 2030
The Health Insurance Fund forecasts next year's expenditures at nearly €2.7 billion, and the deficit is expected to shrink to €44 million. The fund aims to reach budget balance gradually by 2030.
On Friday, the supervisory board of the Health Insurance Fund approved the institution's draft budget for next year, which will be taken to state budget negotiations.
The goal for the coming years is to ensure that the budget moves gradually toward balance. According to current projections, the Health Insurance Fund's deficit will decrease by nearly half next year, and balance will be achieved by 2030.
Next year, the Health Insurance Fund expects its expenditures to reach nearly €2.7 billion. Investments across the entire healthcare system will increase by approximately €90 million. To reduce the deficit, a target was set to bring it down from this year's roughly €90 million to €44 million.
The chair of the Health Insurance Fund's supervisory board, Minister of Social Affairs Karmen Joller, said that the goal for the coming years is to restore the fund's financial sustainability while maintaining access to essential services for people.
"My goal is to pull the Health Insurance Fund out of its financial crisis and put the budget back on a sustainable path," Joller said, adding that by 2030 the fund could even reach a surplus.
According to Joller, achieving budget balance will require difficult choices, but essential healthcare services must not be reduced — instead, care pathways must be made smoother.
"If we can implement the reforms already underway — using more digital, data‑based, and AI‑based solutions, expanding the use of e‑consultations, and strengthening primary care and prevention — then achieving budget balance is realistic," the minister said.
According to Siiri Lahe, chair of the Health Insurance Fund's management board, the budget for the next four years has been prepared with the principle that every euro invested in healthcare should create the greatest possible value for people's health.
"We invest in healthcare according to our means — that is, according to how much money is in the system. This means we must find a balance between different needs. It is important to link healthcare funding more closely to the quality and outcomes of care," Lahe explained.
The development plan of the Health Insurance Fund aims to increase the number of healthy life years for Estonian people, and Lahe said this will be the focus in the coming years: every euro directed into healthcare must support the growth of healthy life years.
"Against the backdrop of implementing the development plan's goals, we are focusing on organizing the healthcare system more efficiently. Freed‑up resources will be directed toward funding new services and medicines. Our goal is that the quality and accessibility of services do not decline, and that every person receives the necessary help at the right time and in the right place," Lahe said.
The Health Insurance Fund's four‑year forecast continues to account for wage increases for healthcare workers, as Estonia's average wage is also expected to rise. However, in the current financial forecast, the update of the wage component included in service prices has been postponed by nine months. Thus, the wage component will increase starting not on 1 April next year, but on 1 January 2028.
The Health Insurance Fund emphasized that this is a budgeting assumption that will still be discussed during the decision‑making process. Minimum wage levels for healthcare workers are agreed upon in collective bargaining negotiations between unions and employers.
According to OECD data, healthcare expenditures in Estonia amount to 7.5 percent of GDP, while the EU average is just under 10 percent.
--
Editor: Karin Koppel, Argo Ideon

items.title: Serbian President Vucic Says UN Court ‘Wanted Mladic to Die Behind Bars’
items.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said the UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague was guilty of "uncivilised" and "unjustifiable" behaviour for not releasing the Bosnian Serb genocide convict before his death this week.
items.body_text:
Serbian President Vucic Says UN Court ‘Wanted Mladic to Die Behind Bars’
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said on Friday that “The Hague wanted [Ratko] Mladic to die behind bars, not in a hospital” because the UN court declined to release the former Bosnian Serb military chief for palliative care in Belgrade ahead of his death.
“We have seen that they did not want to allow the general to die in Serbia, where he wanted to die. That is uncivilised behaviour, behaviour without precedent and without justification,” Vucic said in his first public statement after the death of Mladic on Thursday.
He added that he had been in close contact with Mladic’s family, and that Serbia would ensure that the former Bosnian Serb military leader’s funeral would be “done in a dignified and proper manner”.
On Thursday, Serbia’s Justice Minister Nenad Vujic said that Mladic would be buried with state honours in Serbia. Vucic introduced a note of doubt, however, saying that everything published in the press had been inaccurate.
Vucic also claimed that “the West” had only found Serbs guilty of war crimes from the 1990s.
“Do I believe in justice from The Hague? I never have, and I still do not,” he said.
“All those who took part in crimes against Serbs in the former Yugoslavia were always either acquitted or given token sentences, only for those decisions to later be changed on appeal and the defendants ultimately released,” he added.
Vucic’s statement, slamming the Hague court, echoes Thursday’s reactions to Mladic’s death in pro-government media, among members of the governing Serbian Progressive Party, from hardline nationalist politicians Vojislav Seselj and Aleksandar Vulin and from Bosnian Serb political leader Milorad Dodik.
Serbia is an EU candidate state, and on Friday, the European Commission told Radio Free Europe that it was up to the Belgrade authorities to decide what role they would play in the funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic.
However, the Commission warned: “The European Commission considers any glorification of war criminals to be contrary to the most fundamental European values and to have no place either in the EU or in countries that are candidates for EU membership.”

items.title: Montenegro President Summons Security Council Over ‘Destabilisation Threats’
items.summary: President Jakov Milatovic has called an emergency session of the country’s Defence and Security Council after claims that two neighbour states are seeking to destabilise Montenegro and obstruct its EU accession progress.
items.body_text:
Montenegro President Summons Security Council Over ‘Destabilisation Threats’
President Jakov Milatovic’s office said on Friday that he has called the heads of the country’s security sector Defence and Security Council after allegations by Prime Minister Milojko Spajic that the country faces “hybrid threats” from two of its neighbours.
Spajic claimed that officials from at least two countries in the region are involved in coordinated activity aimed at destabilising Montenegro and undermining its path towards European Union membership.
Milatovic’s office said the security chiefs will be asked to provide precise information on Spajic’s allegations, as well as a comprehensive assessment of the country’s security situation.
Spajic said on Thursday that Montenegro had “serious operational security information” that threats would accompany the country’s expected progress in opening new EU negotiating chapters. Montenegro is currently seen as the frontrunner among Balkan states to become the next EU member.
“According to our information, such activities are aimed at destabilising Montenegro, with the expected support of certain political actors and part of the media scene in our country,” Spajic posted on X.
On Friday, Montenegrin newspaper Vijesti reported that Serbia and Albania are the two countries referred to by Spajic.
Vijesti quoted an unnamed source who said that some key players in the region were unhappy with Montenegro’s rapid progress toward European integration and wanted to slow it down.
Another anonymous source quoted by the newspaper claimed that a senior government official was vulnerable because of compromising information that could be used by foreign powers. The source suggested that the official’s political party might leave the ruling coalition as a result.
Milatovic’s office said that the president was concerned by the reports, and that “the public has the right to know which official this is”. But it added that serious security issues should not be used to score political points.
“Issues concerning the security and stability of the state must be addressed responsibly, based on facts and through the institutions of the system,” it said.
The warning did not stop some prominent figures connecting the security issue to responses to the death on Thursday of the Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic.
After parliamentary speaker Andrija Mandic stated that he had sent condolences to the former general’s family, the head of Montenegro’s Islamic Community, Rifat Fejzic, asked if politicians who “mourn war criminals [are] in collusion with this hybrid war?”
Albania’s Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Ferit Hoxha has rejected the suggestion that his country was part of any “destabilising scenario” in Montenegro. Posting on X, Hoxha insisted that the allegations could not “artificially create problems between our two countries”.
“Although no formal accusations have been articulated against Albania, I wish to state clearly and strongly that Albania is not, and cannot be, part of any destabilising scenario, whether in Montenegro – a neighbour, friend, partner, and NATO ally with whom we share the same EU membership goal – or anywhere else,” he wrote.

items.title: Week in Review: Hopes and Dilemmas
items.summary: From Turkey’s search for peace to Serbia’s creeping elections, our selection of Premium stories takes a look at the hopes and dilemmas bubbling away in the background of these developments.
items.body_text:
Week in Review: Hopes and Dilemmas
Forcing a deal
The question of who owns Bosnia and Herzegovina’s state property is a major point of dispute and an unresolved issue on the country’s path away from supervision by the Office of the High Representative and towards membership of the EU. Not surprising, perhaps, in a country where the core issue of sovereignty is contested.
Intractable though the issue may seem, might there be movement towards resolving it? Washington’s newly-discovered interest in energy, mining and infrastructure projects in the country is putting the spotlight on this issue. Now the question is whether Bosnia will solve the issue of state property on Washington’s terms or its own.
Read more: Could Trump’s Administration Force a Deal on Bosnia’s State Property? (August 21, 2026)
Pre-campaigning
Will he? Won’t he? For much of the year, Serbia’s President Aleksandar Vucic has kept the public guessing over if and when he might call early elections. Indeed, Vucic himself may still not have made up his mind.
But in the meantime, the Serbian leader has been on a blitz tour of the country, visiting factories, checking on roadworks and hearing the pleas and grievances of ordinary people. The pace and scale of the campaign have caught many by surprise. In his opinion piece for Balkan Insight, Bojan Vranic dissects the motivation for Vucic’s manoeuvres.
Read more: Hanging Out: Serbia’s Ruling Party Funfair is About Suppressing Voter Turnout (August 24, 2026)
Courting Trump
As the conflict between the US and Iran limps on, ordinary Americans are feeling the pinch. So, it seems, are Donald Trump’s approval ratings on handling the economy, as November’s crucial mid-term elections approach.
Yet while Trump’s appeal may be tanking in the US, his star still shines in faraway corners of the world, including the Balkans. In her regular ‘Letter from Washington’ column, Jovana Djurovic takes a look at the latest attempts by Balkan countries and their leaders to ingratiate themselves with Trump.
Read more: Letter from Washington: Buying Trump’s Favour with UFC in Serbia, Arms in Albania (August 27, 2026)
Making peace
As Turkey moves to end its four decade-long conflict with the Kurdish PKK militant group, the prospect of peace is opening up new dilemmas for Kurdish villagers displaced by years of fighting. Tens of thousands of people have fled areas of fighting over the decades, leaving several thousand villages depopulated.
With peace apparently within grasp, some of those displaced are revisiting their homes and villages. While many long to return for good, rebuilding normal life in most of these villages will be anything but simple, as our report shows.
Read more: As Turkey Makes Peace, Kurdish Villagers Who Fled Conflict Contemplate Return (August 25, 2026)
Brewing resistance
Have people across the Balkans had enough of foreign-backed luxury development projects? Campaigns against two very prominent projects linked to the Trump family in Serbia and Albania seem to suggest so.
In his opinion piece for Balkan Insight, Ted Todorovic-Thomas takes a look at whether something is stirring across the region. He argues that the trend has deeper and more long-standing roots.
Read more: Across the Balkans, Foreign-Backed Luxury Developments Cause Local Anger (August 25, 2026)
Missing millions
In 2017, a private company agreed a concession with the Albanian government to build and operate a waste disposal and incineration facility outside the capital, Tirana. By 2023, some 104 million euros had been transferred to the company in public funds and other revenues.
But there was a catch. When the state took over the project in 2023, there was next to nothing to show for all the money spent. Our investigation takes a look at the ongoing trial over the missing money behind Albania’s ghost incinerators.
Read more: Waste Money Wasted: The Millions of Euros Behind Albania’s Ghost Incinerators (August 21, 2026)

items.title: EU Acknowledges Concerns Over Asbestos Contamination
items.summary: The European Commission acknowledges the seriousness of concerns over asbestos contamination in Hungary, the head of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Environment informed Laurie Kazan-Allen, coordinator of an international organization advocating an asbestos ban. The letter was forwarded to MTI on Thursday by Dániel Holdosi, an activist from Szombathely. François Wakenhut was responding to an open […] The post EU Acknowledges Concerns Over Asbestos Contamination appeared first o
items.body_text:
Temporary chemical measures on affected roads must not distract from the fact that the government still lacks a genuine and transparent action plan.Continue reading
The European Commission acknowledges the seriousness of concerns over asbestos contamination in Hungary, the head of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Environment informed Laurie Kazan-Allen, coordinator of an international organization advocating an asbestos ban. The letter was forwarded to MTI on Thursday by Dániel Holdosi, an activist from Szombathely.
François Wakenhut was responding to an open letter written in early July by 14 international anti-asbestos occupational safety, health, and environmental protection organizations and experts to the leaders of the European Union and Hungary.
In the document, they drew attention to the gravity of the situation in Szombathely, highlighting the dangers posed by the contamination, posing a particular threat to children’s health.
In a letter written on behalf of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the director-general emphasized that it is primarily the responsibility of the competent national authorities to ensure compliance with applicable EU rules in such cases, to assess the risks, and to take the necessary protective and remediation measures.
The European Commission is confident that the national authorities will continue to act swiftly and decisively to protect public health in the affected areas,”
François Wakenhut stated.
The asbestos contamination scandal broke out the day after Hungary’s parliamentary elections, when in Vas County the head of the environmental protection department at the local government office and the mayor of Szombathely announced at an emergency press conference that, in one of the city’s single-family residential areas, on several streets of the “Oladi Plateau,” crushed stone containing asbestos had been spread years earlier. Airborne asbestos fibers are seriously harmful to health.
István Orbán, director general of the government office, said that, according to reports, four quarries in Burgenland, Austria, had previously been closed due to high asbestos content, and they suspect the material may have come from there.
András Nemény, mayor of Szombathely, announced that 12 kilometers of streets in that part of the city are covered with asbestos-contaminated crushed stone, and the cost of safely removing and disposing of it exceeds the city’s financial resources.
To access the force majeure fund, he appealed to both the outgoing government and the incoming government for assistance. Tibor Navracsics, the outgoing Minister of Regional Development, promised to make the fund available, and a supporting government resolution was passed, but only the local government was able to take concrete steps; to prevent dust from spreading, they began regularly watering the affected streets and even applied a layer of bitumen to some sections, while awaiting guidance from experts on exactly what steps to take.
In the following weeks, several municipalities in Vas County—including Kőszeg, Lukácsháza, Bük, and Sárvár—reported that they might also be affected; laboratory tests revealed asbestos levels exceeding the threshold in all of these locations.
In Táplánszentkereszt, the areas in front of the daycare center, kindergarten, and school were inadvertently covered with asbestos-containing material; there, too, the local government had no other option but to spray the area with calcium chloride. In Bük, the local government had the material removed at its own expense, in compliance with regulations governing hazardous materials.
In Szombathely, weekly public forums were held; construction in the area was halted due to the imposed restrictions, and heavy vehicle traffic was temporarily banned and then restricted during certain periods.
On May 21, the Hungarian prime minister held talks in Vienna with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker.

I only found out on Facebook that Béla Csiszár, the representative for the Fejér 1 congressional district and also […] The post Wind Power Plans Draw Criticism as Mayors Are Sidelined appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
The company aims to reduce its exposure to energy costs over the long term.Continue reading
Wind turbines are to be built in Fejér County. András Cser-Palkovics, the mayor of Székesfehérvár, stated that they were deliberately excluded from the negotiations, Világgazdaság reported.
“Is not Székesfehérvár part of the Fejér 1 congressional district? I only found out on Facebook that Béla Csiszár, the representative for the Fejér 1 congressional district and also our city’s representative, had organized an online forum on the topic of wind turbines for the (quote!) ‘mayors of the municipalities in his district.’
I do not understand why Székesfehérvár did not receive an invitation to this meeting,”
wrote András Cser-Palkovics (FIDESZ), mayor of the city with county rights, in his Facebook post on Wednesday.
“I did not think this would need to be emphasized again, but Székesfehérvár is also part of the Fejér 1 electoral district. It is the center of both the county and the electoral district. The government previously announced that it would include local municipalities in the wind power program. I would like to point out that Székesfehérvár is also a local community—one that rightfully expects answers to such a controversial issue, which also involves strategic and environmental policy matters. I would therefore have liked to participate in the consultation.
After all, local communities must not be left out of the decision-making process,”
András Cser-Palkovics added.
The mayor made it clear that they would have to take this matter into their own hands in the future. He concluded his remarks by announcing that he would provide details shortly.
On Thursday afternoon, he reported in a comment under his own post that Béla Csiszár (TISZA) had since initiated a personal meeting with him on this topic. “I certainly welcome this and am grateful for it! I believe it is important that we discuss matters affecting our city, as well as government plans, from time to time, and that we are able to inform the public about them—jointly, if necessary. I am also open to making this a regular practice,” wrote the mayor.
Via Világgazdaság; Featured photo: Pexels
