items.title: Seven Hungarians to Make History in Champions League
items.summary: Dominik Szoboszlai Barnabás Varga’s stunning two-goal performance fired Greek champions AEK Athens into the UEFA Champions League league phase—and helped set a new record for Hungarian players in Europe’s elite competition. A total of seven Hungarians will thus represent five clubs in the 36-team league phase this season, the largest contingent in Champions League history. […] The post Seven Hungarians to Make History in Champions League appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
Despite his strong performance, the Hungarian forward faces a tough battle for a spot in the starting lineup.Continue reading
                                    
                                        Hungary Today
                                         2026.08.28.                                
                                                    Barnabás Varga’s stunning two-goal performance fired Greek champions AEK Athens into the UEFA Champions League league phase—and helped set a new record for Hungarian players in Europe’s elite competition. A total of seven Hungarians will thus represent five clubs in the 36-team league phase this season, the largest contingent in Champions League history. Adding to the excitement, Péter Gulácsi’s Villarreal will face defending champion Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool, which boasts two Hungarian players in its squad.
On Wednesday night, 31-year-old Hungarian national team striker Barnabás Varga was the hero of the second leg of AEK Athens’ playoff against Levski Sofia. After a scoreless 0-0 draw in the first leg in Bulgaria, AEK wasted little time in front of its home crowd. Varga scored twice within the opening 30 minutes, putting the Greek side firmly on course for victory. AEK ultimately cruised to a convincing 4-0 win.
For AEK, the result marks a return to European soccer’s elite after an eight-year absence, while Varga will make his personal Champions League debut. At the same time, his two-goal performance sealed a new Hungarian record.
The previous record was four Hungarian players, set during the 2011/12 and 2024/25 seasons, Magyar Nemzet writes. While there have technically been more Hungarians on the Champions League stage—Hungarian clubs Ferencváros Budapest (1995/96) and Debrecen VSC (2009/10) each fielded 15 domestic players in their respective group-stage campaigns—never before have so many Hungarian players simultaneously represented foreign clubs in Europe’s top competition. In the previous record-setting 2011/12 season, the four Hungarians were spread across KRC Genk (Dániel Tőzsér and László Köteles), Olympiacos (Balázs Megyeri), and Zenit St. Petersburg (Szabolcs Huszti).
Seven Hungarian players at five clubs across five of Europe’s top leagues make up this year’s record contingent.
The outlook for the 2026/27 season is promising, as most of the Hungarian athletes are expected to play important roles for their respective teams.
- Liverpool FC: Dominik Szoboszlai has established himself as a leader in the Reds’ midfield. Alongside him is Milos Kerkez, who already has considerable experience at the highest level after helping Liverpool reach the quarterfinals last season.
- RB Leipzig: Defensive leader Willi Orbán returns to the European stage with Leipzig after a one-year absence.
- Villarreal CF: 36-year-old goalkeeper Péter Gulácsi joined the Spanish top-flight club in early August after 11 years at RB Leipzig. He signed a two-year contract and, according to Spanish reports, is expected to be the club’s primary goalkeeper in Champions League matches.
- Galatasaray and AEK Athens: Roland Sallai has joined the Turkish powerhouse, while AEK Athens will have both star striker Barnabás Varga and Milán Vitális available for the league phase.
Soccer fans can look forward to an unprecedented Hungarian presence on the continent’s biggest stage this fall. The Champions League draw will also see Hungarians go head-to-head, with Péter Gulácsi’s Villarreal set to face Liverpool and its two Hungarian stars, Dominik Szoboszlai and Milos Kerkez, in the league phase.

items.title: Iványi Gábor iskolájuk újranyitásáról: Érdemes megvárni, amíg a világ változik, kiállni, szólni
items.summary: A MET vezetője egyeztetést kezdeményezett az oktatási és gyermekügyi miniszterrel a többi bezárt iskolájuk újranyitásáról.
items.body_text:
Iványi Gábor iskolájuk újranyitásáról: Érdemes megvárni, amíg a világ változik, kiállni, szólni
„Érdemes kitartani, érdemes megvárni, amíg a világ változik, kiállni, szólni és csinálni, ameddig csak lehet. Az én elvem az, hogy menjünk el a falig” – mondta az RTL Híradónak Iványi Gábor, miután két évvel a bezáratása után idén szeptemberben újra megnyílik a Wesley Kincsei Iskola. Az iskolát fenntartó Magyarországi Evangéliumi Testvérközösség szerdán megkapta a működési engedélyt a kormányhivataltól, illetve az egyetértő nyilatkozatot Lannert Judit oktatási minisztertől.
A Wesley-ben egyelőre csak egy első osztály indul majd tíz, sajátos nevelési igényű tanulóval, mivel az iskolának kevés ideje volt a felkészülésre. Az intézmény vezetője, Iványi Júlia azt mondta: a feladat, hogy hirtelen elkezdjék, az borzasztóan nagy kihívás, de nem megugorhatatlan. Iványi Júlia arról is beszélt, hogy szinte azonnal túljelentkezés volt, olyanok is visszatérnének, akik korábban az iskolába jártak.
A jelentkezéseket az iskola folyton veszi fel, mert az intézményvezető szerint 2027-től már minden osztályt szeretnének feltölteni. A Magyar Evangéliumi Testvérközösség bezárt iskolái újranyitásáról Iványi Gábor egyeztetést kezdeményezett Lannert Judit oktatási és gyermekügyi miniszterrel.
A fővárosi kormányhivatal még két éve, pár nappal a tanévkezdés előtt jelentette be, hogy törölte a nyilvántartásból a MET által fenntartott két oktatási intézményt: a Wesley János Óvoda, Általános Iskola és Gimnáziumot, illetve a Wesley Kincsei Általános Iskola és Gimnáziumot. A Sára Botond vezette hivatal azzal indokolt, hogy a MET felhalmozott közüzemi tartozásaival veszélyezteti a gyermekek folyamatos és biztonságos nevelését. Az intézmények vezetői bíróságra vitték az ügyet, ahol a 2025-ös döntés után idén tavasszal is kimondták: jogellenes volt a kormányhivatal lépése.

items.title: Kétszázzal száguldó folyékony betonként tarolt le mindent, és egy aggasztó tavat is felduzzasztott a villámárvíz
items.summary: Közel 2500 embert még mindig keresnek, legkevesebb 580-an meghaltak az egész településeket megsemmisítő árban. A mentést egy időre fel kellett függeszteni, miután egy kialakult tó miatt újabb áradás veszélyére figyelmeztettek a kínai és nepáli hatóságok.
items.body_text:
Kétszázzal száguldó folyékony betonként tarolt le mindent, és egy aggasztó tavat is felduzzasztott a villámárvíz
Új vizsgálatok szerint nemcsak egy gleccser, hanem az alatta lévő hegyoldal leomlása együtt okozhatta a péntek délutáni legfrissebb adatok szerint már legkevesebb 580 ember halálát okozó nepáli villámárvizet, ami mindent elsöpört, ami az útjába került.
Pénteken 1900 embert még mindig eltűntként tartottak nyilván a himalájai országban, köztük az ott eltűnt három magyar állampolgárt, több mint 550 embert pedig a kínai oldalon keresnek, ahol a mentőalakulatok csak délutánra érték el az áradástól érintett, nehezen megközelíthető területet. A villámárvíz okozta pusztításról itt olvashat részletesen.
Újabb áradástól tartottak
A mentést pénteken egy időre fel kellett függeszteni, miután a kínai és a nepáli hatóságok arra figyelmeztettek, hogy újabb áradással fenyeget a két ország határán lévő folyón a jég- és földcsuszamlás miatt kialakult tó, amiben több mint kétmillió köbméternyi víz gyűlt fel. A tó a CCTV kínai állami televízió által közölt adatok szerint a Gyirong határátkelőtől nagyjából tíz kilométernyire alakult ki a folyó felső folyásán.
A kínai hatóságok arra számítottak, hogy a tóban a napokban több mint hárommillió köbméternyi víz gyűlhet fel. A kínai állami sajtó péntek délelőtt arról számolt be, hogy a tóból elkezdett ömleni a víz, ezért a kínai hatóságok visszahívták a Gyirong határátkelő felé tartó mentőalakulatokat. Hasonló döntést hoztak Nepálban is, ahol a túlélők is elkezdtek magasabban fekvő területekre menekülni. A kialakult tavat tartó természetes gát végül nem szakadt át, csak lassan kezdett el folyni belőle a víz, a tó vízszintje így tíz métert csökkent.
A veszély azonban nem múlt el, a területen a következő napokban ugyanis erős esőzések várhatóak, és a felette lévő hegyoldal is instabil, akár egy újabb hegyomlás is bekövetkezhet – mondta a BBC-nek Jakob Steiner, a Grazi Egyetem geológusa. Az egyetlen dolog, amit tenni lehet, hogy reménykednek, hogy a tóból szép lassan elfolyik a víz, magyarázta. A szakértő szerint azonban még egy gátszakadás esetén sem kell arra számítani, hogy a szerdaihoz hasonló árvíz zúdulna le.
Kétszázzal száguldó folyékony beton
Eddig úgy lehetett tudni, hogy az áradást egy gleccserről leszakadt hatalmas, több mint fél kilométer széles jégtömeg okozta, ami több mint egy kilométert zuhant az alatta elterülő folyóvölgybe, és közben vízzé olvadt. A katasztrófa okait vizsgáló tudósok csütörtökön már arról számoltak be az érintett területről készült legfrissebb, felhőktől nem takart műholdfelvételek tanulmányozása után, hogy nemcsak a gleccser, hanem az alatta lévő sziklaréteg is leszakadt a hegyről.
„Sokkal nagyobb omlás volt, mint ahogy azt eleinte láthattuk a műholdas felvételeken” – mondta a New York Timesnak Kristen Cook, a francia Université Grenoble Alpes egyetem szakértője. Stephen Hicks, a londoni College egyetem szeizmológusa szerint a lezuhant szikla és jég tömege közel négyszázmillió tonna volt, és az áradás ezer tonna TNT-nek megfelelő energiát szabadított fel.
Az ebből kialakult ár így nem csupán vízből állt, hanem iszap, homok, kavics és hatalmas sziklatömbök is voltak benne, ami „folyékony betonként” száguldott végig a völgyeken – mondta a CNN-nek Hatim Sharif, a Texasi Egyetem mérnökprofesszora. Ráadásul hatalmas sebességgel söpört el mindent: egy kínai kormányzati geológus közlése szerint az áradat majdnem 200 km/h-s sebességgel kezdett el száguldani lefelé, egyes helyeken elérve a több mint száz méteres magasságot.
„Még soha nem láttam ekkora katasztrófát”
A nepáli katasztrófavédelmi hivatal (NDRRMA) magyar idő szerint péntek kora délutáni adatai alapján 116 külföldi állampolgárt mentettek ki az áradástól érintett területekről, míg a nepáli turisztikai hivatal 121 külföldit említett. A legtöbben indiaiak és kínaiak, de mellettük kilenc dél-koreai, két olasz és két amerikai állampolgár is van. Az Ekantipur nepáli lap információi szerint helyi idő szerint délután

items.body_text:
Unger Anna: A jogállami megoldás nem az, hogy én most pofára odamegyek Felcsútra, és azt mondom, hogy Mészáros Lőrinc, jöjjön velem!
„Tudom, hogy mindenki az elszámoltatást várja, tudom, hogy mindenki a bilincsek kattanását várja, és tudom, hogy mindenki szeretné hallani a zörgő rácsokat, de létre kell hozni a hivatalt, meg kell választani még három elnökhelyettest” – mondta Unger Anna, akit pénteken titkos szavazáson választott meg az Országgyűlés a Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatal (NVVH) élére. Megválasztása után először a Telexnek adott interjút.
Unger azt ígérte, a következő hetekben azon lesz, hogy megtalálja a legjobb munkatársakat az elnökhelyettesekkel együttműködve minden lehetséges pozícióra. Azt mondta, nem rajta múlik, hogy a bíróságok mikor hoznak ítéleteket, az NVVH arra tud vállalkozni, hogy többek között feltárja a visszaéléseket, biztosítsa a vagyonvisszaszerzés lehetőségeit, amikorra már megszületnek az ítéletek. A hivatal szerinte azt tudja vállalni, hogy felkutatja az eltűnt közvagyont, amiről „mindannyian tudjuk, hogy 20 és 60 ezer milliárd forint között van”.
Unger azt mondta, az év végéig már elindulhatnak a vizsgálatok, azt viszont csak a hivatal működésének hatodik éve végére ígérte, hogy teljesen feltárják, pontosan mennyi pénz tűnt el. Semmiképpen sem elméleti kutatóintézet lesz a hivatal, de lesz egy olyan része, ami nemcsak a feltárt ügyekről, hanem magáról a korrupciós rendszer bemutatásáról fog szólni. Szerinte az emberek nem buták, ha közzéteszi a hivatal az erről szóló információkat, akkor meg fogják érteni, hogyan működött a rendszer.
Korábban is használta már a Felcsúti Számvevőszék kifejezést, amiről most azt mondta, alapvetően arra utal, hogy egy jól körülhatárolható kör döntötte el, mi legyen az 500 milliárd forint feletti állami beruházások sorsa. Szerinte „Orbán Viktor nem egyszer utalt erre”, és az oknyomozó újságírók munkája alapján okkal feltételezhető, hogyan hoztak döntéseket az ilyen, nagy értékű beruházásokról. Attól viszont Unger többszöri kérdésre is elzárkózott, hogy bárkit is megnevezzen. Szerinte „lesz bizonyíték, lesz eljárás”, de törvényt sértene, ha „az emlékei és olvasmányélményei” alapján megmondaná, kik ellen fognak vizsgálódni.
„Nem vagyok hülye a joghoz” – mondta az NVVH megválasztott elnöke a személyét ért kritikákra reagálva. Azt mondta, politológusként nagyon sok jogi tárgyat hallgatott. Elmondta azt is, hogy a Tiszából senkivel, Ruff Bálinttal sem egyeztetett arról, hogy pályázni fog. Ezt egyedül két jogásznak, a férjének és „az ország egyik legjobb közigazgatási jogászának” mondta el.
Azt mondta: „nincs eredményességi kritérium” a munkaköri leírásában, bármennyi visszaszerzett vagyonnal elégedett lenne. Egyelőre viszont fel kell tárni, mennyi tűnt el, aztán ebből minél többet visszaszerezni.

items.body_text:
Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
Prague Morning
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.
Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.
At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.
The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.
The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.
The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.
How the Champions League league phase works
The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.
Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.
The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.
The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

MINT Market Returns to Prague's Náplavka with More Than 130 Local Brands
Prague Morning
MINT Market returns to Prague’s Rašín Embankment on Sunday, September 6, bringing more than 130 independent brands and makers to the Vltava riverbank.
From 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., visitors can browse a wide selection of independent fashion, jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations and original accessories, with many of the products made by small Czech and Prague-based businesses.
The popular design market is also known for its relaxed atmosphere, food stalls and chill-out area. Admission is free, and the riverside venue is fully accessible. The event is suitable for visitors of all ages.
MINT Market has been supporting independent and local creators since 2010.
Over the past 16 years, the project has grown from a small market into a nationwide platform, hosting more than 450 events in over 20 Czech cities and bringing together a community of more than 1,500 designers and makers.
For visitors, the September event offers a chance to discover products that are often made locally and in small quantities, while meeting the people behind the brands directly.
View this post on Instagram
“Supporting small and local brands has been one of the core ideas of our project from the very beginning,” says MINT Market organizer Lenka Šašková.
“We provide creators with a place where they can showcase their products and meet their customers, because nothing can replace a personal meeting.”
The full list of vendors and further information about the September market can be found on the MINT Market website. Updates are also available through the Facebook event and Instagram.

items.body_text:
Historic Invalidovna Building in Prague Begins Major Reconstruction
Prague Morning
The long-awaited reconstruction of Prague’s Invalidovna has officially begun.
The Baroque complex in Karlín will undergo a major renovation costing CZK 2.15 billion, with work scheduled for completion in 2030.
The project is the largest investment in the history of the National Heritage Institute (NPÚ). Alongside the restoration of the historic building, two new extensions will be constructed on the southern side of the complex.
One will provide facilities for the Prague Philharmonic Choir, while the other will house technical infrastructure needed to operate the site.
Much of Invalidovna will remain open to the public
Once the reconstruction is complete, the NPÚ will use part of the complex for restoration workshops, laboratories, archives and study rooms.
An underground garage with space for 50 vehicles is also planned.
Around 80 percent of the complex is expected to remain accessible to the public. The restored site will include exhibition and conference spaces, visitor routes through the Baroque interiors, a café and facilities for children’s groups operated by Prague 8.
A new multi-purpose hall in one of the extensions will be suitable for concerts, conferences and other events. The modern section will also contain technical facilities that cannot be accommodated inside the protected historic building.
The courtyard and gardens will be opened through the original entrances.
A Baroque complex with a long military history
Invalidovna was built between 1731 and 1737 based on plans by Kilián Ignác Dientzenhofer, one of the leading architects of the Czech Baroque. The institution provided accommodation and care for war veterans and their families until 1935.
The original complex was designed at a time when European armies were beginning to develop more systematic forms of care for soldiers who had been wounded or disabled in war.
Military campaigns were often accompanied by outbreaks of diseases such as cholera and typhus, which could kill even soldiers whose battlefield injuries were not life-threatening. Separate psychiatric institutions were later established for veterans suffering severe mental trauma after their military service.

items.body_text:
Orchards, Roads Damaged as Rains Cause Flooding in Imereti
Heavy rains on August 27 damaged orchards, crops, and roads in the western Georgian region of Imereti, with the damage particularly affecting neighborhoods and villages in Baghdati Municipality.
Videos from the scene show streams of water rushing through roads and orchards and entering homes, with locals saying the rains caused small rivers to swell suddenly. Residents are seen struggling to protect their houses, yards and belongings, while appealing to the authorities for assistance.
“In just half an hour, this small river wreaked havoc on all my family’s work,” a resident of Obcha village of Baghdati municipality wrote on social media, posting videos of the orchard filled by rapidly moving water and a flooded house. “I have no words. I walk around in tears.”
Local media also published an image showing a section of a forest-covered slope that had collapsed.
Heavy flooding was also reported in villages in nearby Zestaphoni Municipality, while rainwater flooded streets in Kutaisi, the region’s administrative center.
The Baghdati Municipality City Hall said authorities are operating in emergency mode, and a commission has been set up to assess the damage. Hundreds of households have been left without gas and electricity.

Abkhaz Blogger Daur Buava Found Dead in Tbilisi
Daur Buava, a 31-year-old Abkhaz blogger and TikToker who lived in Tbilisi-controlled territory and published videos promoting Abkhaz-Georgian friendship, was found dead in Tbilisi.
The Interior Ministry told Civil.ge that it is investigating the case under Article 115 of the Criminal Code, which covers incitement to suicide and is commonly invoked when a person is found dead in unclear circumstances in Georgia.
His body was reportedly discovered in a Tbilisi apartment on August 27, days after his presumed death. The Interior Ministry said a preliminary inspection of the body found no signs of violence, with forensic reports to establish the cause of death pending.
Buava, known on TikTok as Tarielovich and followed by more than 100,000 people, was born in Tkvarcheli, occupied Abkhazia, and moved to Georgia proper in 2021, where he was granted Georgian citizenship under a simplified procedure in 2022.
In 2022, the de facto security service of Sokhumi filed charges of high treason against Buava, saying the blogger published videos with “direct and latent appeals to an unlimited circle of users aimed at damaging sovereignty, territorial integrity, national security and defense capacity.”
The de facto authorities also claimed Buava aided Tbilisi in “conducting hostile activity” against Abkhazia by advocating for the occupied region’s “accession” with Georgia.

items.body_text:
Kavelashvili Pardons Several Jailed Protesters
Up to nine people jailed in connection with the anti-government protests of 2024–2025 have been reported to be among the 226 people pardoned by Georgian Dream-elected President Mikheil Kavelashvili on the religious holiday, marking the first known instance of Kavelashvili using his pardon powers to release imprisoned protesters.
On August 27, Kavelashvili’s administration reported granting 226 pardons on the occasion of the Dormition of the Virgin Mary (Mariamoba). In the hours that followed, reports emerged that among the pardonees were up to nine persons convicted in connection with protests. According to various media reports, the nine include Pridon Bubuteishvili, Davit Khomeriki, Saba Jikia, Daniel Mumladze, Guram Khutashvili, Tornike Mchedlishvili, Denis Kulanin, Simon Makharadze, and Avtandil Topchishvili.
Bubuteishvili was arrested during the spring 2024 protests against the foreign agents law, while Khomeriki, Jikia, Mumladze, and Khutashvili were serving multi-year sentences after being convicted in connection with pro-EU protests that erupted in November 2024. Mchedlishvili, Makharadze, and Topchishvili were among dozens arrested and tried in connection with October 4, 2025 election-day unrest.
While there have been repeated calls on Kavelashvili and Georgian Dream authorities to release those imprisoned in connection with the protests, ruling party leaders have implied that considering such a move would require applying for a pardon and showing remorse. Part of the detained protesters had openly refused such a move, seeing their charges as politically motivated.
In later months, however, plea deals and pardons have been discussed more openly, both amid shifting attitudes within protest circles and what appeared to be a more openly expressed willingness on the part of the authorities. It was reported in May that Bubuteishvili had applied for a pardon, while it remains unknown whether any of the other pardonees had also submitted formal requests.
Dozens have also left prison early or had their sentences reduced as part of plea agreements, particularly among those arrested in connection with the October 4 unrest.
The pardoned protesters include:
- Pridon Bubuteishvili was arrested in spring 2024, during the protests against Georgian Dream’s reintroduction of the foreign agents law, on allegations of causing GEL 500 [around USD 180] worth of damage to the gate of the Parliament building and throwing a stone at a firefighter, resulting in injury. He was found guilty and sentenced to five years in prison in January 2025.
- Davit Khomeriki was arrested during the pro-EU protests that erupted in November 2024, and was sentenced in August 2025 to four years and six months in prison on charges of plotting an explosion. Prosecutors alleged that Khomeriki carried bottles with inflammable substances in his bag, preparing a Molotov cocktail attack.
- Saba Jikia was arrested during the pro-EU protests that erupted in November 2024 and sentenced in July 2025 to four years and six months in prison on charges of assaulting a police officer.
- Daniel Mumladze and Guram Khutashvili were arrested during the pro-EU protests that erupted in November 2024 and sentenced in June 2025 to three years each for damaging surveillance cameras during protests, with prosecutors reportedly denying them plea deals.
- Denis Kulanin, a Russian citizen, was arrested in spring 2025 and sentenced to two years in jail in June 2025 on allegations of damaging a police car.
- Tornike Mchedlishvili, Simon Makharadze, and Avtandil Topchishvili were arrested in connection with the October 4, 2025, election-day unrest. Mchedlishvili was sentenced to five years in prison, while Makharadze and Topchishvili had their sentences reduced to one year in addition to three years of suspended sentences as part of plea agreements.

items.title: Asbestos allegedly found under Rustaveli Avenue during renovation
items.summary: The Public Defender’s Office has urged the authorities to verify the reports.
items.body_text:
Georgia’s Public Defender’s Office has issued a warning, calling on Tbilisi City Hall to investigate the presence of asbestos allegedly found under Rustaveli Avenue during ongoing rehabilitation work.
The agency issued its appeal after pictures of what appears to be asbestos found on Rustaveli Avenue surfaced online on 21 August. Social media user Irakli Pipia said that asbestos was used by the Soviet authorities to construct water pipes under the thoroughfare.
On Thursday, urban and environmental activist Nata Peradze said that samples of the shattered asbestos pipes were collected and are ready to be sent to a laboratory in Berlin. She added that they need to raise funds for the analysis.
The Public Defender of Georgia issued its appeal on Facebook on Thursday.
‘Asbestos is a substance with high health risk and its exposure is related to serious diseases, including mesothelioma and lung cancer. The risk increases sharply during mechanical exposure, cutting, crushing, drilling and removal from the ground.’
‘International standards for asbestos regulation have not been fully implemented in Georgia, technical regulations have not been adopted that would regulate the protection of employees from exposure to asbestos in the workplace’, the agency said.
It also warned that schools located around the avenue will start their classes on 15 September, and that students could potentially be exposed to asbestos.
‘Children are a particularly vulnerable group to asbestos exposure, as their respiratory system is still in the process of formation, and the latent period of asbestos-related diseases lasts for decades.’
The Public Defender called on Tbilisi City hall to determine whether the material found in the renovation area contains asbestos, and to spread awareness about the matter.
In 2019, more than 70,000 people in the EU died from past exposure to asbestos at work.
Authorities have been discussing the renovation of Rustaveli Avenue since 2023. The renovation started in late July, 2026 with authorities saying it is scheduled to be finished in November.
The construction company responsible for the rehabilitation work has been fined four times for failing to adhere to the stipulated work schedule, leading to a total of ₾5,000 ($1,900) in fines.
Rustaveli Avenue has historically been the site of numerous mass protests and clashes between protesters and riot police.

items.title: Lavrov says Armenia must choose between EU and EAEU
items.summary: Lavrov also criticised Yerevan for its handling of Russia’s concession over Armenia’s railways.
items.body_text:
Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said Armenia must choose between the EU and its membership in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), echoing previous remarks issued by other Russian officials.
Lavrov’s remarks reflect the deepening standoff between the two countries. Armenia pushes towards EU integration, which Russia sees as incompatible with EAEU membership. Pashinyan also wants to restructure the ownership of the Russia-run national railway over concerns about deterring foreign investments. Those two issues together highlight Armenia’s effort to balance its relationship with historical partner Russia while pivoting towards the West.
On Armenia’s EU aspirations, Lavrov said that Pashinyan’s position, that a referendum on EU membership can only be discussed after Armenia submits its application and drafts a ‘road map’, shows that he does not fully ‘trust his own people’ to make an honest choice. Lavrov recalled that in May, EAEU countries called on Armenia to hold a referendum to decide whether to stay with the EAEU or join the EU, which he said is a justified request.
‘The norms of one organisation are incompatible with the norms of the other organisation. This has been said many times’, Lavrov said.
Lavrov argued that Armenia now has to choose between the EU and what it already has, pointing to trade turnover which he said exceeded $6 billion in the past three years and had reached $12 billion in one year. He did not specify whether he meant trade between Armenia and the EAEU or with Russia.
Turning to the railway issue, Lavrov stressed that Russia has done everything for its part to normalise relations with Armenia, and expressed surprise that Armenia discusses the railway concession publicly rather than directly with its partner.
Armenia’s railway system is owned by Russian Railways (RZhD) under a 30-year concession signed in 2008.
Earlier in August, Pashinyan told reporters that Armenia is seeking to negotiate a compromise with Russia over the Russian-run national railway, rather than unilaterally cancelling Russian Railways’ (RZhD) management contract. Pashinyan first called for ending the RZhD’s presence in February, arguing that Russian control discourages investment from international partners. In July, he threatened arbitration and a $2 billion annual bill for RZhD’s management rights, triggering warnings from Russia.
The Russian Foreign Ministry, in response, has accused the West of ‘blackmailing’ Armenia over the concession of the railway.

items.title: Azerbaijan calls on Russia to investigate protest in front of its embassy in Moscow

items.body_text:
Azerbaijan has called on Russia to investigate three National Bolsheviks for putting up banners on the walls of the Azerbaijani Embassy in Moscow calling for the release of Russians detained in Azerbaijan. Baku has called the incident an ‘unacceptable provocation’.
Footage from the small protest appeared on a Telegram channel linked to the National Bolshevik Movement. In the video, the protesters criticised Azerbaijan for launching criminal cases against Russians.
Their banners read: ‘Azerbaijan’s State Security Service tortures, [Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev] covers it up!, ‘Russian blood is on your hands!’, and ‘Let the Russian citizens go!’.
The movement said that Azerbaijan ‘consistently pursues an anti-Russian policy’.
A few hours later Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry issued an official statement saying that the incident might be aimed ‘at artificially straining Azerbaijani-Russian relations’.
The ministry described the protest as an ‘ugly and biased campaign’ against Azerbaijan, which it claimed was being waged in certain Russian media outlets.
On 19 August, Azerbaijan Prosecutor General’s Office issued warrants for three Russian citizens accusing them of making calls to overthrow the government.
Relations between Azerbaijan and Russia deteriorated following the crash of an Azerbaijan Airlines passenger plane shot down in Grozny in December 2024, which resulted in the deaths of 38 people.
Russia subsequently arrested Azerbaijanis, accusing them of crimes committed as far back as the early 2000s; Azerbaijan characterized these actions as an instance of ethnic discrimination.
The arrests of Azerbaijanis in Russia were followed by the arrests of Russian citizens in Azerbaijan in June.

items.title: OPINION: Sweden keeps bodging its migration laws – it needs to do better
items.summary: Time and again, Swedish migration laws lead to people whom nearly everyone agrees should be allowed to stay being forced out the country. Sweden needs to do better, says James Savage.
items.body_text:
Let’s start with the obvious: Sweden can have any immigration policy it chooses, and it has chosen a strict one, for understandable reasons. The migration crisis of 2015 saw stations in Sweden started filling up with refugees from wars a continent away and the government didn’t seem to have a plan to cope with it. It looked chaotic, and in a sense it was.
But Sweden’s immigration policy hasn’t just become stricter: due to a combination of incompetent drafting and bureaucratic inflexibility it has become unfair, counterproductive and damaging to Sweden’s national interest. And the problem isn’t just down to the current government, it’s systemic.
We saw it in 2017, when the previous government was still in power: stories emerged of work permit holders who were settled in Sweden and whose talents were in demand, being refused renewals for small bureaucratic errors by their employers, like buying the wrong health insurance. The rules were eventually made more flexible to allow the Migration Agency to look at the bigger picture, but only after much foot-dragging by politicians and bureaucrats — and too late for many people.
We saw it again with teen deportations: we knew in 2022 that the young-adult children of immigrants were being deported, often in the middle of their studies, in many cases because their parents, who came on work permits, had been granted permanent residency (children of permanent residents need permits in their own right after 18, children of work permit holders after 21). This was allowed to continue for four years until politicians acted.
The latest situation affects British citizens living in Sweden. Many people who lived here legally for years, often more Swedish than British, are being kicked out of the country because they messed up the paperwork after Brexit. Many had been granted “permanent right of residence” (“permanent uppehållsrätt”) under EU rules and mistakenly believed that this meant they didn’t need to take further action. Sweden only made fairly limited, half-hearted attempts to contact British citizens in Sweden, so many didn’t know they had to act.
Others, like John Sellers, fulfilled the criteria for citizenship and applied for that instead. The problem was, in the years it took the Migration Agency to look at John’s citizenship application, Britain had left the EU, John’s right to remain in Sweden had disappeared with it — and as a consequence he no longer qualified for citizenship. Now John, 34, who has lived in Sweden since he was 10 and has a Swedish wife, is stuck in Britain with no obvious way back to Sweden. Computer says no.
Two migration ministers have vowed to The Local that they want British people to be allowed to stay, as British and EU leaders promised they would be able to do. Yet still nothing happens. Sweden is the only country in the EU to deport significant numbers of Brits after Brexit, and coverage of the cases around Europe is now damaging Sweden's reputation.
Again and again, Sweden passes migration laws in which bureaucratic logic takes precedence over justice for individuals and Sweden’s national interest. Again and again, everyone agrees that the victims of the latest immigration blunder should have been allowed to stay — and could have stayed if they’d just understood the bureaucracy better. Yet again and again bureaucratic logic is allowed to win. Who knows, maybe the next accidental deportations scandal is already lurking in a forgotten, lazily-drafted paragraph of one of the many immigration laws passed this parliament.
Sweden prides itself on agencies that act independently and follow the law. Ministers can’t and won’t get involved in individual cases or in steering how agencies interpret the law. This is sensible in many ways, but it means that we need well-drafted laws that take into account edge cases and avoid unjust outcomes. That’s not what we’ve been getting.

items.title: Midterms: What Americans in Europe need to know about changes to mail-in voting
items.summary: As Donald Trump's administration seeks to limit mail-in voting, overseas Americans have been left wondering what to expect for the upcoming midterm elections.
items.body_text:
The US midterm elections are approaching, with the first mail ballots due to be sent out in the coming weeks.
But many Americans in Europe are unsure of what to expect, as a result of President Donald Trump's executive order limiting mail-in voting.
Concerns for overseas Americans
The March 2026 executive order, "Ensuring citizenship verification and integrity in federal elections", says that each state must create a list of US citizens over 18 at least 60 days before the upcoming federal election.
It also prohibits USPS from transmitting mail-in ballots from individuals not listed and requires the use of "unique ballot identifiers" on envelopes.
In addition to criticism regarding the constitutionality of the executive order, voting rights groups worry overseas voters would be at risk of being wrongfully excluded from voter lists, despite the fact that their right to vote is protected by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act.
The non-partisan U.S. Vote Foundation wrote in a press release that "[The executive order] threatens U.S. citizens living overseas and uniformed service members, whose already time-sensitive voting process depends on efficient mail systems.
"These new requirements risk making it impossible for many of these voters to successfully cast a ballot."
What does this mean for the midterm elections?
Several democratic states and voter rights groups have challenged the executive order, but earlier this week the US Supreme Court paved the way for its implementation.
The Supreme Court on Monday ruled that it was too early for courts to assess the legality of the executive order.
The legal battle will undoubtedly continue to make its way in the lower courts, eventually landing back in front of the Supreme Court, particularly now that USPS has published its plans to comply with the executive order.
In terms of the upcoming midterm elections, USPS has said it will not deliver mail-in ballots without state citizen lists and specially formatted envelopes, according to reporting by the Associated Press.
Where does this leave Americans in Europe?
As the lawsuits are still ongoing, it is too early to say whether the executive order will be implemented.
In the meantime, Americans in Europe can take a few steps. You can start by going to the Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) website to find out your state's guidelines, as well as the election deadlines.
Voter activist groups, like Vote from Abroad, advise requesting your ballot by email instead of by mail. They also recommend using a backup ballot - you can read about how to request one here.
If you have any questions, you can still contact the Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) via email at Vote@FVAP.gov or by telephone at 0800-917-304 (toll-free from France).

items.title: Germany expected to miss its climate goal in 2026
items.summary: Germany risks missing an annual climate target in 2026 for the first time unless cuts to greenhouse gas emissions sharply accelerate, a think tank warned Friday.
items.body_text:
The warning from Agora Energiewende will add to criticism that Europe's biggest economy is backsliding on fighting the climate crisis under conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government.
Carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in Europe's biggest economy fell around two percent in the first half of the year, driven largely by weaker oil demand amid the Middle East war energy shock, the think tank said.
But if reductions continue at the same pace, emissions in 2026 would fall only to 635 million tonnes -- 13 million below 2025 levels but 10 million above a cap set out in Germany's climate protection act, Agora said.
While there may be no immediate consequences for missing this year's target, it signals that the country is on course to miss a legally binding 2030 target of cutting emissions 65 percent by 2030.
"To be able to meet the 2030 climate target, annual savings of around 40 million tonnes of CO2 are required," the think tank said.
Germany has a legally binding goal of achieving greenhouse gas neutrality by 2045.
The slowing pace of reductions has sparked worries that Merz's government is more focused on helping big business and boosting the stagnant economy than tackling climate change.
Criticism intensified after Germany, like elsewhere in Europe, faced a summer of droughts and heatwaves.
Merz sought to assuage his critics this week, insisting that "long-term lessons" would be drawn from the difficult summer.
The council of experts on climate change, an independent body appointed by the government, also warned in May that Germany was not on track to hit its 2030 climate goal.

items.title: A snack lover’s guide to German crisps
items.summary: Why is everything paprika flavoured? From the history behind Germany's favourite flavour to the tastes newcomers yearn for, and the top ones to try – here’s the scoop on German chips.
items.body_text:
Moving to Germany means adjusting to many unfamiliar things. The language, the recycling system and the supermarket opening hours are all predictable culture shocks.
Less expected is the moment many newcomers experience standing in front of a shelf of Chips and wondering where all the flavours have gone.
In Germany, crisps are called the standard American term, Chips, or also, Kartoffelchips (potato chips). British chips are Pommes or Pommes frites. (And just for the record Americans use 'chips' for what Britons call 'crisps', and 'fries' for what Brits call 'chips'. All clear?)
But figuring out the terminology is just the beginning.
Ask international residents about German crisp culture and one theme emerges almost immediately: paprika. Lots and lots of paprika.
For anyone still trying to make sense of Germany's crisp shelves, here's a guide to the country's paprika obsession – and some of the best crisps currently available here.
The paprika monopoly
Regardless of whether someone comes from Britain, Sweden, the United States, India or Australia, one observation about German crisps tends to come up repeatedly.
A supermarket shelf appears to offer variety, only for closer inspection to reveal paprika, sweet paprika, or Hungarian-style (Ungarish) paprika.
Germany's love affair with paprika-flavoured crisps dates back to the late 1950s. At a Frankfurt food fair in 1959, one of the country's earliest crisp manufacturers found that shoppers showed enormous enthusiasm for paprika-flavoured crisps while largely ignoring salted ones.
READ ALSO: Which drinks will Germany's coming 'sugar tax' really apply to?
The flavour also likely benefited from post-war migration from central and eastern Europe, where paprika was already a kitchen staple. As large numbers of people moved westwards or returned to Germany over the following decades, it became increasingly familiar on German dinner tables and supermarket shelves.
Over time, it became embedded in German snack culture in much the same way that cheese and onion became a staple in Britain.
Where foreigners disagree
Anecdotally, once the paprika observations are out of the way, international residents tend to divide into separate camps when it comes to the flavours they miss.
Britons and Irish residents often miss strong salt and vinegar, smoky bacon, roast chicken, prawn cocktail and cheese and onion.
Scandinavians long for dill, sour cream and onion or the rich savoury flavours common in Swedish snack aisles.
North Americans frequently wonder why barbecue flavours seem relatively restrained and why spicy options are often milder than advertised.
Residents from Asia find German crisps too conservative, missing bold sweet, sour, spicy and umami combinations.
READ ALSO: Germany's top regional food products and how to spot them in the supermarket
In an age when the same soft drinks, chocolate bars and fast-food staples are sold across much of the world, crisp flavours appear to offer a rare example of globalisation failing to create consensus.
But while people from different countries often have sharply differing opinions about what's wrong with German crisps, it’s Brits in particular who seem to be most vocal on the subject.
Part of the reason could be that crisps occupy a special place in everyday life in the UK. There, they’re not simply an occasional evening snack – as is often the case in southern Europe – but a daily lunch companion, a lunchbox staple and a standard pub snack.
Germany's selection of crisps is improving
The good news is that Germany's snack landscape is already far more varied than it used to be.
International travel, immigration and changing consumer tastes have gradually expanded the range of flavours available.
Salt and vinegar is easier to find than it once was. Chilli and lime flavours have appeared in major supermarket chains. Imported snacks are increasingly common, while Asian, Polish and international food shops offer options that would have been difficult to fi

items.title: Midterms: What Americans in Europe need to know about changes to mail-in voting
items.summary: As Donald Trump's administration seeks to limit mail-in voting, overseas Americans have been left wondering what to expect for the upcoming midterm elections.
items.body_text:
The US midterm elections are approaching, with the first mail ballots due to be sent out in the coming weeks.
But many Americans in Europe are unsure of what to expect, as a result of President Donald Trump's executive order limiting mail-in voting.
Concerns for overseas Americans
The March 2026 executive order, "Ensuring citizenship verification and integrity in federal elections", says that each state must create a list of US citizens over 18 at least 60 days before the upcoming federal election.
It also prohibits USPS from transmitting mail-in ballots from individuals not listed and requires the use of "unique ballot identifiers" on envelopes.
In addition to criticism regarding the constitutionality of the executive order, voting rights groups worry overseas voters would be at risk of being wrongfully excluded from voter lists, despite the fact that their right to vote is protected by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act.
The non-partisan U.S. Vote Foundation wrote in a press release that "[The executive order] threatens U.S. citizens living overseas and uniformed service members, whose already time-sensitive voting process depends on efficient mail systems.
"These new requirements risk making it impossible for many of these voters to successfully cast a ballot."
What does this mean for the midterm elections?
Several democratic states and voter rights groups have challenged the executive order, but earlier this week the US Supreme Court paved the way for its implementation.
The Supreme Court on Monday ruled that it was too early for courts to assess the legality of the executive order.
The legal battle will undoubtedly continue to make its way in the lower courts, eventually landing back in front of the Supreme Court, particularly now that USPS has published its plans to comply with the executive order.
In terms of the upcoming midterm elections, USPS has said it will not deliver mail-in ballots without state citizen lists and specially formatted envelopes, according to reporting by the Associated Press.
Where does this leave Americans in Europe?
As the lawsuits are still ongoing, it is too early to say whether the executive order will be implemented.
In the meantime, Americans in Europe can take a few steps. You can start by going to the Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) website to find out your state's guidelines, as well as the election deadlines.
Voter activist groups, like Vote from Abroad, advise requesting your ballot by email instead of by mail. They also recommend using a backup ballot - you can read about how to request one here.
If you have any questions, you can still contact the Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) via email at Vote@FVAP.gov or by telephone at 0800-917-304 (toll-free from France).

items.title: APEC projects regional economy to grow by 3.2 percent in 2026
items.summary: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) projects the average economic growth of its member economies to reach 3.2 ...
items.body_text:
According to a report released in Dalian, China, on Friday, APEC analysts stated that this growth is underpinned by robust trade in technology products and digital services, alongside steady investment flows into these sectors.
"Trade remains one of the brighter spots in the region. The expansion recorded in 2025 continued into early 2026, driven mainly by technology products," the report noted.
Export values surged by 18.8 percent year-on-year, with a 10.8 percent increase in volume. Meanwhile, import values grew by 10.2 percent, accompanied by an 11.1 percent rise in volume.
The digital services sector also continues to significantly contribute to the region's economic expansion. Throughout 2025, the export and import values of digital services surpassed US$1.8 trillion and US$1.5 trillion, respectively, jumping 70 to 75 percent from pre-pandemic levels.
This growth is further supported by stable foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows, with greenfield investments primarily focusing on digital services, electronics, and energy.
These three sectors accounted for 57.6 percent of total global greenfield investments in 2025, a surge of nearly 10 percentage points compared to five years ago.
This trend reflects a structural shift among APEC member economies toward a more digitalized economy with a stronger focus on energy resilience.
Nevertheless, relatively high inflation remains a looming threat. Average inflation in the region is projected to rise from 2.4 percent in 2025 to 2.9 percent in 2026.
The report attributed the inflationary rise partly to ongoing geopolitical tensions, which have elevated energy prices and logistics insurance costs, ultimately driving up global shipping rates.
Additionally, extreme weather and the El Niño phenomenon have hampered agricultural production, prompting a spike in food prices.
Analysts warn that rising logistics costs and food prices could erode public purchasing power, elevate business operational costs, and create a more volatile investment climate.
To address these economic risks, APEC outlined four policy recommendations: accelerating digital transformation, strengthening supply chains, enhancing climate adaptation and food security, and mobilizing productive investments.
"Achieving this will require stronger regional cooperation, continued investment in infrastructure and (human resources) skills, and policies that support broad-based growth and strengthen the region’s capacity to navigate future shocks," the report concluded.

items.title: OJK targets 98 pct financial inclusion by 2045
items.summary: The Financial Services Authority (OJK) aims to raise Indonesia's financial inclusion rate to 98 percent by 2045, in ...
items.body_text:
"God willing, we hope to achieve 98 percent financial inclusion in Indonesia by 2045," Chair of the OJK Board of Commissioners, Friderica Widyasari Dewi, said at the Indonesia Savings Day event in Bekasi, West Java, on Friday.
According to Friderica, students and young people in higher education still lag behind the national average in financial literacy and inclusion.
This gap makes students a primary target for OJK’s efforts to improve financial literacy and inclusion.
"It is our collective responsibility, alongside regional leaders, to improve students' financial literacy and inclusion across Indonesia," she stated.
The 2026 National Financial Literacy and Inclusion Survey (SNLIK) shows that the financial literacy rate among students stood at 62.72 percent, below the national average of 69.57 percent.
Meanwhile, their financial inclusion rate reached 92.76 percent, which is below the national average of 93.61 percent.
Friderica highlighted the urgency of improving these indicators among youth given the sheer size of the youth demographic.
Data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS) in 2025 shows there are approximately 88 million school- and college-aged individuals, accounting for roughly 31 percent of Indonesia’s total population of 287.2 million.
She noted that broad access to financial products and services must be accompanied by the ability to understand and use them wisely.
Furthermore, Friderica acknowledged that financial literacy challenges for the younger generation are mounting alongside seamless access to online shopping and digital financial services, which can encourage impulsive spending.
Therefore, she urged financial service providers to strengthen efforts to educate and protect consumers, including ensuring that prospective users have an income and fully understand the obligations associated with using financial products.
Additionally, she encouraged young people to build a saving habit early on, emphasizing that teaching early financial discipline is key to helping them manage their money wisely.

items.body_text:
"We have distributed a total of 5.3 million masks to the wildfire-affected areas. Provincial stocks remain sufficient, with 2.7 million masks still available," Deputy Health Minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono said in Jakarta on Friday.
He expressed hope that ongoing firefighting efforts will reduce pollution and lessen the demand for masks, which remain one of the best protections in addition to avoiding outdoor activities in areas with poor air quality.
Additionally, the ministry continues to identify needs across affected provinces, districts, and cities to ensure adequate mask supplies, while actively educating the public.
To address urgent medical needs, the Ministry of Health is also supplying oxygen concentrators to hard-hit areas to ensure a steady supply of oxygen.
Key strategies deployed by the ministry include intensifying health promotion and public outreach; monitoring cases of acute respiratory infections (ARI), pneumonia, asthma, as well as eye and skin irritation; tracking air quality; and issuing advisories.
Furthermore, the ministry has alerted the Public Safety Center, set up emergency health posts, prepared referral hospitals, and mobilized logistical aid.
According to data from the ministry's Public Health Emergency Operations Center, as of August 27, 4,082 respiratory infection cases were reported in areas affected by forest and land fires, bringing the cumulative total in these regions to 13,449 cases.
A prolonged dry season has triggered an increase in wildfires, particularly in South Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan, West Kalimantan, East Kalimantan, Jambi, Riau, and South Sumatra.
As of August 27, 2026, Air Pollutant Index data for the affected provinces showed that Pontianak, West Kalimantan, recorded a score of 328, placing it in the hazardous category.

items.title: Di Hadapan Megawati, Presiden Timor Leste Ramos-Horta Puji Toleransi di Indonesia
items.summary: Ramos-Horta turut memuji ketangguhan (resilience) dan kehangatan karakter rakyat Indonesia dalam menghadapi berbagai ujian bencana alam
items.body_text:
Di Hadapan Megawati, Presiden Timor Leste Ramos-Horta Puji Toleransi di Indonesia
Ramos-Horta turut memuji ketangguhan (resilience) dan kehangatan karakter rakyat Indonesia dalam menghadapi berbagai ujian bencana alam
Ringkasan Berita:
- Jose Ramos-Horta menyampaikan kekagumannya terhadap tingginya nilai toleransi dan kerukunan umat beragama di Indonesia
- Peraih Nobel Perdamaian ini membeberkan fakta menarik yang kerap luput dari pandangan dunia Barat
- Ramos-Horta turut memuji ketangguhan (resilience) dan kehangatan karakter rakyat Indonesia dalam menghadapi berbagai ujian bencana alam
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA - Presiden Timor-Leste Jose Ramos-Horta menyampaikan kekagumannya terhadap tingginya nilai toleransi dan kerukunan umat beragama di Indonesia yang dinilainya patut menjadi teladan bagi masyarakat internasional.
Peraih Nobel Perdamaian ini membeberkan fakta menarik yang kerap luput dari pandangan dunia Barat, yakni besarnya populasi umat Kristiani dan Katolik di Indonesia yang hidup berdampingan secara damai di tengah negara berpenduduk mayoritas Muslim terbesar di dunia.
Baca juga: Momen Hangat Megawati Terima Kunjungan Presiden Timor Leste Ramos Horta, Saling Genggam Tangan
Pernyataan tersebut disampaikan Ramos-Horta saat menghadiri pertemuan bersama Presiden Kelima RI Megawati Soekarnoputri dan deretan peraih Nobel, serta para ilmuwan dunia di Megawati Institute, Menteng, Jakarta, Jumat (28/8/2026).
"Indonesia adalah negara dengan mayoritas Muslim terbesar di dunia, tetapi juga memiliki lebih banyak umat Katolik daripada banyak negara di Eropa," kata Ramos-Horta.
Ramos-Horta merinci, populasi umat Katolik dan Kristen Protestan di Indonesia diperkirakan mencapai 30 hingga 40 juta jiwa, dengan jumlah umat Katolik sendiri mencapai kisaran 10 hingga 14 juta jiwa.
Jumlah ini, menurutnya, jauh melampaui populasi umat Katolik di sejumlah negara Eropa.
"Berapa banyak negara di Eropa yang memiliki 10 juta atau 14 juta umat Katolik? Inilah yang sebagian besar orang di dunia tidak ketahui. Mereka hanya tahu Indonesia adalah mayoritas Muslim terbesar di dunia," papar Ramos-Horta.
Namun, yang paling membuat Ramos-Horta terkesan bukanlah sekadar angka statistik, melainkan bagaimana kemajemukan tersebut dirawat dengan penuh keharmonisan, rasa saling menghormati, dan keterbukaan antarumat beragama.
"Saya katakan, ya, mereka mayoritas Muslim, tetapi mereka juga punya lebih banyak umat Katolik daripada beberapa negara Eropa, yang hidup dengan cara yang paling damai, saling bertoleransi, dan saling menerima," tegasnya.
Selain menyoroti harmoni keberagaman, Ramos-Horta turut memuji ketangguhan (resilience) dan kehangatan karakter rakyat Indonesia dalam menghadapi berbagai ujian bencana alam.
Ia menyebutkan, dengan populasi lebih dari 300 juta jiwa yang tersebar di 17.000 pulau, Indonesia kerap diuji oleh bencana geologis seperti gempa bumi dan banjir besar.
Baca juga: Megawati Kritik Keberadaan PBB yang Tak Mampu Hentikan Perang, Usulkan Rombak Dewan Keamanan
Namun, bangsa Indonesia selalu memiliki daya lenting luar biasa untuk bangkit kembali.
"Alam tidak begitu bersahabat dengan Indonesia karena terus-menerus mengalami gempa bumi dan banjir yang besar. Namun demikian, setiap kali terjadi, rakyat Indonesia selalu bangkit kembali. Dan setiap kali bangkit, mereka menjadi lebih baik," ungkapnya.
Di mata Ramos-Horta, terlepas dari segala dinamika geografis dan tantangan sosial yang dihadapi, masyarakat Indonesia tetap memancarkan keramahan yang tulus kepada siapa pun.
"Terlepas dari semua tantangan tersebut, rakyat Indonesia selalu tetap menjadi orang-orang yang paling ramah dan paling hangat di dunia," tandas Ramos-Horta.
items.normalised_title: di hadapan megawati presiden timor leste ramos horta puji toleransi di indonesia

- Eksistensi PDIP tidak lepas dari sejarah perlawanan terhadap praktik Korupsi, Kolusi, dan Nepotisme (KKN).
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA - Sekretaris Jenderal (Sekjen) PDI Perjuangan (PDIP), Hasto Kristiyanto, memastikan bahwa partainya mendukung penuh pengesahan Rancangan Undang-Undang (RUU) Perampasan Aset. 
Hasto menyebut, DPP PDIP telah menugaskan Fraksi PDIP di DPR RI untuk proaktif mengawal dan memberikan penjelasan kepada publik terkait rancangan beleid tersebut.
Baca juga: Target RUU Perampasan Aset Disahkan 15 Desember 2026, Mahfud MD: Permainan di DPR kan Kadang Aneh
"Jadi komitmen PDI Perjuangan tidak diragukan lagi, termasuk di dalam sikap proaktif kami untuk menyelesaikan RUU Perampasan Aset," kata Hasto saat ditemui di Megawati Institute, Menteng, Jakarta, Jumat (28/8/2026).
Hasto meminta publik tidak meragukan komitmen antikorupsi partai berlambang banteng moncong putih tersebut.
Ia mengingatkan bahwa eksistensi PDIP tidak lepas dari sejarah perlawanan terhadap praktik Korupsi, Kolusi, dan Nepotisme (KKN).
"Bahkan eksistensi dari PDI Perjuangan salah satunya karena perjuangan untuk melawan berbagai bentuk KKN yang terjadi selama 32 tahun pemerintahan Soeharto," ujarnya.
Ia juga menambahkan bahwa bukti nyata komitmen PDIP terhadap pemberantasan korupsi adalah berdirinya Komisi Pemberantasan Korupsi (KPK) pada masa pemerintahan Presiden ke-5 RI yang juga Ketua Umum PDIP, Megawati Soekarnoputri.
Lebih lanjut, Hasto menekankan bahwa pemberantasan korupsi tidak bisa hanya mengandalkan keberadaan undang-undang semata. Menurut dia, dibutuhkan kesatuan komitmen dari berbagai elemen negara.
Baca juga: Surat Komitmen RUU Perampasan Aset Tanpa Teken Ketua DPR RI Puan Maharani, Ini Kata Mahfud MD
Aspek kepemimpinan nasional (national leader) yang tegas serta supremasi hukum di kalangan aparat penegak hukum menjadi kunci utama agar beleid seperti RUU Perampasan Aset bisa berjalan efektif.
"Undang-undang harus dilihat spirit-nya, tetapi juga komitmennya dari seluruh para penyelenggara negara," ungkap Hasto.
Sebagai informasi, DPR RI telah menyepakati dan berkomitmen untuk merampungkan pembahasan RUU Perampasan Aset.
DPR menargetkan rancangan undang-undang yang telah lama ditunggu publik tersebut dapat disahkan paling lambat pada 15 Desember 2026 mendatang.

items.body_text:
Demo di Jakarta
TAUD Beberkan 6 Temuan Represif Aparat saat Demo 27 Agustus: Ada Penangkapan Sewenang-wenang
TAUD melontarkan kritik pedas terhadap penggunaan istilah “preventive strike” oleh Polda Metro Jaya dalam merespons aksi demonstrasi 27 Agustus 2026
Ringkasan Berita:
- TAUD mengungkap sejumlah dugaan tindakan represif dan pelanggaran prosedur yang dilakukan aparat kepolisian dalam pengamanan demonstrasi pada Kamis, 27 Agustus 2026
- TAUD mengecam keras tindakan tersebut karena dinilai melanggar hukum acara pidana dan hak konstitusional warga negara.
- TAUD melontarkan kritik pedas terhadap penggunaan istilah “preventive strike” oleh Polda Metro Jaya dalam merespons aksi demonstrasi 27 Agustus 2026.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA – Tim Advokasi untuk Demokrasi (TAUD) mengungkap sejumlah dugaan tindakan represif dan pelanggaran prosedur yang dilakukan aparat kepolisian dalam pengamanan demonstrasi pada Kamis, 27 Agustus 2026.
Peringatan satu tahun Aksi Agustus 2025 tersebut diwarnai oleh aksi penangkapan sewenang-wenang terhadap massa aksi maupun masyarakat sipil.
Baca juga: Ayahnya Meninggal dalam Kericuhan Demo 27 Agustus, Yoga Kenang Nasihat yang Selalu Diingat
TAUD mengecam keras tindakan tersebut karena dinilai melanggar hukum acara pidana dan hak konstitusional warga negara.
“Upaya paksa sewenang-wenang dengan dalih ‘mengamankan’ oleh Polda Metro Jaya melanggar hukum acara pidana. Hal ini terbukti melalui penangkapan, penyitaan hingga penggeledahan oleh Kepolisian tanpa dasar,” tulis TAUD dalam siaran persnya, Jumat (28/8/2026).
Baca juga: Polisi Amankan 5 Anak Pembawa Buah Bintaro Dicampur Bensin Saat Kerusuhan Usai Demo di DPR
Berdasarkan pemantauan di lapangan dan aduan di hotline, TAUD menghimpun enam temuan utama terkait praktik represif aparat:
1. Penargetan Admin Media Sosial: Aparat Kepolisian diduga melakukan pemantauan dan penargetan terhadap admin media sosial, individu kritis, hingga pihak yang terlibat dalam acara amal untuk korban gempa NTT.
2. Penangkapan Tanpa Prosedur: Sejumlah individu diduga ditangkap tanpa prosedur, dasar hukum, dan bukti yang memadai.
3. Penyisiran di Stasiun: Warga diduga dicegat di beberapa titik stasiun dan digeledah tanpa dasar hukum jelas, lalu beberapa di antaranya dibawa ke Polda Metro Jaya.
4. Pemeriksaan di Jam Tidak Wajar: Terdapat pemeriksaan saksi yang dilakukan pada dini hari tanpa didampingi advokat atau bantuan hukum.
5. Aparat Tanpa Seragam: Ditemukan sejumlah aparat yang dikerahkan di sekitar titik aksi tanpa menggunakan seragam maupun atribut resmi Kepolisian.
6. Penahanan Melebihi 24 Jam: Hingga siaran pers diterbitkan, sejumlah korban penangkapan belum dilepaskan, bahkan beberapa di antaranya telah ditahan lebih dari 24 jam.
TAUD menilai, status “pengamanan” atau pemeriksaan sebagai “saksi” yang digunakan polisi seringkali hanya dalih untuk melakukan perampasan kemerdekaan.
“Status Saksi tidak menghapus kewajiban aparat untuk menempuh prosedur yang sah,” tegas TAUD.
Pihaknya menemukan banyak warga yang ditangkap dengan status saksi, namun tidak dipanggil secara patut dan diperlakukan tidak sesuai dengan asas praduga tidak bersalah.
Selain itu, organisasi yang terdiri antara lain dari YLBHI, KontraS, serta Amnesty International ini menyoroti adanya pemeriksaan terhadap warga di ruang publik atau sweeping hanya berdasarkan atribut atau dugaan akan mengikuti aksi.

Alex Eala, Iva Jovic share court with dads in US Open exhibition
MANILA, Philippines —Alex Eala fell to close friend Iva Jovic, 6-3, in the Stars of the Open exhibition on Friday morning, but both enjoyed a lighthearted tuneup ahead of the US Open.
Towards the end of the match, the two rising stars brought their fathers onto the court for a brief mixed doubles match, ending the exhibition with a heartwarming moment and a hug with their dads.
A father-daughter moment to remember 💙
Alexandra Eala and Iva Jovic bring their dads on court for a little friendly competition. pic.twitter.com/JGfvPZM9rv
— US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 28, 2026
Eala and Jovic also exchanged messages in their native languages, addressing the crowd at a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium in Flushing Meadows.
Eala fought back from a 0-2 deficit to tie the one-set match at 3-all, but Jovic won the final three games to finish the exhibition in less than an hour.
Jovic has now beaten Eala three times this year, including at the French Open and HSBC Championships.
Proceeds from Stars of the Open will go to the USTA Foundation.
Eala, seeded 17th in the US Open, will face a qualifier in the first round. Should she advance, she will meet the winner between Oleksandra Oliynykova and wild card Reese Brantmeier.
Eala could face No. 14 seed Jovic in the third round. The American opens against Magdalena Fręch, with the winner facing Magda Linette or another qualifier in the second round.

items.body_text:
Nepal floods: Survivors, swallowed by silt, recount horror
BIDUR, Nepal —Survivors from Nepal’s flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others gently supported by the shoulders, were airlifted to safety on Thursday as the constant roar of helicopters echoed across the devastated town of Bidur.
A few walked alone, their faces frozen in shock, as helicopters landed every few minutes on a football field inside the town’s military cantonment, whipping up clouds of dust.
Among the survivors was customs agent Omkar Joshi, who spent the previous night stranded on a hilltop in the border town of Timure before being rescued.
READ: Nepal-Tibet floods: Death toll nears 400, rescuers search for 1,400 missing
“Everything is finished,” Joshi, 35, told AFP, his voice breaking with emotion.
The town he fled had all but vanished beneath a torrent of water, mud and debris.
“Ninety percent” of its people were dead, he said, swallowed by silt.
“It is a giant graveyard. All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood.”
He said hundreds of people survived only by scrambling up nearby slopes as floodwaters roared through the valley below.
READ: Breakdown of nationalities missing after Nepal-Tibet flash floods
“It rained all night, but we stayed put till the choppers came for us,” he added.
On Wednesday, a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through villages and towns along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Nepali police have recovered 270 bodies, but search operations continue.
Many of the missing are foreign tourists caught in the disaster, which according to the US Geological Survey was caused by a glacial collapse that resulted in an overwhelming flow of icy debris.
Buried alive
In Bidur, scores of anxious relatives peered through the barbed wire separating the football ground from the road, hoping to see the familiar face of a loved one.
Sita BK was searching for her younger brother Ramchandra, a schoolteacher in Timure.
“I spoke to him in the morning just before I heard the news,” said the 37-year-old. “But ever since, his phone is switched off.”
She said she had no choice but to wait.
READ: 1 Filipino missing due to massive Nepal flash flood – tourism board
“They (officials) said their first priority is to rescue people who are contactable,” she said. “But my brother is not.”
Nearby, Anisha Nepali sat quietly in a corner, tears running down her cheeks.
The 24-year-old had rushed back from Kathmandu on Wednesday after hearing about the disaster, but has received no news of her missing mother and younger brother.
“I have given their names, but am yet to hear anything,” she said.
Two young girls climbed out of a helicopter, still in their bright green school uniforms. A rescuer gently caressed their heads and offered them biscuits and water, before leading them away to safety.
Farther downstream, the devastation was etched into the shattered landscape of Devighat.
Residents said only one of roughly 150 houses along the banks of the Trishuli River remained intact: a four-storey old-age care home.
But rescuers said up to seven elderly residents were buried when a landslide crashed into the home as they tried to flee.
Images shared by a rescuer showed one of the victims trapped beneath an uprooted tree.
Sabir Miyan, a resident of the town, said warnings that floodwaters were racing down from the mountains had helped save lives.
“Many of us could save our lives but everything else is gone,” he said. “It is all ruins now.”

items.title: Kai Sotto denies Jordan as Gilas Pilipinas gets World Cup bid back on track
items.summary: Kai Sotto caps a prolific performance with the win-sealing block as Gilas Pilipinas noses out Jordan in overtime to start the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- Gilas Pilipinas secured a narrow overtime victory against Jordan, 82-81, in the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers, marking a return to winning form with Kai Sotto back on the team.
- Sotto had a standout performance with 18 points, 14 rebounds, and 2 crucial blocks, helping the Philippines end a four-game losing streak and improve their record to 3-4 in Group E.
- Key contributions came from Kevin Quiambao and CJ Perez, who scored 14 points each, with Perez notably scoring 14 of his points in the fourth quarter and overtime.
MANILA, Philippines – It probably is not coincidence that Gilas Pilipinas rediscovered its winning ways just when Kai Sotto came back.
Sotto capped a prolific performance with the win-sealing block as the Philippines nosed out Jordan in overtime, 82-81, to start the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers at the Mall of Asia Arena on Friday, August 28.
Back in national team duty for the first time in two years, the 7-foot-3 Sotto produced a double-double of 18 points and 14 rebounds to go with 2 blocks, the last of which allowed the Nationals to snap a four-game skid and improve their record to 3-4 in Group E.
A five-second inbound violation by Scottie Thompson with less than 10 seconds left kept the comeback door ajar for Jordan, but Abdullah Olajuwon saw his potential game-winning shot layup swatted away by Sotto.
Heroes were aplenty for Gilas Pilipinas as Kevin Quiambao and CJ Perez hit big baskets down the stretch, rising to the occasion in the absence of injured naturalized star Justin Brownlee.
Perez scattered 14 of his 16 points in the fourth and overtime periods and also tallied 4 rebounds and 2 steals, while Quiambao finished with 14 points, including a gutsy three-pointer that gave the Filipinos an 82-79 lead with 13 seconds remaining.
Dwight Ramos also supplied 14 points, 5 rebounds, and 3 assists in the win, which saw the Philippines fight back from a 17-point deficit following a red-hot start by Jordan fueled by former NBA player Jalen Harris.
Harris went 3-of-3 from beyond the arc in the opening quarter as Jordan mounted a 28-14 lead before being neutralized the rest of the way.
The leading scorer of the Asian Qualifiers with an average of 27.0 points going into the game, Harris got limited to 19 points on 6-of-22 shooting.
Up next for the Philippines is Iran on Sunday, August 30, at the same venue.
The Scores
Philippines 82 – Sotto 18, Perez 16, Quiambao 14, Ramos 14, Edu 9, Tamayo 8, Fajardo 2, Thompson 1, Gomez de Liaño 0, Newsome 0, Baltazar 0.
Jordan 81 – Ibrahim 22, Harris 19, Olajuwon 17, Saleh 5, Al Dwairi 4, Alshami 4, Alhamarsheh 4, Abu Hawwas 3, Kilani 2, Salman 1, Shaher 0.
Quarters: 14-28, 39-44, 54-58, 72-72 (reg.), 82-81 (OT).
– Rappler.com

items.title: EJ Obiena earns 2027 World Athletics Championships berth
items.summary: EJ Obiena gains direct entry to the 2027 World Athletics Championships by clearing exactly the entry standard of 5.90 meters at Weltklasse Zurich in Switzerland
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – EJ Obiena punched his ticket to the 2027 World Athletics Championships following his fifth-place finish at Weltklasse Zurich in Switzerland on Thursday, August 27 (Friday, August 28, Manila time).
Obiena gained direct entry to the global showdown by clearing exactly the entry standard of 5.90 meters in the meet once again ruled by world record holder Armand Duplantis of Sweden.
Duplantis posted a new meet record of 6.25m to claim the gold medal as he edged Greece’s Emmanouil Karalis for the gold medal in a thrilling mano a mano between the two highest-ranked pole vaulters in the world.
Karalis recorded a new career best of 6.20m but still settled for silver, while Norway’s Sondre Guttormsen bagged bronze with 6.00m.
USA’s Chris Nilsen edged Obiena for fourth place via countback, with the Filipino needing three attempts to surpass 5.80m.
After hurdling 5.90m in one try, Obiena sought to clear the six-meter bar for the first time since he won a historic silver in the 2023 World Athletics Championships but to no avail.
Despite finishing out of the podium for the third straight meet, Obiena has shown consistency by vaulting at least 5.80m in each of them.
He landed sixth in the Athletissima in Laussane, Switzerland, with 5.81m, then seventh in the Kamila Skolimowska Memorial in Chorzow, Poland, with 5.80m. – Rappler.com

items.title: Poa, AFP witnesses to testify on DepEd funds misuse
items.summary: Three officials of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and defense lawyer Michael Poa are expected to testify on the alleged misuse of the Department of Education (DepEd)’s confidential funds next week.
items.body_text:
Poa, AFP witnesses to testify on DepEd funds misuse
MANILA, Philippines — Three officials of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and defense lawyer Michael Poa are expected to testify on the alleged misuse of the Department of Education (DepEd)’s confidential funds next week.
The prosecution panel said one of the witnesses, Col. Manaros Boransing II, will testify how an annual military event received no reward money or financial assistance from DepEd, even though the agency used the military activities in explaining its use of confidential funds.
Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, a spokesman for the panel, also said the prosecution intends to revisit certifications involving the AFP and the Youth Leadership Summit, after DepEd used the activities in explaining confidential fund expenditures questioned by state auditors.
During the House inquiry in 2024, military officers whose certifications were later used in DepEd’s response to Commission on Audit findings testified that the Youth Leadership Summits were funded by the military and participating local governments and that their units received no DepEd confidential funds for those activities.
Adiong said Boransing’s testimony will be weighed together with the audit records and other evidence for the appreciation of the Senate impeachment court.
The testimony of Col. Magtangol Panopio will also focus on the issue, particularly on the AFP certification used by DepEd, even though the signatories previously said they did not know that purpose.
Prosecution adviser and spokesman Ace Barbers said the hearing should also protect the military’s institutional neutrality, as the officials’ testimonies will show whether military officers knowingly took part in the funding process or whether their signatures were used without a full explanation of the documents’ purpose.
He said the certifications matter because they may have been used to answer an audit question and support a public fund liquidation.
Meanwhile, Poa’s testimony could fill important gaps from his previous appearance before the House inquiry about the DepEd’s confidential funds, the prosecution said.
Poa served as DepEd chief of staff and spokesman while Vice President Sara Duterte was education secretary. He is now part of Duterte’s defense team and serves as defense spokesman.
The House prosecution plans to call him as a hostile witness in connection with the alleged misuse of P112.5 million in DepEd confidential funds.
Barbers said Poa’s former position placed him close to documents and official responses that the senator-judges need to understand.
